entries.name: African Harrier-Hawk

modes.label: Clambering • Probing • Methodical

waveform.description: A patient working rhythm: slow repeated probing rather than fast strikes.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, patient and defined by access rather than speed.

entries.name: African Palm Civet

modes.label: Arboreal • Nocturnal • Fruit-led

waveform.description: A quiet low rhythm with small variations: an unhurried circuit repeated each night.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: quiet, economical and built on repeating a known low-competition round.

entries.name: African Penguin

modes.label: Excavating a burrow in deep guano • Shading eggs and chicks from direct sun • Returning to the same burrow with the same partner each year

waveform.description: A regular alternation of similar magnitude, because the year is built from repeated foraging trips and nest reliefs.

entries.closingLine: Since foraging trips repeat, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: African Pygmy Hedgehog

modes.label: Nosing the litter • Rolling when touched • Anointing what is new

waveform.description: A low pottering rhythm interrupted twice by short flat troughs, because the animal's response to danger is to stop entirely rather than to accelerate.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs slowly and cheaply through the night, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: African Sharptooth Catfish

modes.label: A pair of branched tree-like structures above the gill chambers, densely supplied with blood and open to the air • Air gulped at the surface held against that huge folded surface for oxygen uptake • The fish surviving in water with almost no oxygen and crossing wet ground between pools when one dries

waveform.description: A steady repeating rhythm of surfacing, because the fish must return to the air at regular intervals.

entries.closingLine: Because surfacing is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Agrarian Sac Spider

modes.label: Building a closed silk sac in a rolled leaf, a corner or a fold of cloth • Spending the day sealed inside it • Hunting on foot at night with no web at all

waveform.description: Long sealed stretches alternating with an active period, because the animal is either shut inside the sac or out hunting.

entries.closingLine: Since hunting recurs nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Albino Iridescent Shark

modes.label: Moving with the shoal • Reading the rising water • Running upstream

waveform.description: A rolling mid-level line that drifts steadily upward across the frame, because the whole movement has a direction as well as a rhythm.

entries.closingLine: Because the movement is continuous, collective and sustained over weeks, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Alderfly

modes.label: An aquatic larva with lateral abdominal gills, hunting small invertebrates in the silt of slow water for one to two years
A terrestrial adult living a few days with non-functional mouthparts, flying weakly near the water and doing nothing but mating and laying

waveform.description: A long flat aquatic stretch breaking into a brief agitated burst, because the two stages are different animals in effect.

entries.closingLine: The division is architectural rather than behavioural, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Alpine Marmot

modes.label: Grazing alpine meadow through a short summer • Building fat and maintaining a shared burrow • Posting sentries and whistling at raptors
The whole group sealed in one chamber • Bodies packed together to share heat • Adults rousing in synchrony and warming the young

waveform.description: A brief active section against a very long depressed one, because more than half the year is spent in the second state.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two physiologies, making it a bimodal system.

entries.name: Alpine Musk Deer

modes.label: Browsing • Scent-marking • Keeping the same weapon

waveform.description: A flat, unvarying trace with no annual spike anywhere in it.

entries.closingLine: Solitary, secretive and slow, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Amano Shrimp

modes.label: Living and breeding as adults in fresh water • Releasing larvae that drift downstream into brackish water • Producing postlarvae that migrate back upstream months later

waveform.description: A long even line rising into one broad seasonal event, because the reproductive movement is the only large feature of the year.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Amazon Sailfin Catfish

modes.label: The whole body covered in overlapping bony plates rather than scales • Rigid spines in the pectoral and dorsal fins that lock outward when the fish is seized • Predators and birds unable to swallow or process it, so the fish survives attacks that would kill an unarmoured one

waveform.description: A very flat placid line, because the fish grazes slowly and relies on armour rather than on any response.

entries.closingLine: Because the defence is passive and continuous, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Amazonian Giant Centipede

modes.label: The animal climbing a cave wall and anchoring its rear legs to the ceiling • The body held hanging free in the air below, in the flight path bats use to leave the roost • Bats struck in flight and held by the forcipules, the whole capture happening with nothing beneath the centipede at all

waveform.description: A long motionless wait broken by sudden strikes, because the animal hangs still until something passes.

entries.closingLine: Because the hunt is occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Amber Snail

modes.label: Ingesting flatworm eggs from bird droppings on vegetation • The parasite growing broodsacs that push into the snail's eye stalks and pulsate there • The snail moving into open sunlight and exposed leaves instead of hiding, until a bird takes it

waveform.description: A slow rise and fall over the whole line, because the infection develops gradually and then takes the animal.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs across seasons, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Amboina Sailfin Lizard

modes.label: Basking on the branch • Carrying the sail • Dropping into the river

waveform.description: A moderate even rhythm of basking and moving, with nothing abrupt because the escape route is always a step away.

entries.closingLine: Because the basking, feeding and moving proceed at one steady daily tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: American Badger

modes.label: Digging the prey out • Sealing the exits first • Moving to the next colony

waveform.description: A heavy working rhythm of deep regular efforts, because the whole hunt is sustained digging rather than any moment of speed.

entries.closingLine: Since the digging runs at one sustained heavy tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: American Black Bear

modes.label: An active bear feeding heavily, excreting normally and laying down fat through the autumn
A denning bear neither eating, drinking, urinating nor defecating for months, with heart rate and metabolism sharply reduced but body temperature only slightly lowered

waveform.description: A vigorous active rhythm collapsing into a flat suppressed line, because the two states are physiologically different systems.

entries.closingLine: This is a different operating architecture rather than a slowed version of the same one, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: American Crocodile

modes.label: Floating • Salt-excreting • Waiting
Lunging • Explosive • Brief

waveform.description: A near-motionless line broken by one explosive event.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: prolonged stillness and a rare violent strike.

entries.name: American Crow

modes.label: Learning the face of a person who threatened it • Scolding that face on sight for years • Passing the association to birds that never saw the event

waveform.description: Ordinary activity broken by strong sustained reactions that decay slowly, because a recognition event produces a prolonged response rather than a reflex.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: American Giant Millipede

modes.label: Coiling tightly when disturbed • Releasing benzoquinones from pores along each body segment • Staining and repelling whatever is handling it, and remaining coiled until the threat leaves

waveform.description: A slow line interrupted by a discharge and then a long flat raised stretch, because the animal coils and stays coiled.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: American Kestrel

modes.label: Perching in the open on wires and posts with the back exposed • Carrying two black ocelli on the nape that read as a face • Hunting small prey from that perch and from a hover

waveform.description: A watchful baseline broken by regular decisive drops, because the bird perches and then strikes at intervals.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: American Lobster

modes.label: Moulting throughout life rather than reaching a final size • Continuing to grow, feed and reproduce at ages of many decades • Showing little of the decline in fertility or survival that age normally brings

waveform.description: A long slow line with widely spaced small steps, because growth happens only at moults and those become rarer with age.

entries.closingLine: Since moults are years apart, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: American Robin

modes.label: Head cocked sideways • Listening for movement below • Pulling

waveform.description: Flat runs broken by short identical strikes, because the bird alternates between holding still and pulling.

entries.closingLine: Because the hunting runs continuously through daylight, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: American Toad

modes.label: Gathering in huge numbers at temporary water • Calling and spawning within days • Producing tadpoles that develop fast enough to leave before it dries

waveform.description: A flat line interrupted by one narrow block of activity, because the entire reproductive year happens in a single short window.

entries.closingLine: Since the whole cycle runs once a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: American White Pelican

modes.label: Birds forming a line or arc on the water and swimming forward together • Beating wings and feet to drive fish ahead of them into shallows • Dipping in unison once the fish are concentrated against the shore or against each other

waveform.description: A steady coordinated rhythm, because the herding and dipping cycle repeats through the day as a group.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle repeats daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Anegada Rock Iguana

modes.label: Basking • Fermenting • Decadal

waveform.description: Two shallow warming humps tied to the sun's height, riding on a floor that never drops far — a day governed by temperature rather than by hunger.

entries.closingLine: Because a low-cost body converts poor food into size over very long periods, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Annam Pond Turtle

modes.label: A wild population reduced to almost nothing by collection for trade • Managed breeding groups held in Vietnam and abroad carrying nearly the whole gene pool • Offspring produced under management rather than in the marshes the species came from

waveform.description: A long decline levelling into a flat low line, because the wild collapse ended in a small managed population held steady.

entries.closingLine: Because the timescale is generational, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Apostlebird

modes.label: Living permanently in a group of about a dozen • Building one mud nest that all members attend • Foraging, roosting and moving as a single unit year round

waveform.description: A very even line with one broad gentle rise, because the group's life is continuous and the breeding season is a raised phase rather than an event.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle turns over annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Apple Snail

modes.label: Breathing through a gill while submerged • Grazing plant material underwater • Sealing the shell with an operculum when disturbed
Extending a long siphon to the surface or leaving the water entirely • Breathing air through a lung in the left mantle cavity • Sealing up and waiting out a dry season in mud

waveform.description: Ordinary variation alternating with long flat depressed stretches, because the animal genuinely alternates between two respiratory regimes.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two respiratory architectures, making it a bimodal system.

entries.name: Arctic Char

modes.label: Landlocked • Dwarfed • Resident
Sea-run • Large • Migratory

waveform.description: A low resident level and a raised migratory one in the same trace — the same fish running at a different setting.

entries.closingLine: Because the same system reconfigures itself to its context rather than running one way, it is an adaptive system.

entries.name: Artichoke Plume Moth

modes.label: Wings divided along their length into narrow feather-like lobes rather than forming continuous surfaces • Those lobes rolled tightly together at rest and held out at right angles to the body • The whole insect reduced to a thin T-shape that reads as a dry grass stem

waveform.description: A very flat quiet line, because the insect rests immobile and flies only weakly at dusk.

entries.closingLine: Because the posture is held through the day, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Arowana

modes.label: Taking the fertilised eggs into the mouth • Holding developing young there for weeks without feeding • Releasing free-swimming fry and taking them back in when threatened

waveform.description: A steady line that drops to a sustained lower level and returns, because the brooding period is a long enforced pause in normal life.

entries.closingLine: Since breeding runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian common toad

modes.label: Sitting under a streetlight • Swelling and tilting • Secreting from behind the eyes

waveform.description: A slow low line with two small lifts, because a toad that cannot run has almost nothing that registers as activity.

entries.closingLine: Since everything else runs slowly through the night, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Fairy-bluebird

modes.label: Feather barbs containing a spongy keratin structure with air spaces of a consistent size but no regular arrangement • Light scattered by that structure reinforcing one wavelength regardless of the direction it is viewed from • A deep even blue that does not shift or flash with angle, unlike the iridescence of a starling or a sunbird

waveform.description: A very even rhythm with little variation, because the property does not change with circumstance.

entries.closingLine: Because the property is constant, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Forest Tortoise

modes.label: Raking leaf litter backwards with the forelimbs into a large mound • Laying the eggs inside the pile where decomposition generates heat • Remaining on the mound for days or weeks driving off anything that approaches

waveform.description: A flat line with one raised episode, because nest building and guarding is a single concentrated event in an otherwise slow year.

entries.closingLine: Because the sequence runs once a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Glossy Starling

modes.label: Taking small fruit whole in large flocks • Passing seeds through the gut intact within minutes • Voiding them under a roost or a perch elsewhere

waveform.description: A busy repeated pattern of similar events, because the flock feeds and moves in continuous bouts through the day.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding bouts repeat, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian honey bee

modes.label: Detecting a scouting hornet at the nest entrance • Engulfing it in a ball of hundreds of workers • Vibrating flight muscles until the centre reaches a temperature the hornet cannot survive and the bees can

waveform.description: A calm line rising into a sustained intense event and returning, because the response builds, holds for minutes and then ends.

entries.closingLine: Since the response is measured in minutes, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Leaf Turtle

modes.label: A juvenile with a rigid plastron joined solidly to the shell and a serrated rear margin • Relying on running, hiding in leaf litter and dropping into water when threatened • Defence through movement because the shell cannot be shut

An adult in which the plastral sutures have loosened into a flexible ligament • Drawing the front lobe up against the carapace to close the shell on the head and forelimbs • Defence through sealing rather than fleeing

waveform.description: An active early phase settling into a slower later one, because the animal changes from a runner into a closer as it matures.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal operates one defensive architecture as a juvenile and a different one as an adult, it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Asian Palm Civet

modes.label: Moving the canopy • Taking only ripe fruit • Depositing the seed elsewhere

waveform.description: A flat daytime floor with a raised active block dropped into the middle of it, because the animal's operating day is a bounded night shift.

entries.closingLine: Because that nightly search is continuous, unhurried and repeated year-round, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Small-clawed Otter

modes.label: Feeling under stones • Crushing • Passing it on

waveform.description: A close-packed busy chatter of small movements, none of them large, because the work is done in many quick touches rather than in strokes.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole animal is one continuous close-range tactile search, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian subterranean termite

modes.label: Gathering plant material • Feeding it to a fungus comb inside the mound • Eating the fungus and the partly digested substrate

waveform.description: A long steady line with one dramatic excursion, because the colony runs continuously and releases its reproductives all at once.

entries.closingLine: Since foraging and comb turnover run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian swamp eel

modes.label: Gulping air into a mouth and throat richly supplied with blood vessels • Crossing wet ground and burrowing into mud • Surviving in water with almost no oxygen at all

waveform.description: A steady moderate rhythm with no dramatic features, because the animal breathes and moves at an even unhurried rate.

entries.closingLine: Since breathing recurs continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Tramp Snail

modes.label: Circling a partner for an extended courtship • Driving a calcareous dart through the body wall of the other • Mating reciprocally with the dart's secretion already acting inside the recipient

waveform.description: A long slow line with brief sharp interruptions, because a very slow animal's life contains one abrupt event.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across a season, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Weaver Ant

modes.label: Chaining across gaps • Holding leaves together • Squeezing a larva along the seam

waveform.description: A tight busy chatter of small even peaks with no gaps, the trace of thousands of small simultaneous actions.

entries.closingLine: Because thousands of small actions run simultaneously and never stop, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Asiatic Black Bear

modes.label: Climbing • Feeding • Loading
Denned • Slowed • Spending

waveform.description: A rising feeding rhythm settling into a long low winter floor.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: concentrated accumulation and a long slow drawdown.

entries.name: Asiatic Rhinoceros Beetle

modes.label: Adults boring into the unopened crown of a coconut or oil palm • Cutting through the folded fronds before they have expanded • Leaving a single tunnel that becomes a row of V-shaped cuts across every leaf as it unfurls

waveform.description: A flat line with one damaging excursion, because a single boring event produces consequences that unfold slowly afterwards.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is generational, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Atlantic Blue Marlin

modes.label: Cruising blue water • Diving cold • Explosive pursuit

waveform.description: Repeated explosive surges separated by fast cruising.

entries.closingLine: Fast, volatile and short-horizon in every pursuit, this is a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Atlantic Cod

modes.label: Growing large over many years • Producing egg numbers that rise steeply with body size • Releasing them into the water column and providing nothing further

waveform.description: A quiet line rising to one broad annual event, because spawning is a concentrated season inside an otherwise steady year.

entries.closingLine: Since generations take years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Atlantic Herring

modes.label: Synchronised • Dense • Rule-following

waveform.description: An even, tightly repeating wave: many identical small movements staying in step.

entries.closingLine: That makes the herring a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, networked and powerful only as a coordinated group.

entries.name: Atlantic Mackerel

modes.label: Swimming continuously from hatching to death • Driving water over the gills by forward motion rather than by pumping • Having no swim bladder, so stopping means sinking

waveform.description: A shallow perfectly regular oscillation with no interruption at all, because the animal never stops for any reason.

entries.closingLine: Since the tailbeat continues every second of life, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Atlantic Wolffish

modes.label: Crushing urchins, whelks and crabs with conical front teeth and molar plates • Grinding the shell fragments on a toothed palate • Feeding steadily on armoured prey nothing else takes
Ceasing to feed for several weeks after spawning • Shedding the entire dentition at once • Regrowing every tooth before feeding resumes

waveform.description: Steady feeding activity interrupted by a long flat depressed stretch, because the animal genuinely stops eating while the teeth are replaced.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, a weeks-long toothless non-feeding state is a distinct architecture, making it bimodal.

entries.name: Australasian Swamphen

modes.label: Pulling up a reed stem or a rhizome • Holding it in one foot raised to the bill • Stripping and chewing the soft base and discarding the rest

waveform.description: A steady deliberate rhythm of moderate excursions, because each item is handled individually and takes comparable effort.

entries.closingLine: Since items are processed continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Australian Funnel-web Spider

modes.label: A silk-lined burrow with a collapsed funnel entrance under a log or in a bank • Irregular silk trip lines radiating outward across the ground from that entrance • The spider waiting just inside, striking outward the instant a line is disturbed

waveform.description: A long flat waiting line with sudden brief strikes, because the spider sits motionless inside until a line moves.

entries.closingLine: Because strikes are infrequent, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Australian Pelican

modes.label: Waiting through years in coastal and inland waters without breeding • Detecting and travelling hundreds of kilometres inland when monsoon rain fills Lake Eyre • Breeding in enormous colonies on the temporary lake and leaving as it dries

waveform.description: A very long flat stretch with one large irregular event, because breeding waits years for a flood and then happens all at once.

entries.closingLine: Because the trigger is irregular and rare, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Australian Pineapplefish

modes.label: A pair of light organs on the lower jaw housing dense colonies of luminous bacteria • The bacteria supplied with nutrients and oxygen by the fish and producing continuous light in return • That light shuttered and directed by the fish to illuminate small shrimp in the dark

waveform.description: A single nocturnal plateau, because the fish is inactive by day and hunts through the dark hours.

entries.closingLine: Because hunting is nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bala Shark

modes.label: Shoaling in fast-flowing river channels in Southeast Asia • Being farmed in enormous numbers for the aquarium trade • Having the wild population collapse over the same period without anyone noticing

waveform.description: A steady shoaling rhythm without extremes, because a schooling river fish's day is continuous and even.

entries.closingLine: Since shoaling and feeding are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bald-faced Hornet

modes.label: One mated queen • Overwintering alone • Starting the first cells herself
Hundreds of workers • Envelope enlarged outward • Defended as a unit

waveform.description: A long flat floor rising into a single broad hump and collapsing back to it, because the colony is built from nothing each year and does not survive the winter.

entries.closingLine: Because a solitary founding state and a large defended collective state are both indispensable, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Ball Python

modes.label: Concealed • Waiting • Economical
Strike • Coil • Committed

waveform.description: A long flat wait, one sharp strike, then a sustained elevated hold that eases back down.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: an extremely cheap waiting state and a short, fully committed application of force.

entries.name: Ballan Wrasse

modes.label: Pulling molluscs and barnacles from rock with strong front teeth • Crushing them on paired pharyngeal plates in the throat • Working the same stretch of reef for years

waveform.description: A slow steady line with occasional modest rises, because a long-lived reef fish working the same ground has an even routine.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Banana Slug

modes.label: Laying trail • Rasping • Paying in water

waveform.description: A near-flat drift with a single slow undulation, the trace of an animal whose fastest state is still barely movement.

entries.closingLine: Because every process is slow and metered against a water budget, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Band-eyed Drone Fly

modes.label: Hovering at flowers • Passing for a bee • Larva breathing through a tube

waveform.description: A quick hovering flutter of even peaks, because the animal holds position at flowers rather than travelling between them.

entries.closingLine: Because the adult's hovering and feeding run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Banded Humbug Damselfish

modes.label: Living as a group in a single coral head with a strict size hierarchy • Each fish maintaining a size just below the one above it • Every fish moving up one place when a larger one is removed

waveform.description: A steady even rhythm with no extremes, because a group in one coral head does much the same thing all day.

entries.closingLine: Since interactions recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bank Vole

modes.label: Breeding rapidly when seed and berry crops are good • Building to high density across a whole region • Collapsing within a season as food fails and predators concentrate

waveform.description: A large slow oscillation repeating across the span, because the population itself rises and falls on a multi-year cycle.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs over years while the animals live months, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bar-headed Goose

modes.label: Crossing high passes on migration • Loading oxygen from air a third as dense • Beating continuously with no soaring

waveform.description: A working rhythm that climbs into a sustained elevated section and returns, because the crossing is a prolonged extreme effort within an ordinary year.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle repeats seasonally within a working year, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Barbel

modes.label: Holding position on gravel in fast water with a flat belly and large pectoral fins • Using the current's own force to press itself down • Feeling for invertebrates in the gravel with four barbels

waveform.description: A steady shallow rhythm sustained without large events, because the fish holds position and works the bed continuously.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Barn Funnel Weaver

modes.label: Building a tangle above with taut silk lines running down to the ground • Gluing the lower ends and leaving them under tension • Having a walking insect stick, snap the line and be lifted off its feet

waveform.description: A still line broken by isolated sharp events, because nothing happens until a line is triggered and then the capture is immediate.

entries.closingLine: Since triggers occur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Barnacle Goose

modes.label: Grazing the flush • Flying as a family • Returning to the same ledge

waveform.description: A grazing baseline lifting twice into long flat elevated plateaus, because the two journeys are sustained crossings rather than events.

entries.closingLine: Because a single continuous grazing operation is maintained across a moving geography, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Barred Eagle-Owl

modes.label: Still in the mid-storey • Ear tufts level • Listening down
Dropping • Taking • Carrying it up

waveform.description: A high quiet line with three narrow downward strikes, each returning immediately to the same level.

entries.closingLine: Because hours of near-costless listening fund a movement lasting a second, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Baya Weaver

modes.label: Weaving a hanging shell from torn grass strips • Pausing at the helmet stage for inspection • Completing only the nests a female accepts

waveform.description: Repeated climbs that reach different heights before dropping back, because each nest is built up and only some are carried through.

entries.closingLine: Since nests are built within weeks, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bearded Vulture
entries.archetype: Bones Dropped Onto a Known Rock

modes.label: Carrying • Dropping • Swallowing

waveform.description: A slow, low-cost search cycle with rare deliberate efforts.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: patient, cheap, and aimed at a resource with no queue.

entries.name: Bicolor Angelfish

modes.label: Living as one of several females in a harem held by a single male • Feeding on algae and detritus across a small area of reef • Being ranked by size within the group
Changing sex within days of the male being lost • Taking over the harem and defending it • Producing sperm from tissue that was producing eggs weeks before

waveform.description: One level held, a single transition, and a different level afterwards, because the change happens once and does not reverse.

entries.closingLine: Because the change happens once and irreversibly, it operates as a phase-change system.

entries.name: Bicolor Parrotfish

modes.label: An initial-phase female, white with a broad orange band across the head and a dark eye patch, feeding within a harem on a defended stretch of reef
A terminal-phase male, green and pink with heavy scale outlines and a yellow spot behind the pectoral, holding a territory and displaying to a group of females

waveform.description: A subdued early rhythm giving way to a bolder later one, because the animal changes its whole role partway through life.

entries.closingLine: Parrotfish of both phases scrape algae and coral with fused beak-like teeth and produce large quantities of sand, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Bivalve

modes.label: Adding shell material in daily and seasonal increments throughout life • Locking the chemistry of the surrounding water into each increment as it forms • Producing a banded record in which temperature, salinity and productivity at the time are readable decades or centuries later

waveform.description: A regular seasonal oscillation repeated without variation, because growth follows the same annual cycle every year.

entries.closingLine: Because the record accumulates over years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Black and Yellow Mud Dauber

modes.label: Building a mud cell • Stocking it with spiders stung into paralysis • Sealing one egg in with food that stays alive

waveform.description: A long series of near-identical working cycles, because the wasp repeats the same build-hunt-seal sequence cell after cell.

entries.closingLine: Since cells are completed within days, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Ant

modes.label: Laying pheromone on the return from food • Reinforcing the trail only while the source lasts • Letting it evaporate when the food runs out

waveform.description: Gradual build-ups and equally gradual declines, because a trail is reinforced into existence and then allowed to fade.

entries.closingLine: Since trails build and fade within minutes, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Giant Squirrel

modes.label: Hooking the hind feet over a branch and hanging out into space • Using both forefeet to handle large hard fruit while suspended • Feeding at the ends of branches that will not carry its weight

waveform.description: A steady moderate rhythm, because the animal moves and feeds continuously at an even pace.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding bouts recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Ground Beetle

modes.label: Running down prey and predators alike on the ground at night • Turning the tip of the abdomen toward an attacker • Discharging formic acid, quinones or other compounds from paired glands directly onto it

waveform.description: Steady running broken by extremely brief sharp discharges, because the animal moves constantly and fires rarely.

entries.closingLine: Since discharges are over in milliseconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Horse Fly

modes.label: Blade-like mandibles that cut and scissor through skin rather than piercing it • Blood welling into the resulting wound and pooling at the surface • The fly lapping that pool with a spongy mouthpart while anticoagulants in the saliva keep it flowing

waveform.description: A rapid persistent rhythm of approach and retreat, because the fly returns repeatedly after each disturbance.

entries.closingLine: Because approaches repeat constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Molly

modes.label: Internal fertilisation through a modified anal fin acting as a gonopodium • Storing viable sperm in folds of the female's reproductive tract for months • Producing several successive broods of live young from that one stored supply

waveform.description: A repeating cycle of broods at regular intervals, because each stored batch is released on the same rhythm.

entries.closingLine: Because broods recur on a cycle of weeks, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Rat
entries.archetype: Climbing to Nests Nothing Else Reaches

modes.label: Climbing rigging and branches • Breeding fast • Emptying a seabird colony

waveform.description: A fast volatile rhythm of rapid breeding and constant movement.

entries.closingLine: Short lives and rapid breeding make this a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Sea Bass

modes.label: Occupying wrecks, reefs and hard structure on the shelf • Moving inshore and offshore with the seasons • Shifting the whole distribution northward as bottom water has warmed

waveform.description: A varying line whose whole level drifts steadily upward across the span, because the baseline itself is moving.

entries.closingLine: Since the shift runs across decades, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Skirt Tetra

modes.label: Shoaling loosely while feeding • Releasing alarm chemical when skin is torn • Contracting the whole shoal within seconds

waveform.description: A long calm line broken by one abrupt vertical drop with a slow recovery, because the alarm is instantaneous while the return to normal is not.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding and shoaling run through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Spiny-tailed Iguana

modes.label: Basking in the open where escape distance is long • Running on the hind legs at speeds recorded above thirty kilometres an hour • Reaching a burrow, a crevice or a tree before anything can close

waveform.description: A still basking line broken by extremely sharp brief events, because the animal is motionless and then running flat out.

entries.closingLine: Since escape runs are brief and repeated, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Black-crested Coquette

modes.label: The wing tracing a horizontal figure of eight rather than beating up and down • The shoulder joint rotating so the wing inverts at the end of each stroke • Lift generated on the backstroke as well as the forward stroke, holding the body still in the air

waveform.description: An extremely fast even oscillation with no variation, because both halves of every stroke do the same work.

entries.closingLine: Because wingbeats run dozens per second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Black-footed Cat
entries.archetype: A Kill Every Half Hour, All Night

modes.label: Hunting • Relentless • Successful

waveform.description: Dense unbroken hunting activity across a whole night.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: continuous, unbanked and running with no margin.

entries.name: Black-headed Gull

modes.label: Nesting on open ground in a dense colony • Picking up the shell within minutes of a chick hatching • Flying it away from the nest before returning

waveform.description: A colony baseline broken by regular brief events, because the removals are short deliberate actions within continuous activity.

entries.closingLine: Since removals recur through the season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Black-naped Oriole

modes.label: A horizontal fork selected near the end of a slender outer branch rather than against the trunk • Fibre, bark strips and grass woven and bound around both arms of the fork to form a deep hanging cup • The nest suspended beyond the reach of anything that cannot fly, on branches too thin to bear a climbing animal

waveform.description: A single seasonal build and decline, because the construction and the brood run once through the year.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Black-winged Stilt

modes.label: Wading in water deeper than any comparable wader can enter • Picking invertebrates from the surface and just below with a fine straight bill • Feeding on ground that shorter-legged species have to leave

waveform.description: A steady deliberate rhythm of similar events, because the bird picks continuously at an unhurried pace.

entries.closingLine: Since picking recurs constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blacktip Reef Shark

modes.label: Never stopping • Reading electrical fields • Working a small known patch

waveform.description: A continuous unbroken swell that never touches a baseline, because this animal has no resting state to return to.

entries.closingLine: Because the swimming and the sensing run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blanket Octopus

modes.label: Drifting in open water • Carrying stolen tentacles • Unfurling when pressed

waveform.description: A loose drifting swell with no sharp edges, because an animal with nowhere to hide never accelerates to hide in it.

entries.closingLine: Because the drifting and hunting run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blood Parrot Cichlid

modes.label: Drawing food in by suction through a permanently open beak-like mouth • Failing to grip or tear anything • Feeding slowly on small sinking items

waveform.description: A shallow repetitive pattern with no strong events at all, because every feeding action is weak and nothing about the routine varies.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding attempts repeat through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blossom-headed Parakeet

modes.label: A bill built for cracking seed and climbing, not for excavating sound timber • Nest sites limited to existing holes cut by woodpeckers and barbets or produced by decay • Competition with other cavity nesters for a supply the parakeet has no way to increase

waveform.description: A steady annual rhythm with a raised breeding period, because the constraint applies once a year.

entries.closingLine: Because breeding is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue Crane

modes.label: Nesting on open dry grassland and cropland rather than in marsh • Laying directly on bare ground with no built nest and no surrounding water • Defending the site by long sightlines and aggressive approach instead of by inaccessibility

waveform.description: A flat line with one long raised breeding season, because the whole commitment falls in a single annual period.

entries.closingLine: Because breeding is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue Glaucus

modes.label: Floating upside down • Eating the stinger • Storing its cells intact

waveform.description: A slow surface drift with no propulsion in it, because the animal does not swim and the current supplies the movement.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at the speed of a current, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue Mud Dauber

modes.label: Carrying water • Remodelling somebody else's mud • Stocking one cell at a time

waveform.description: A measured repeating rhythm of separate errands, each one similar to the last because each cell is filled the same way.

entries.closingLine: Because that cycle runs steadily through the warm months, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue Parrotfish

modes.label: Biting algae and its rock substrate with fused beak-like teeth • Crushing the whole mouthful in a pharyngeal mill • Voiding the rock as fine carbonate sand

waveform.description: A very dense and completely regular series of identical bites, because the animal works the substrate continuously all day.

entries.closingLine: Since bites recur every few seconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue Tang
entries.archetype: A Folding Blade at the Tail

modes.label: Grazing algae across the reef in loose groups • Keeping a hinged spine folded flat in a groove at the tail base • Flicking the tail sideways to cut anything that presses too close

waveform.description: An even grazing rhythm broken by occasional sharp events, because the blade is deployed rarely against a background of ordinary feeding.

entries.closingLine: Since grazing is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue Tit
entries.archetype: A Brood Timed to a Peak

modes.label: Reading spring temperature and vegetation to set laying date • Incubating so hatching meets the caterpillar peak • Feeding a large brood through a window of about a fortnight

waveform.description: A long ordinary line rising to one concentrated peak and falling back, because everything in the year converges on a single short window.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding trips recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue Wildebeest

modes.label: Walking the green edge • Cropping short grass • Never settling
Calving together • Standing within minutes • Swamping the predators

waveform.description: A long even walking rhythm interrupted by one short raised block, because the calving is a narrow window rather than a spike or a season.

entries.closingLine: Because a continuous movement funds one narrow synchronised release, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Blue-and-yellow Macaw

modes.label: Flying wingtip to wingtip • Calling continuously • Landing at the same clay bank

waveform.description: A loud regular exchange of similar peaks, because the calling is continuous and answered rather than occasional.

entries.closingLine: Because the calling and flying run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue-crowned Hanging Parrot

modes.label: The female cutting strips of leaf and bark with her bill • Tucking those strips among the feathers of her rump and flanks rather than carrying them in the bill • Flying to the nest hole with both bill and feet free and unloading the strips there

waveform.description: A brisk repeating rhythm of trips, because the bird makes many short journeys carrying material.

entries.closingLine: Because nest building is seasonal, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue-fronted Amazon

modes.label: A thick muscular tongue with its own skeletal support and fine motor control • Food rotated and positioned against the bill by the tongue while the bill does the cutting • The same tongue shaping the airflow from the syrinx to produce consonant-like sounds without lips or teeth

waveform.description: A busy continuous rhythm, because the tongue is working constantly during both feeding and calling.

entries.closingLine: Because both activities are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue-headed Macaw

modes.label: Feeding on unripe seeds and fruit protected by tannins and alkaloids that most animals cannot process • Gathering at exposed riverbank clay faces and eating the clay itself • Clay minerals binding those compounds in the gut so the toxins pass through without being absorbed

waveform.description: A regular daily rhythm with a recurring dip, because the birds feed steadily and gather at the clay at a predictable time.

entries.closingLine: Because the visits are daily and the diet steady, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue-naped Parrot

modes.label: Birds feeding scattered through dense canopy where none can see any other • Loud contact calls exchanged constantly to establish who is where • The flock held together as a structure in sound rather than in sight

waveform.description: A rapid call-and-answer rhythm, because the exchange continues constantly while the birds feed.

entries.closingLine: Because calling is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue-rumped Parrot

modes.label: Two toes forward and two back on each foot, giving an opposed grip rather than a perching one • Food lifted to the bill in one foot while the bird stands on the other • The bill acting as a third point of contact so climbing and manipulation use the same three limbs

waveform.description: A steady busy rhythm of handling, because the bird works continuously at food with feet and bill.

entries.closingLine: Because handling is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue-winged Macaw

modes.label: Flocks that on close inspection consist of pairs flying side by side rather than a uniform mass • Each pair maintaining position relative to one another rather than to the flock as a whole • The bond persisting across years and outside the breeding season entirely

waveform.description: A close paired rhythm in which two elements track each other, because the unit of the flock is two birds rather than one.

entries.closingLine: Because the coordination is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bluebottle Fly

modes.label: Detecting sulphur compounds from decomposition at long range • Flying upwind to the source • Laying within hours of death

waveform.description: A fast continuous oscillation with no structure at a larger scale, because the animal is searching constantly and everything happens within hours.

entries.closingLine: Since the whole search-and-lay cycle runs within hours, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Blueface Angelfish

modes.label: Grazing sponges and tunicates loaded with toxins and glass spicules • Processing those compounds rather than avoiding them • Feeding on a resource left almost untouched by other reef fish

waveform.description: A very even line, because the food supply is constant and requires no timing or pursuit at all.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is steady, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Bluespine Unicornfish

modes.label: Ranging the reef • Cropping tough weed • Blades always out

waveform.description: A steady rolling browse with even peaks, because the animal works its way across reef without stopping or hurrying.

entries.closingLine: Because the browsing is continuous and unhurried across a large area, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bluestreak Cleaner Wrasse

modes.label: Stationed • Repeat-trade • Trusted

waveform.description: A steady working rhythm: client after client handled at the same pace through the day.

entries.closingLine: That makes the wrasse a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, networked and built on repeated exchange rather than any single event.

entries.name: Bocage's Wall Lizard

modes.label: Dorsal patterning of green, brown and black reticulation matching lichen-mottled granite • Populations differing in ground colour and pattern density according to the rock they occupy • Individuals remaining on the substrate their pattern matches rather than moving between rock types

waveform.description: A brisk regular rhythm of basking and darting, because the lizard alternates between stillness and short sprints.

entries.closingLine: Because basking and darting alternate constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Boeseman's Rainbowfish

modes.label: A species confined to a small group of connected lakes in the Vogelkop peninsula of West Papua and nowhere else on earth • Males carrying a striking split colouring, blue-grey at the front and orange at the rear, that made them highly desirable in the aquarium trade • Enormous numbers exported from those lakes through the 1980s and 1990s, from a total range of a few square kilometres

waveform.description: A decline flattening at a low level, because the population fell under collection and has stayed reduced.

entries.closingLine: Because the decline runs across decades, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Bold Jumper

modes.label: Attaching a dragline before every leap • Paying it out during the jump and using tension to control pitch and rotation • Braking on it if the landing fails, and climbing back up the same line

waveform.description: Steady movement broken by very brief full-depth events, because the animal stalks constantly and jumps occasionally.

entries.closingLine: Since jumps recur through the day, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Bornean Pygmy Elephant

modes.label: Walking river valleys • Opening paths • Remembering routes for decades

waveform.description: A slow steady rhythm of travel measured in decades.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Brahminy Kite

modes.label: Soaring low over harbours, estuaries and fishing grounds watching other birds rather than the water • Harrying terns, gulls and other raptors until they release or drop what they are carrying • Catching the dropped item in the air or taking it from the surface before the owner recovers it

waveform.description: A steady patrolling rhythm with repeated chases, because the bird soars continuously and harries whenever an opportunity appears.

entries.closingLine: Because chases recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Brazilian Lava Lizard

modes.label: Moving between sun and shade many times an hour • Changing posture and orientation to the sun to control heat gain • Holding body temperature within a narrow band by position alone

waveform.description: A rapid regular alternation maintained throughout, because the animal is moving between sun and shade continuously.

entries.closingLine: Since the shuttling recurs constantly, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Brill

modes.label: Settling onto a new substrate and comparing it against the eyes' input • Redistributing pigment within chromatophores under nervous control • Reproducing the tone, contrast and coarseness of the ground within minutes

waveform.description: A smooth slow oscillation with no sharp features, because the change is gradual and continuous rather than a switch.

entries.closingLine: Since matching happens over minutes, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Brimstone Butterfly

modes.label: Flying from early spring through summer • Feeding at flowers and searching for buckthorn to lay on • Living as an active adult for weeks at a time
Hanging among ivy or bramble with wings closed and leaf-shaped • Accumulating glycerol and other cryoprotectants in the tissues • Surviving frost, snow and rain without shelter for months

waveform.description: Long flat depressed stretches alternating with an extended active period, because the year is genuinely divided into two different states.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two physiologies, making it a bimodal system.

entries.name: Bristlenose Pleco

modes.label: Males developing branched fleshy tentacles across the snout that resemble a mass of wriggling larvae • Occupying and defending a cave or crevice into which a female is invited to lay • The male remaining alone in the cave fanning and guarding the eggs until they hatch and the fry disperse

waveform.description: A long sustained raised commitment, because the male holds the cave and tends the clutch continuously for days.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Broad-bodied Chaser

modes.label: Watching from a perch with an upward-facing eye region • Launching on an intercept course • Taking the prey from beneath in flight

waveform.description: Very frequent near-vertical spikes from a constant baseline, because each attack is a brief, violent excursion from a motionless perch.

entries.closingLine: Since attacks recur within seconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Bronze Ground Beetle

modes.label: Seizing a slug or caterpillar with curved mandibles • Regurgitating digestive fluid onto it • Sucking up the liquefied tissue and leaving the rest

waveform.description: A quiet line with occasional broad raised sections, because feeding is a slow process rather than a rapid strike.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding bouts recur nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Brown Anole

modes.label: Holding a low perch and watching • Snapping the dewlap open on a hinged cartilage • Folding it away again immediately

waveform.description: A dense train of very sharp identical spikes, because each display is a brief full-amplitude event repeated many times an hour.

entries.closingLine: Since displays repeat within minutes, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Brown Crab

modes.label: Feeding on molluscs and crustaceans with heavy black-tipped claws • Buried in sediment or wedged into rock by day • Carrying a hard shell that grows not at all
Withdrawing from the old shell over hours • Lying soft, swollen with water and unable to feed or defend itself • Hardening over days to weeks before returning to normal life

waveform.description: Normal activity interrupted by a long flat depressed section, because the animal genuinely stops being capable of anything while it is soft.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two different states, making this a bimodal system.

entries.name: Brown Rat

modes.label: Avoiding the new • Taking a trace • Coming back if nothing happened

waveform.description: A cautious baseline with small probes that grow steadily taller, because each successful test licenses a larger one.

entries.closingLine: Because the sampling routine runs continuously every night, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Brown Recluse

modes.label: Flat against a hidden surface • Irregular sheet web • Months without food if needed

waveform.description: A near-flat line with almost no movement at all, because an animal built around not being found does very little that would reveal it.

entries.closingLine: Since everything runs slowly and continuously, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Brown Shrike

modes.label: Feet built for perching rather than for gripping and tearing, unlike a raptor's • Prey carried to a thorn, barbed wire or a sharp twig and pushed onto it • The spike holding the carcass while the hooked bill tears it, and the same larder storing surplus for later

waveform.description: A patrolling rhythm with repeated captures, because the bird hunts from perches through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because captures recur through the day, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Brown Shrimp

modes.label: Settling onto sand and beating the pleopods to throw grains over the back • Working the body down until only the eyes and antennae remain clear • Emerging at night to hunt across the same sediment

waveform.description: Long buried stretches alternating with an active period, because the animal is either inside the sediment or hunting over it.

entries.closingLine: Since burial and emergence recur daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Brown Widow Spider

modes.label: Colonising urban structures far more densely and rapidly than the native widow it replaces • Juveniles preying on black widow spiders where the two meet, rather than merely competing for space • A venom of comparable potency delivered in far smaller quantity and with a far lower tendency to bite

waveform.description: A steady expansion levelling off, because the spread is continuous and eventually saturates the available structures.

entries.closingLine: Because the spread runs across seasons, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Brown-throated Sunbird

modes.label: A bird that perches beside a flower rather than hovering in front of it • A decurved bill and tubular tongue reaching into the corolla from that fixed position • Flowers selected partly for whether there is something to stand on, so the plant's structure determines which birds can use it

waveform.description: A busy rhythm of short flights between perches, because the bird moves constantly but never hovers for long.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Brownbanded Bamboo Shark

modes.label: Suppressing metabolic rate and brain activity when oxygen in a tide pool falls away • Surviving hours with almost none rather than attempting to leave • Walking between pools on the pectoral and pelvic fins when it does move

waveform.description: A slow trough rather than a peak, because the animal responds to stress by dropping activity down and then recovering.

entries.closingLine: Because tidal cycles govern the pattern, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Budgerigar

modes.label: Calling constantly • Matching the flock • Following the rain

waveform.description: A dense rapid chatter of near-identical peaks, because the flock's sound is a continuous overlapping exchange.

entries.closingLine: Because the calling and matching run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Buff-tip Moth

modes.label: Wings rolled tightly around the body into a cylinder rather than held flat • Silvery grey wing surfaces and buff patches at the head and wingtips reproducing bark and the pale exposed wood of a break • The insect resting in the open as a broken twig rather than hiding against a surface

waveform.description: An almost perfectly level line, because the animal rests without moving for the whole of the day.

entries.closingLine: Because the posture is held all day, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Buffy Fish Owl

modes.label: Low perch • Bare legs over water • Reading the surface
Dropping • Gripping • Lifting clear

waveform.description: A high quiet line dropping three times to the floor and returning, because the action in this system goes downward rather than upward.

entries.closingLine: Because hours of almost costless watching fund a movement measured in seconds, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Bumblebee

modes.label: Decoupling the flight muscles from the wings and contracting them against each other • Generating heat until the thorax reaches around thirty degrees regardless of the air temperature • Flying in cold, wet and early-morning conditions that ground other bees entirely

waveform.description: A steep initial climb settling into a busy sustained rhythm, because warming precedes a long working day.

entries.closingLine: Because warming and foraging repeat constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Burbot

modes.label: Gathering on gravel shoals in the coldest weeks of the year • Forming a writhing ball of dozens of fish beneath the ice • Releasing eggs and milt into the middle of it and dispersing

waveform.description: One deep sustained excursion at the start of the span with a long flat remainder, because the single event falls in midwinter.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Burgundy Goliath Birdeater

modes.label: Turning the abdomen towards a threat and rubbing the hind legs across it • Releasing a cloud of barbed urticating hairs into the air • Producing a hissing stridulation with the leg bristles at the same time

waveform.description: A flat line with a short burst of sharp activity, because the spider does nothing for long periods and then defends violently.

entries.closingLine: Because episodes are rare, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Cabbage Cluster Moth

modes.label: Eggs laid in clusters on the undersides of leaves near the centre of the plant • Larvae moving inward to the growing point and feeding within the folded heart leaves • The tissue around them shielding them from any spray applied to the outside of the plant

waveform.description: A gradual build to a peak and decline, because the infestation develops inside the plant over weeks.

entries.closingLine: Because generations run over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Cabbage White

modes.label: Feeding on brassica leaves that release mustard oils when damaged • Redirecting that reaction in the gut with a nitrile-specifier protein • Excreting harmless nitriles instead of the toxic isothiocyanates

waveform.description: A rapid unvarying repetition, because generations follow one another continuously through the season.

entries.closingLine: Since generations turn over in weeks, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Calico domestic cat

modes.label: Calm • Watchful • Rhythmic
Precise • Fast • Opportunistic

waveform.description: A controlled mid-frequency rhythm interrupted by a precise high-frequency pounce.

entries.closingLine: The cat is therefore a bimodal system: cruise quietly, then act fast when the opening is right.

entries.name: California Sea Lion

modes.label: Manoeuvring • Pursuing • Whisker-guided

waveform.description: A continuously curving line that never settles into one direction.

entries.closingLine: That makes the sea lion a mid-frequency system: continuous, agile and organised around changing direction rather than sustaining one.

entries.name: California Spiny Lobster

modes.label: Sheltering in rock crevices by day with antennae outward • Drawing a soft plectrum at the antenna base across a file on the head • Producing a rasping noise that continues even immediately after a moult

waveform.description: A rapid regular rasping pattern held throughout, because the sound is produced by a repeated slipping motion rather than by discrete strikes.

entries.closingLine: Since the rasp repeats many times a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Candy-striped Leafhopper

modes.label: Specialised gland cells producing protein granules a few hundred nanometres across, secreted in liquid and dried onto the surface • The insect combing that powder over its whole body with brushes on its legs • A microscopically rough coating that water and sticky plant sap cannot wet or adhere to

waveform.description: A steady maintenance rhythm, because the insect grooms and recoats itself continuously while feeding.

entries.closingLine: Because the maintenance is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Cape Buffalo
entries.archetype: A Herd That Votes by Gaze

modes.label: Resting as a herd before a move • Having individual females stand, gaze in a direction and lie down again • Moving off in the average of the directions gazed in rather than following any leader

waveform.description: A long steady line with periodic broad rises, because the herd is at rest and then moves as a single event.

entries.closingLine: Since moves occur daily within a slow annual cycle, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Cape Teal

modes.label: Supraorbital salt glands excreting concentrated brine through the nostrils • Feeding on brine shrimp and invertebrates in saline and alkaline pans other ducks avoid • Moving between scattered temporary pans as they fill and dry across the interior

waveform.description: A steady moderate rhythm, because the bird works shallow water continuously and moves between pans as they change.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding and movement are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Capuchin Monkey

modes.label: Juveniles sitting close to adults cracking nuts and watching the whole sequence repeatedly • Handling the discarded hammers and anvils afterwards without producing a strike • Acquiring a technique over years that no individual works out alone

waveform.description: A busy repeating rhythm of attempts and observation, because learning happens through constant repetition.

entries.closingLine: Because learning and use are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Caribbean Spiny Lobster

modes.label: Sheltering communally in crevices with others • Detecting a chemical cue from an infected individual in the urine • Refusing to share a den with it and moving elsewhere

waveform.description: A social baseline broken by decisive avoidance events, because ordinary communal life is interrupted by rejections.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Carpenter Ant

modes.label: Cutting galleries through dead and damp wood with the mandibles • Carrying the shavings out and discarding them rather than eating them • Feeding instead on honeydew from sap-feeding insects and on other insects entirely outside the nest

waveform.description: A long nocturnal build and decline, because this is a night-foraging ant whose activity rises and falls with darkness.

entries.closingLine: Because colony cycles run across seasons, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Carpenter Bee

modes.label: Landing on the outside of a long tubular flower rather than at its opening • Slitting the base of the corolla with sharp mandibles • Drinking nectar directly through that hole without contacting the anthers or stigma at all

waveform.description: A brisk repeating rhythm of visits, because the bee works flower after flower steadily through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because visits are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Carrion Beetle

modes.label: Downwind • Scanning • Converging

waveform.description: A long even searching rhythm interrupted by the occasional find.

entries.closingLine: The searching never stops and rarely pays, which makes this a mid-frequency system whose entire return is concentrated into a handful of finds.

entries.name: Cat Flea

modes.label: A fully formed adult remaining inside its silk cocoon rather than emerging when development finishes • That adult waiting for weeks or months, resistant to insecticide and to drying while sealed • Emergence triggered by vibration, warmth and carbon dioxide, so it appears only when something is present to feed on

waveform.description: A long flat dormant line with one abrupt emergence, because nothing happens until a host arrives and then everything does.

entries.closingLine: Because the wait runs across months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Celebes Crested Macaque

modes.label: Crowding in close • Bared teeth as greeting • Copying what worked

waveform.description: A varied social rhythm of unequal peaks, because each is a different interaction rather than a repeat of the last.

entries.closingLine: Because the watching and copying run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Centipede

modes.label: Running down prey on many pairs of legs • Seizing it with the first pair of legs converted into hollow fangs • Injecting venom through them before anything can be lost

waveform.description: Rapid movement broken by extremely narrow full-depth strikes, because the animal runs constantly and the seizure is instantaneous.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes occur in a fraction of a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Central American Agouti

modes.label: Burying • Stolen • Re-buried

waveform.description: A steady repeated caching rhythm.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady repeated burying in which the losses do the work.

entries.name: Central Bearded Dragon

modes.label: Shuttling • Sun-set • Economical

waveform.description: A low line drifting gently up and down as the animal corrects its temperature.

entries.closingLine: That makes the dragon a low-frequency system: economical, unhurried and regulated by position instead of by expenditure.

entries.name: Cetti's Warbler

modes.label: Skulking • Covered • Unseen
Explosive • Loud • Brief

waveform.description: A quiet hidden baseline punctuated by two extremely tall, very narrow bursts.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a quiet concealed baseline and a short, very high-output broadcast.

entries.name: Chaco Golden Knee Tarantula

modes.label: A metabolic rate far below that of comparable active invertebrates • Long periods motionless in a burrow with no feeding at all, sometimes months • A lifespan reaching two decades or more in females, with growth measured in years

waveform.description: An almost completely level line, because the animal's activity barely varies from one month to the next.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs on a timescale of months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Chain Pickerel

modes.label: The body drawn into an S shape while hanging motionless among weed • The whole trunk musculature contracting along one side to straighten it in a single stroke • Acceleration produced by the body itself rather than by any fin, covering the strike distance in a fraction of a second

waveform.description: A quiet waiting baseline with extremely abrupt vertical strikes, because the attack is a single explosive event.

entries.closingLine: Because the strike itself takes hundredths of a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Cherry Shrimp

modes.label: A wild form that is drab translucent brown with no bright colour at all • Selectively bred lines fixed for red, yellow, blue, green and black over many generations • Any two colour lines crossed producing offspring that revert towards the wild brown within a few generations

waveform.description: A steady rhythm drifting back upward, because the colour lines revert whenever selection stops.

entries.closingLine: Because reversion runs across generations, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Chicken Mite

modes.label: Feeding on roosting birds for under an hour at night and then leaving them entirely • Spending the day in cracks, perch joints and structural crevices away from any bird • Surviving months in those crevices without feeding if the birds are removed

waveform.description: A flat daytime line with a single nocturnal feeding episode, because the mite is on the bird only briefly each night.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is nightly and development takes days, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Chickweed Geometer Moth

modes.label: Carrying feathered antennae with an enormous surface area of receptors • Detecting female pheromone at concentrations of a few molecules • Flying upwind along the plume until the source is reached

waveform.description: A rapid fine oscillation with no strong features, because the searching flight is continuous small adjustment.

entries.closingLine: Since the flight is continuous adjustment, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Chinese Hwamei

modes.label: Learning and incorporating phrases from other species heard in the surrounding scrub • Assembling them into long varied sequences rather than repeating a fixed species song • Continuing to add new material through life so no two individuals sing the same thing

waveform.description: An irregular varied rhythm that never repeats exactly, because the song is assembled rather than fixed.

entries.closingLine: Because learning and singing are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Chinese Mantis

modes.label: Waiting motionless on vegetation and increasingly at garden feeders • Striking with raptorial forelegs in a few hundredths of a second • Taking prey up to and including small birds

waveform.description: A long motionless line broken by extremely brief full-depth strikes, because nothing happens and then the capture is over.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes are sudden and rare, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Chinese Pond Heron

modes.label: Standing folded and drab • Striking • Opening into white

waveform.description: A patient wading rhythm of small regular dips, because the strikes are frequent and the animal rarely stops moving.

entries.closingLine: Because the stalking and striking run together through the workable hours, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Chinese Rice Grasshopper

modes.label: A rice pest occurring in very large numbers in the same fields as the crop it damages • Collected, farmed and sold as food across parts of China, where it is a valued seasonal item • Harvesting operating simultaneously as pest control and as production, so the insect is both the problem and a product

waveform.description: A seasonal build and collapse, because the population rises through the crop season and is then harvested.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is seasonal, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Chital

modes.label: Grazing under the troop • Taking what is dropped • Barking what it smells

waveform.description: A steady grazing rhythm with two brief sharp lifts, because the alarm is an interruption rather than a state.

entries.closingLine: Because the grazing and the listening run together through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Chocolate Chip Sea Star

modes.label: Gripping • Creeping • Rebuilding

waveform.description: A single almost imperceptible swell across the whole span, the flattest trace a working animal can produce.

entries.closingLine: Because every process it runs is measured in months and costs close to nothing per hour, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Christmas Island Red Crab

modes.label: Waiting in forest burrows through the dry season • Moving to the coast en masse when the wet season rains begin • Releasing larvae into the sea at the turn of the high tide on a specific lunar day

waveform.description: A long flat line rising into one concentrated event and falling back, because everything happens in a few weeks of one month.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Cichlid

modes.label: Oral jaws at the front used only for catching and holding • A second set of jaws in the throat, formed from modified gill arches, used for processing • Each set free to specialise because neither has to do the other's job

waveform.description: A busy varied rhythm without a single dominant pattern, because the family does many different things at once.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Citrus Mealybug

modes.label: Settled • Wax-covered • Sap-fed

waveform.description: An almost unchanging low line: a settled feeder that barely moves at all.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, settled and protected by what it builds over itself.

entries.name: Clothes & House Moth

modes.label: Feeding as a larva on wool, fur, feathers and horn • Running a highly alkaline gut with strongly reducing conditions • Breaking the disulphide bonds that make keratin indigestible to almost everything else

waveform.description: A long slow even line with a small rise, because the larva feeds quietly for months and the adult stage is brief.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Clown Knifefish

modes.label: Holding the body rigid and driving with a long undulating anal fin • Reversing direction by reversing the wave • Manoeuvring through submerged roots without turning around

waveform.description: A smooth continuous wave of constant amplitude, because propulsion itself is a travelling wave rather than a series of strokes.

entries.closingLine: Since fin waves run many times a second, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Coal Tit
