modes.label: Taking one seed at a time and hiding each in a separate place • Distributing caches over a wide area of bark, moss and needles • Returning to specific sites over weeks using spatial memory

waveform.description: A rapid unvarying repetition of identical small actions, because the bird makes the same short trip over and over.

entries.closingLine: Since caching trips recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Cobweb Spider

modes.label: Vertical silk lines running from a tangled web down to the ground, glued at the bottom and held under tension • An insect walking into one sticking to the glue and snapping the line free • The prey hauled up off the surface as the line contracts, leaving it hanging and helpless

waveform.description: A long flat line with sudden sharp releases, because the web sits loaded until something triggers it.

entries.closingLine: Because triggering is occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Cocoa Tussock Moth

modes.label: A winged male flying at night, tracking female pheromone across distance and mating with whatever he finds
A wingless female emerging from her cocoon, remaining on it, releasing pheromone and laying her entire clutch on the cocoon she emerged from

waveform.description: A mobile varied rhythm giving way to a flat stationary one, because the two sexes are doing entirely different things.

entries.closingLine: The two sexes run different architectures, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Coconut Octopus

modes.label: Gathering • Hauling • Deploying

waveform.description: A laboured working pace lifted where the shells are pulled shut.

entries.closingLine: Continuous transport and deployment of its own cover makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Collared Peccary

modes.label: A gland on the lower back releasing a strong musky secretion • Animals rubbing head and flank against each other's glands repeatedly through the day • The whole herd converging on one blended odour that marks membership

waveform.description: A continuous even rhythm, because the rubbing and reinforcement happens throughout every day without episodes.

entries.closingLine: Because the reinforcement is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Commerson's Frogfish

modes.label: A modified first dorsal spine forming a rod with a fleshy lure at the tip • That lure worked in front of the mouth so it moves like a small worm or shrimp • The mouth expanding explosively when a fish comes to investigate, drawing it in faster than any strike can be seen

waveform.description: A near-motionless line broken by two extremely brief events, because nothing happens until the strike.

entries.closingLine: Because strikes are rare, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Blackbird

modes.label: Flicking leaves aside • Running and stopping • Listening down

waveform.description: Flat runs broken by short identical flicks, because the bird alternates between holding still and turning something over.

entries.closingLine: Since the searching and listening run together through every daylight hour, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Bream

modes.label: Tilting head down over soft mud • Shooting the jaws forward and downward into a tube • Sucking sediment in, sorting the invertebrates and blowing the rest back out

waveform.description: A steady even rhythm of similar events, because the fish works the bottom at a constant deliberate pace.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding actions repeat constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Buzzard

modes.label: Circling in rising air with broad wings and splayed primary feathers • Gaining height at almost no metabolic cost • Covering ground and scanning it from a height nothing else can hold for hours

waveform.description: A slow smooth drifting line with very little structure, because the animal is being carried rather than driving itself.

entries.closingLine: Since soaring is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Carpet Moth

modes.label: Settling flat against a surface with wings spread rather than folded • Carrying dark bands that run continuously across fore and hind wing • Having the outline of a moth replaced by a pattern of stripes on a flat plane

waveform.description: A quiet even line with small occasional disturbances, because the animal is motionless for long periods and flies briefly.

entries.closingLine: Since resting bouts alternate with flight through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Chiffchaff

modes.label: Singing a simple two-note phrase repeated from high in a tree • Recognising and responding only to that pattern • Ignoring the near-identical bird singing something else

waveform.description: A strict alternation of two levels repeated without variation, because the song is literally two notes traded back and forth.

entries.closingLine: Since song bouts recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Cusimanse

modes.label: Spread out • Nose down • Chirping

waveform.description: A dense, unbroken chatter rhythm with no long pauses in it.

entries.closingLine: Continuous, unhurried ground searching makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Darter

modes.label: Basking flat on a warm surface to raise thoracic temperature • Flying only once the flight muscles are warm enough • Angling the abdomen to the sun to control the temperature

waveform.description: Repeated short flights from a returning baseline, because the animal alternates between perching and brief sorties all day.

entries.closingLine: Since sorties recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Earthworm

modes.label: Continuous • Processing • Burrowing

waveform.description: A steady mid-frequency rhythm: the same modest amount of work repeated without pause.

entries.closingLine: That makes the earthworm a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, continuous and defined by steady throughput rather than any decisive event.

entries.name: Common Eastern Firefly

modes.label: Flying a rising J-shaped flash at dusk • Waiting a fixed interval for a reply • Answering only a response with the correct delay

waveform.description: Alternating tall and short spikes separated by even gaps, because the exchange is a call and a reply with a fixed interval between them.

entries.closingLine: Since flashes repeat every few seconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Common European Harvestman

modes.label: Taking small prey, carrion and plant material directly into the mouth • Swallowing particles rather than liquefying them outside the body • Feeding on things no spider could process at all

waveform.description: A steady even rhythm with no dramatic features, because the animal forages continuously and slowly.

entries.closingLine: Since foraging is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Field Grasshopper

modes.label: Males stridulating by drawing a row of pegs on the hind femur across a vein on the forewing • Each species producing a characteristic pattern of pulses and pauses rather than a distinctive appearance • Females responding only to their own species' pattern, so the song rather than any structure decides who mates with whom

waveform.description: A patterned sequence of pulses and gaps repeated exactly, because the rhythm rather than the pitch carries the information.

entries.closingLine: Because the song cycles many times a second, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Flesh Fly

modes.label: Finding • Depositing • Leaving

waveform.description: Repeated short bursts of finding and depositing.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: brief contested opportunities captured by deleting the slowest step.

entries.name: Common Frog

modes.label: Feeding on land through spring and summer • Breathing with lungs and skin together • Hunting invertebrates in damp vegetation
Lying at the bottom of a pond through winter • Taking up oxygen entirely through the skin from the water • Not surfacing, not feeding and barely moving for months

waveform.description: Active variation alternating with a long flat depressed stretch, because the animal genuinely switches between two ways of breathing.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two respiratory regimes, making it a bimodal system.

entries.name: Common fruit-piercing moth

modes.label: Flying into orchards after dark • Driving a stiffened barbed proboscis through intact fruit skin • Drinking juice from inside and leaving a puncture that rots

waveform.description: A flat nocturnal baseline with isolated deep punctures, because each feeding event is a discrete penetration rather than a continuous draw.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding visits recur nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Grass Blue

modes.label: Completing a generation in a few weeks on low-growing legumes • Producing overlapping broods all year in warm climates • Colonising any patch of clover, medick or lucerne that appears

waveform.description: A rapid unvarying repetition across the whole span, because generations follow one another with no seasonal break at all.

entries.closingLine: Since generations turn over in weeks, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Green Darner

modes.label: Intercepting • Turning on the wing • Covering ground

waveform.description: A dense fast oscillation running the full height of the frame with almost no gaps, because this animal is either flying hard or not operating.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal's operating existence is fast and short-horizon, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Green Magpie

modes.label: Brilliant green plumage produced by a yellow carotenoid pigment laid over blue structural colour • That carotenoid obtained entirely from the diet, principally from invertebrate prey • The green fading to turquoise and then blue when the diet lacks it or when sunlight degrades it faster than it is replaced

waveform.description: A steady rhythm drifting gradually downward, because the colour is maintained continuously and declines when it is not.

entries.closingLine: Because the turnover runs over weeks, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Harvestman

modes.label: Stilted • Slow • Shedding

waveform.description: A low, slow, almost featureless trace with very little variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, cheap and built on distance and sacrifice rather than on defence.

entries.name: Common Hill Myna

modes.label: Young birds learning calls from same-sex neighbours in their own small area rather than from their parents • Distinct local dialects forming across distances of a few kilometres • No imitation of other species in the wild at all, despite a famous capacity for it in captivity

waveform.description: A varied local rhythm, because the material is specific to one place and exchanged constantly within it.

entries.closingLine: Because calling is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Hippopotamus

modes.label: Submerged • Pod-bound • Holding a stretch
Walking out • Cropping short grass • Returning before dawn

waveform.description: A deep flat floor with a raised plateau lifted out of it once, because the animal changes medium rather than intensity.

entries.closingLine: Because one low-cost aquatic state and one nightly terrestrial one are each indispensable, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Common House Gecko

modes.label: Vertical • Waiting • Nightly

waveform.description: Repeated short strikes from a held position through the night — many small events, none of them dominant.

entries.closingLine: Because returns come from repeated small captures at a held position, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Hoverfly

modes.label: Beating • Correcting • Darting

waveform.description: A fine continuous tremor with occasional violent departures.

entries.closingLine: Continuous heavy expenditure and millisecond reactions make this a single high-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Midwife Toad

modes.label: Loaded • Damp-bound • Slow

waveform.description: A long steady loaded line ending in one short release.

entries.closingLine: Few eggs, long investment and very high survival per egg make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Myna

modes.label: Locating an occupied nest hole • Evicting the residents and destroying eggs or chicks • Holding the cavity and breeding in it

waveform.description: A working rhythm punctuated by regular deep events, because ordinary foraging is broken by decisive takeovers.

entries.closingLine: Since takeovers and foraging recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Pill Woodlouse

modes.label: Curling into a closed ball • Plates interlocking • Losing nothing from inside

waveform.description: A slow crawl interrupted by two flat troughs, because the response to trouble is to stop being an animal shape at all.

entries.closingLine: Since everything runs slowly in the damp dark, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Prawn

modes.label: Holding among weed and in rockpools with a shell that transmits light • Being visible only as thin lines and two dark eyes • Flicking the abdomen to shoot backwards when detected

waveform.description: Quiet movement interrupted by extremely sharp escape events, because the animal drifts and grooms until something triggers the tail flick.

entries.closingLine: Since escape responses recur in fractions of a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Quail

modes.label: Breeding in one crop and moving on as it is cut • Crossing the Sahara twice a year • Following green cereal northward across a season

waveform.description: A restless irregular pattern that never settles at one level, because the bird keeps relocating rather than holding a place.

entries.closingLine: Since breeding attempts shift within a season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Roach

modes.label: Shoaling in open water and among weed • Growing deeper-bodied where predators are abundant • Becoming too tall for a pike's gape to close on

waveform.description: A regular unremarkable rhythm without extremes, because a shoaling fish's day is a continuous even routine.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding and shoaling are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Rose

modes.label: Larvae feeding on Aristolochia vines and sequestering aristolochic acids that make the adult genuinely unpalatable • A slow deliberate flight and a conspicuous red body advertising that fact clearly • Several unrelated butterflies converging on the same appearance, so the model bears the cost of the education while the mimics do not

waveform.description: A slow unhurried rhythm with little variation, because a protected butterfly has no reason to fly evasively.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs generationally, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Rough Woodlouse

modes.label: Walking fast and turning often while the air is dry • Slowing and turning less as soon as the air becomes humid • Accumulating in damp places without ever steering towards them

waveform.description: A fast agitated start settling into a slow steady line, because activity falls as the animal reaches humid air.

entries.closingLine: Because the response is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Sole

modes.label: Lying buried in soft sediment through the day • Emerging after dark and pressing the blind side of the head to the bottom • Locating buried worms with dense sensory papillae and taking them without seeing anything

waveform.description: Long buried stretches alternating with a raised active period, because the animal is either in the sediment or working over it.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding actions repeat through the night, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common stingray

modes.label: A serrated spine mounted on the upper surface of the tail, pointing backwards • Backward-facing barbs along both edges so the spine enters cleanly and resists being pulled out • A venom-bearing sheath rupturing on entry and delivering its contents into the wound

waveform.description: A flat buried line with rare sharp defensive events, because the animal lies still and strikes only when trodden on.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters are rare, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Sun Skink

modes.label: Retaining developing embryos inside the body for weeks • Supplying them through a placental connection rather than a yolk alone • Giving birth to fully formed young that can run immediately

waveform.description: A very slow even line with a single modest rise, because the cycle is annual and nothing about it is abrupt.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Wall Lizard

modes.label: Basking on stone until warm enough to move • Foraging across vertical rock and wall faces • Shifting diet to whatever the site actually supplies

waveform.description: A brisk repeating pattern of similar events, because the animal alternates basking and activity through the day.

entries.closingLine: Since foraging bouts recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Wanderer

modes.label: A male in plain bluish white with black veining, flying fast and erratically, unprotected and behaving accordingly
A female patterned in pale blue and black closely resembling the distasteful Parantica tigers she flies among, moving slowly and openly like them

waveform.description: A fast erratic rhythm giving way to a slow steady one, because the two sexes fly in entirely different ways.

entries.closingLine: This is sex-limited Batesian mimicry, and the two sexes therefore run genuinely different defensive systems in the same species, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Common Wolf Snake

modes.label: A pattern of pale bands on a dark body closely resembling that of the kraits it shares its range with • No venom of consequence and no capacity to back the warning up • Predators and people treating it as dangerous on the strength of the pattern alone

waveform.description: A quiet nocturnal line with a broad gentle rise, because the animal moves steadily through the night without bursts.

entries.closingLine: Because activity is nightly, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Wombat

modes.label: Burrowed • Slow • Retained

waveform.description: A very flat low line with almost no variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, retentive and built around a place rather than a behaviour.

entries.name: Corkwing Wrasse
entries.archetype: Males That Build, Males That Do Not

Wearing female colouring and shape • Slipping into another male's nest during spawning • Releasing sperm and leaving without building or guarding anything

waveform.description: Two clearly different levels alternating irregularly, because the two strategies coexist and neither replaces the other.

entries.closingLine: Since the two run side by side through the season, this is an adaptive system.

entries.name: Cotton Bud Moth

modes.label: Males locating females by following a plume of pheromone released in very small quantities • Synthetic pheromone released from dispensers across a whole field at far higher concentration • Males unable to follow any single plume because the entire air carries the signal, so mating rates collapse without anything being killed

waveform.description: A continuous searching rhythm, because the males are flying and sampling the air throughout the night.

entries.closingLine: Because the search is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Couch's Spadefoot

modes.label: Sealed • Dormant • Indefinite
Emerged • Calling • Racing

waveform.description: A buried flat line broken by one very narrow burst of everything.

entries.closingLine: Enormous dormancy punctuated by an explosive window makes this a bimodal system.

entries.name: Cow

modes.label: Cropping • Regurgitating • Chewing it again

waveform.description: An unvarying moderate rhythm with every cycle the same height, because the vat inside is never allowed to stop.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is one continuous conversion at a steady rate, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Coypu

modes.label: Mammary glands positioned along the upper sides of the body rather than on the belly • Young able to reach them while the mother floats with her back at the surface • Suckling continuing during swimming so the litter is never separated from water

waveform.description: A steady aquatic rhythm, because the animal moves and feeds continuously in and around water.

entries.closingLine: Because nursing recurs continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Cozumel Coati

modes.label: Nosing • Turning over • Remembering

waveform.description: A busy continuous searching rhythm across a small area of ground.

entries.closingLine: Continuous social searching over bounded ground makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Crane Fly

modes.label: Flying weakly on long trailing legs that catch on everything • Shedding a leg at a fracture point when it is grasped • Continuing to fly and mate with several legs missing

waveform.description: A loose irregular drift broken by occasional sharp events, because the flight is erratic and the shedding is sudden.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Crenulated Slant-faced Grasshopper

modes.label: Hovering in front of a flower after dark • Uncoiling a proboscis longer than the body into a deep corolla • Taking nectar no shorter-tongued insect can reach

waveform.description: A rapid fine oscillation maintained throughout, because hovering requires continuous wingbeats and the visits follow one another.

entries.closingLine: Since wingbeats and visits recur constantly, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Crested Fireback

modes.label: Bare blue facial skin with lappets that can be engorged with blood within seconds • Those wattles swelling and intensifying in colour during display and deflating afterwards • Colour and size depending directly on circulation and condition rather than on a fixed structure

entries.closingLine: Because displays are seasonal, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Crested Gecko

waveform.description: A steady line interrupted once, after which it settles at a different level, because the loss is permanent rather than temporary.

entries.closingLine: Since climbing and foraging recur nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Crimson Sunbird

modes.label: Landing on a stem beside a flower rather than hovering in front of it • Inserting a decurved bill and tubular tongue into the corolla • Drawing nectar up capillary grooves while the body is supported

waveform.description: A rapid even rhythm sustained throughout, because visits follow one another continuously through the day.

entries.closingLine: Since visits recur constantly, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Crystal Red Shrimp

entries.closingLine: Since grazing is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Cuban Solenodon

waveform.description: A modest repeating rhythm close to the baseline — steady nocturnal rooting rather than any decisive event.

entries.closingLine: Since nest entries recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Cuckoo Wrasse

waveform.description: Ordinary activity alternating with a long flat depressed stretch, because the animal genuinely alternates between two physiological states.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two physiologies, making this a bimodal system.

entries.name: Cyclodes Moth

modes.label: A proboscis stiffened and armed at the tip with barbs and cutting ridges rather than built only for sucking • That tip worked through the intact skin of a ripening fruit by twisting and pressing • Juice drawn out from inside a fruit that no ordinary nectar-feeding moth could open at all

waveform.description: A slow nocturnal build and decline, because the moth works at a single fruit for a long period.

entries.closingLine: Because the feeding is nightly, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Daddy Long-Legs Spider

modes.label: Hanging inverted in a loose tangle • Entering a resident spider's web and vibrating the silk • Killing from beyond reach with very long legs

waveform.description: A flat line disturbed by a short accelerating flutter before one sharp spike, because the deception builds before the strike.

entries.closingLine: Since hunting recurs nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Dall Sheep

modes.label: Growing horn continuously in summer and almost not at all in winter • Leaving a visible constriction at each winter • Carrying a readable record of age and of every hard year on the head

waveform.description: A regular annual oscillation of diminishing amplitude, because growth repeats each year and slows as the animal ages.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Damsel Bug

modes.label: Front legs thickened and held folded, used to seize rather than to walk • A dense pad of fine adhesive hairs on the underside of the tibia gripping the prey's surface directly • The captured insect held by adhesion rather than by force while the beak is inserted

waveform.description: A steady searching rhythm with brief captures, because the bug moves continuously and seizes what it meets.

entries.closingLine: Because captures recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Damselfly

modes.label: Fluttering between stems • Hanging in the air • Picking prey off a leaf

waveform.description: A light continuous hovering wave with no sharp attack in it, because the flight is a hold rather than a chase.

entries.closingLine: Because the flying and gleaning run continuously through warm daylight, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Danube River Snail

modes.label: Retaining developing embryos in a brood pouch for months • Releasing fully formed shelled young a few millimetres across • Producing few offspring, each of them already viable

waveform.description: A long low even line with a single small rise, because a slow-moving animal releasing a few young a year has almost no variation in its year.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Dark Fishing Spider

modes.label: Resting at the edge with front legs touching the water film • Reading the ripples that a struggling insect makes • Running across the surface to reach it and diving beneath when threatened

waveform.description: A still line broken by a short build of small disturbances leading to a sharp event, because the ripples arrive before the run.

entries.closingLine: Since ripple events recur through the night, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Dark-eyed Junco

modes.label: A population establishing on a coastal campus where winters are mild and irrigation keeps food available • Selection there favouring a longer breeding season, more parental effort and less white in the tail • Measurable change in those traits within decades rather than over evolutionary time

waveform.description: A steady rhythm with a persistent drift in one direction, because the change accumulates while daily life continues.

entries.closingLine: Because the change accumulates over generations, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Darwin's Fox

modes.label: Omnivorous • Understorey • Daily

waveform.description: A steady working rhythm — small foraging bouts repeated through the day and into the night.

entries.closingLine: Because foraging runs as a steady daily round rather than in bursts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Desert Cottontail

modes.label: Fermenting plant material in a large caecum where bacteria break down cellulose • Passing soft nutrient-rich caecotrophs and re-ingesting them directly • Digesting those a second time in the stomach and small intestine where the released nutrients can be absorbed

waveform.description: A regular alternating rhythm, because the animal cycles between feeding and re-ingestion through the day and night.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Devil's Coach Horse Beetle

modes.label: The abdomen curved up over the back in a posture that reads immediately as a scorpion
Paired glands at the tip of that raised abdomen releasing a foul-smelling secretion into the air and onto anything close

waveform.description: A quiet line with paired sharp episodes, because the display and the discharge happen together and briefly.

entries.closingLine: The beetle is a fast ground predator of other invertebrates, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Dibbler

modes.label: Probing • Small-prey • Nightly

waveform.description: A fine dense rhythm of small captures across the night, falling away before dawn.

entries.closingLine: Because returns come from many small captures repeated nightly, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Differential Grasshopper

modes.label: Chewing through the season • Laying pods in soil • Surviving as numbers

waveform.description: A steady chewing rhythm of even peaks, because the animal itself does one thing all season regardless of how many of it there are.

entries.closingLine: Because the individual chews steadily through a season at one unvarying tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Canary

modes.label: Singing through the breeding season • Growing the brain regions that produce it • Shedding them again after

waveform.description: A rising and falling rhythm whose peaks grow through the middle and subside, because the capacity itself expands and contracts across the year.

entries.closingLine: Since singing and feeding run together through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Dog

modes.label: Watching the face • Following the point • Checking back

waveform.description: An irregular attentive ripple whose peaks do not repeat evenly, because the rhythm belongs to the household rather than to the animal.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is a continuous, cheap and unbroken reading of another species' attention, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Donkey

modes.label: Walking under load • Stopping to assess • Refusing to bolt

waveform.description: A long shallow line with two brief flat holds in it, because the only interruption this animal offers is stopping.

entries.closingLine: Since every process is slow, economical and built for a long horizon, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Duck

modes.label: Barbules along each feather barb carrying hooks that interlock with the barbs beside them • The bird drawing each feather through the bill to re-zip separated barbs and spread oil from the preen gland • The plumage forming a continuous surface that water cannot pass through, with dry insulating down beneath

waveform.description: A steady even rhythm of preening and paddling, because maintenance is continuous rather than occasional.

entries.closingLine: Because preening is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Goat

modes.label: Reaching • Mouthing • Moving on

waveform.description: A restless uneven flutter where no two peaks match, because the animal never works the same item twice in a row.

entries.closingLine: Because the sampling is continuous and repeated all day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Goose

modes.label: Gripping grass between serrated bill edges and tearing with a head movement • Passing it through a short gut very quickly • Feeding for most of the daylight hours to compensate

waveform.description: A rapid unvarying rhythm sustained across the whole span, because grazing continues with almost no pause through the day.

entries.closingLine: Since bites recur every few seconds, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Horse

modes.label: Grazing most of the day • Fermenting behind the small intestine • Dozing on locked legs

waveform.description: An almost unvarying rhythm with no peaks or gaps, because the animal is designed never to stop taking food in.

entries.closingLine: Since intake and fermentation run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Pig

modes.label: Driving the snout disc into ground • Reading what is turned up • Wallowing to shed heat

waveform.description: A busy rooting rhythm with one flat trough dropped into the middle, because the day is built around hours spent lying in mud.

entries.closingLine: Since rooting runs through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Pigeon

modes.label: Reading the sun's position against an internal clock • Sensing magnetic field and low-frequency sound • Following remembered landmarks near home

waveform.description: A steady repeating pattern of moderate depth, because navigation is a continuous correcting process rather than a series of decisions.

entries.closingLine: Since orientation is corrected continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Rabbit

modes.label: Rotating each ear independently • Scanning almost the full circle by eye at the same time • Shedding heat through the same ear surface

waveform.description: Constant small movements with one much larger excursion, because scanning never stops and a genuine alarm is a different order of event.

entries.closingLine: Since scanning runs continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Sheep

modes.label: Grazing head-down • Watching sideways • Moving as one

waveform.description: A smooth low-amplitude wave with no sharp edges anywhere, because the alertness is continuous rather than episodic.

entries.closingLine: Because the watching and the feeding happen simultaneously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Downy Woodpecker

modes.label: Working thin stems • Drumming a resonant branch • Listening for the reply

waveform.description: Tight bursts of identical strokes separated by flat gaps, because a drum roll is a discrete message rather than a continuous rhythm.

entries.closingLine: Because that day is steady and repeated, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Drain Fly

modes.label: Developing as larvae inside the gelatinous biofilm on the inside of drains • Breathing through a siphon that reaches the surface of that film • Grazing the bacteria and organic matter the film is made of

waveform.description: A rapid shallow rhythm with no larger structure, because the whole life cycle turns over in weeks and nothing about it varies.

entries.closingLine: Since generations turn over in weeks, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Dumbo Octopus

modes.label: Flapping two ear-like fins • Hovering above the mud • Swallowing prey entire

waveform.description: A gentle continuous swell with no floor and no peak, because there is nothing in this environment to react to.

entries.closingLine: Because every process is slow, continuous and shaped by an environment that never changes, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Dusky Lory

modes.label: Flocks of hundreds and occasionally thousands moving together between flowering trees • The whole group arriving, stripping a tree of blossom and leaving together rather than dispersing • Individuals gaining nothing by staying behind because a stripped tree offers nothing and the next is found collectively

waveform.description: A repeating pattern of mass arrivals and departures, because the flock moves as a unit between concentrated resources.

entries.closingLine: Because arrivals and departures recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Earwig

modes.label: Laying a clutch in a chamber under cover • Turning and licking each egg repeatedly through weeks of incubation • Guarding the young through their first instar

waveform.description: A long steady low line with a single small rise, because the work is continuous, unspectacular and sustained over weeks.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs once a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: East African Oryx

modes.label: Storing heat by day • Grazing • Dumping it at night

waveform.description: A slow rise across the day and a slow fall overnight.

entries.closingLine: Conservative and reserve-based, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Eastern Bettong

modes.label: Nightly • Digging • Housekeeping

waveform.description: A busy, evenly distributed night of digging and carrying, with no dominant event and a clean drop at dawn.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole night is spent on steady digging and upkeep rather than on reserves or bursts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Eastern boxelder bug

modes.label: Feeding on seed • Scattered across the tree • Breeding through summer
Packed into a wall cavity • Reproduction shut down • Months without feeding

waveform.description: A busy feeding rhythm falling away to a long flat shelf, because the winter state has no activity in it at all.

entries.closingLine: Because a dispersed feeding season and a hormonally distinct aggregated winter are both necessary and neither is a version of the other, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Eastern Chipmunk

modes.label: Filling pouches • Carrying • Stacking one chamber
Torpid • Cooled to the burrow • Waking to eat

waveform.description: A working rhythm that falls to a deep floor and then ticks upward at intervals, because the animal keeps waking inside its own dormancy.

entries.closingLine: Because a season of accumulation and a season of metered drawdown are each indispensable to the other, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Eastern Collared Lizard

modes.label: Basking • Perched • Watching
Sprinting • Bipedal • Brief

waveform.description: A long warming watch with one short violent sprint raised out of it.

entries.name: Eastern Cottontail

modes.label: Frozen • Flattened • Unseen
Bolting • Turning • Homeward

entries.name: Eastern Gray Squirrel

waveform.description: A rapid repeating rhythm of identical small efforts, because the whole strategy is one action performed thousands of times.

entries.closingLine: Since the caching and recovery run continuously at one tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Eastern Lubber Grasshopper

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Eastern Phoebe

modes.label: Watching from a low exposed perch • Launching to take an insect in the air • Returning to the same perch and pumping the tail

entries.name: Eastern Rat Snake

modes.label: Wedging against bark • Gripping with belly scales • Reaching nests nothing else can
Balled underground with others • Metabolism at a fraction • Months without moving

waveform.description: A climbing season lifted out of a long flat winter floor, because the brumating months register nothing at all.

entries.closingLine: Since a climbing season and a physiologically suppressed winter are both obligatory and neither is a slowed version of the other, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Eastern Tiger Swallowtail

modes.label: Passing as a dropping • Swelling into eyespots • Everting a forked gland

waveform.description: A rising rhythm whose peaks climb through the trace, because each stage of the animal is larger and louder than the last.

entries.closingLine: Because the feeding and growing run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Eastern Yellowjacket

entries.name: Eclectus Parrot

entries.closingLine: Because the provisioning and the guarding proceed together through most of the year, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Edible-nest Swiftlet

modes.label: Producing thick salivary secretion from enlarged glands during the breeding season • Drawing it out in strands against a vertical cave wall • Letting it harden into a shelf of cemented saliva with nothing else in it

entries.closingLine: Since building continues over weeks, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Egyptian Goose

modes.label: Locating an occupied nest in a tree hole, a cliff ledge or another bird's stick nest • Driving out the residents by direct attack • Laying and raising a brood in the site without building anything

entries.name: Egyptian Grasshopper

modes.label: Sitting still on bark and stems with vertically striped eyes • Having the dark pseudopupil broken up by those stripes • Feeding on foliage at a slow deliberate pace without gathering into swarms

waveform.description: A very flat unvarying line with one small rise, because the animal moves slowly and almost nothing about it changes.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Emerald Cockroach Wasp
entries.archetype: Two Stings, the Second Into the Brain

modes.label: Searching • Small • Unarmoured
Stinging • Targeted • Steering

waveform.description: A searching line broken by two sharp precisely placed events.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: unremarkable searching and two surgically exact interventions.

entries.name: Epaulette Shark

modes.label: Walking • Tolerant • Shutting down

waveform.description: A low tolerant line with small slow variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, tolerant and built to persist through what cannot be escaped.

entries.name: Ethiopian Wolf

modes.label: Stalking • Seizing • Patrolling

waveform.description: Steady daily solitary foraging on a shared territory.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady daily solitary foraging inside a collectively defended patch of one very particular habitat.

entries.name: Eupterote Moth

entries.closingLine: Because outbreaks run seasonally, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Eurasian Blackcap

modes.label: Inheriting a compass bearing rather than a route • Departing on that bearing at a genetically set time • Producing offspring that take the parents' direction

waveform.description: A working rhythm broken twice a year by sustained departures, because migration is a seasonal event inside an otherwise steady life.

entries.closingLine: Since departures and song bouts recur seasonally within a steady life, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Eurasian Bullfinch

modes.label: Working along a branch stripping dormant buds • Taking hundreds a day through late winter • Switching to ash keys and seeds when those are available

waveform.description: A steady deliberate rhythm of similar small actions, because the bird works along a branch taking one bud after another.

entries.closingLine: Since bud-taking recurs constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Eurasian Collared Dove

modes.label: Settled • Prolific • Grain-fed

waveform.description: A steady unremarkable rhythm that simply never stops through most of the year.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, unspectacular and built on continuous reliable intake rather than on any decisive capability.

entries.name: Eurasian Magpie

modes.label: Investigating a reflection as though it were another bird • Noticing a mark on its own throat in the mirror • Scratching at the mark on its body rather than at the glass

waveform.description: An irregular exploratory pattern with varied excursions, because the animal is investigating rather than repeating a fixed routine.

entries.closingLine: Since investigative bouts recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Eurasian Reed Warbler

modes.label: Weaving a deep cup slung between standing reed stems • Inspecting the clutch and comparing eggs against each other • Ejecting an egg that does not match, and reacting to a cuckoo at the nest by mobbing

waveform.description: A working rhythm broken by sharp decisive events, because ordinary nest activity is punctuated by rejection episodes.

entries.closingLine: Since nest inspections recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Eurasian Sparrowhawk

modes.label: Females up to twice the mass of males • The male taking tits and finches, the female taking thrushes and pigeons • A pair working prey ranges that barely overlap

waveform.description: A watchful line broken by extremely brief full-depth strikes, because the bird waits concealed and attacks in a rush.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes recur through the day, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Eurasian Tree Sparrow
entries.archetype: A Colony in Other People's Holes

modes.label: Colonial • Cavity-bound • Flocked

waveform.description: A steady sociable rhythm sustained through the year.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, social and entirely dependent on structure it did not build.

entries.name: Eurasian Wolf

modes.label: Howling as a chorus at territorial boundaries • Being answered or not from kilometres away • Adjusting movement to avoid the neighbours that answered

waveform.description: A long quiet baseline interrupted by broad sustained events, because the chorus is infrequent but carries for a long time when it happens.

entries.closingLine: Since chorus events recur across weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: European Chub

modes.label: Taking anything from insects to fruit to small fish at the surface or the bed • Crushing it with paired pharyngeal teeth in the throat • Holding station in current behind cover

waveform.description: An irregular pattern of varied excursions, because the fish takes very different items and each one demands something different.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding events recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: European Field Cricket

entries.closingLine: Because the song cycles many times a second, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: European Flounder

modes.label: Lying on soft bottom in estuaries and coastal shallows • Regulating internal salt concentration actively as the water changes • Moving far upriver into fresh water and back to the sea to spawn

waveform.description: A slow steady rhythm following a tidal rather than a rapid cycle, because the animal's movements track the water.

entries.closingLine: Since movements follow the tide, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: European Garden Spider

modes.label: Taking down the damaged web at the end of its working period and swallowing the silk • Recovering most of the protein and amino acids from it within a few hours • Spinning a complete new orb from that recycled material before the next hunting period

waveform.description: A sharp construction burst followed by a long quiet watch, repeated once per cycle.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is daily, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: European Greenfinch

modes.label: Holding a hard seed in a groove in the palate • Applying jaw force from unusually large adductor muscles • Splitting the husk and extracting the kernel

waveform.description: A steady deliberate rhythm of similar efforts, because each seed takes comparable work and they are dealt with one at a time.

entries.closingLine: Since seeds are handled continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: European hornet

modes.label: One mated queen • Overwintering in a crevice • Starting the comb alone
Several hundred workers • Hunting past dusk • Defending a cavity nest

waveform.description: A flat floor swelling into one broad season and collapsing back, because the colony is assembled from nothing each year and does not survive the winter.

entries.name: European Lobster

entries.name: European Migratory Locust

entries.name: European Perch

modes.label: Holding station among reed stems and submerged branches • Carrying dark vertical bars that match the vegetation • Darting out when a small fish passes and returning to cover

waveform.description: Steady holding broken by sharp brief dashes, because the fish waits in cover and attacks in short bursts.

entries.closingLine: Since dashes recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: European Rabbit

modes.label: Out on the sward • Cropping fast • Ears turning
Underground • Passing it twice • Extracting the rest

waveform.description: A deep underground floor lifted twice into short raised blocks at either end of the day, because the exposed part is deliberately brief.

entries.closingLine: Because a brief exposed intake phase is paired with a long protected processing phase, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: European Rhinoceros Beetle

modes.label: Curled in decaying heartwood • Fermenting what it chews • Years before it surfaces

waveform.description: A near-flat line across the whole span, because a life measured in years of chewing has nothing in it that registers as an event.

entries.closingLine: Since the years that matter run at the pace of microbial digestion, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: European Spiny Lobster

modes.label: Occupying a particular cave or crevice on rocky ground • Foraging out and returning to the same shelter • Holding that site for years and remaining findable in it

waveform.description: A very steady line with small regular excursions, because a long-lived animal on a fixed site has a remarkably uniform life.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: European Starling

modes.label: Driving the closed bill into turf • Forcing it open against the soil • Looking down into the gap with forward-rotated eyes

entries.closingLine: Since probes repeat continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: European Stonechat

entries.closingLine: Because the timescale runs across decades, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Firebug

modes.label: Developing through nymphal stages under hormonal control • Requiring juvenile hormone to fall before the final moult to adult • Being stopped at that point by a compound in North American paper that mimics it

waveform.description: A slow line with periodic broad depressions, because moults are the structure of the animal's year.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Fischer's Lovebird
entries.archetype: A Domed Nest in a Hole

modes.label: Carrying strips of bark and grass to a tree cavity in the bill • Weaving a roofed nest with a side entrance inside it • Filling a cavity that other parrots would simply lay in

waveform.description: A quiet line rising into a sustained building period and subsiding, because the construction is days of work once a year.

entries.closingLine: Since nest building is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Flamed Tigersnail

modes.label: Rasping lichen, fungi and decaying leaves from bark and litter • Gliding on a mucus trail • Working only while the air stays damp
Withdrawing into the shell • Sealing the aperture with a dried mucus epiphragm • Suspending metabolism until moisture returns

waveform.description: Active undulation alternating with long flat depressed stretches, because the animal genuinely alternates between working and being sealed shut.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, a sealed animal with suspended metabolism and no exchange with its surroundings is a different architecture rather than rest within one, which makes this a bimodal system with a low-frequency dormant state.

entries.name: Flat-nosed Pit Viper

modes.label: Selecting a perch on a low branch or a trail edge where prey passes • Holding the same coiled position for days or weeks without feeding • Returning to that identical site after each excursion rather than searching new ground

waveform.description: An almost completely flat line with one small break, because the snake holds position for weeks and strikes very occasionally.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Flathead Catfish

modes.label: Holding station in cover under logs, undercut banks and rock through the day • Hunting live fish at night by ambush rather than searching for carrion or scent trails • Taking only moving prey, so bait that works for every other catfish does not work for this one

waveform.description: A flat daytime line rising into a single nocturnal hunting period, because the animal is inactive by day.

entries.closingLine: Because hunting is nightly and prey is large, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Flathead grey mullet

modes.label: Taking mouthfuls of sediment, algae and detritus from the bottom rather than hunting anything • Grinding it in a thick muscular pyloric stomach that works like a bird's gizzard • Passing it through a gut several times the body length to extract nutrition from very poor material

waveform.description: A steady continuous rhythm of feeding passes, because the fish grazes the bottom without pause.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Flower Crab Spider

modes.label: Sitting motionless on a flower head with front legs held open • Secreting or withdrawing a yellow pigment over days to match white or yellow petals • Seizing bees and hoverflies far larger than itself

waveform.description: A long almost featureless line with a single brief disturbance, because the animal is motionless for days and the strike is the only event.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across a season, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Flower Wasp

modes.label: A female burrowing through soil in search of a scarab beetle larva • Stinging it where it lies to paralyse it permanently • Building a small cell around the grub in the soil and laying an egg on it there rather than moving it

waveform.description: A flat surface line with deliberate descents, because the wasp feeds above ground and works below it in episodes.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs seasonally, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Flowerhorn Cichlid

modes.label: Holding and patrolling a space • Displaying a fluid-filled forehead mass laterally at anything approaching • Settling contests by size rather than by fighting

waveform.description: A continuous pattern of sharp display events at a similar level, because the animal challenges repeatedly and nothing resolves permanently.

entries.closingLine: Since displays recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Forest Wagtail

modes.label: A tail swung from side to side in a horizontal arc rather than pumped up and down • That movement maintained almost continuously while the bird walks on the forest floor • Insects flushed from leaf litter by the disturbance and taken as they move

waveform.description: A regular unbroken lateral rhythm, because the movement continues without pause while the bird forages.

entries.closingLine: Because the movement is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Four-lined Whiptail Lizard

modes.label: Moving almost continuously through vegetation and litter rather than waiting on a perch • Flicking the tongue repeatedly to collect molecules and deliver them to the vomeronasal organ • Locating hidden and buried prey by chemical trace rather than by seeing it move

waveform.description: A fast unbroken high-frequency rhythm, because the animal is moving and sampling almost constantly.

entries.closingLine: Because the sampling is nearly continuous, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Fox Squirrel

modes.label: Handling each acorn and assessing it • Eating the ones that germinate quickly and will be worthless by winter • Burying the ones whose dormancy lets them keep

waveform.description: A rapid repeated rhythm of similar actions, because each nut is handled individually at a constant pace.

entries.closingLine: Since nuts are handled continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Foxface Rabbitfish

modes.label: A clean bright yellow body with a sharply marked black and white face, held while actively grazing in daylight
A mottled dark brown and blotchy pattern assumed within seconds at night or under threat, breaking the outline against reef structure

waveform.description: A bright active rhythm collapsing into a subdued flat one, because the fish changes state entirely between day and night.

entries.closingLine: Aquarists who see the change at lights-out routinely think the fish is sick, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Freshwater Angelfish

modes.label: A body compressed into a thin disc with greatly extended dorsal and anal fins • That shape allowing movement between vertical stems and roots that a deep-bodied fish cannot pass • Dark vertical bars continuing the lines of the surrounding stems so the outline disappears among them

waveform.description: A slow steady rhythm, because the fish hovers and moves deliberately rather than swimming quickly.

entries.closingLine: Because movement is continuous but unhurried, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Freshwater Crab

modes.label: Large yolk-rich eggs carried by the female rather than released into the water • The whole larval sequence completed inside the egg rather than in the plankton • Young hatching as miniature crabs able to walk and feed immediately, with no marine phase at all

waveform.description: A single slow annual swell, because the whole reproductive investment is carried and released once.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Freshwater crayfish

modes.label: A giant interneuron running the length of the nerve cord carrying a single impulse • That impulse firing the abdominal flexor muscles together in a few thousandths of a second • The tail snapping under the body and driving the animal backwards away from the stimulus

waveform.description: A jittery baseline punctuated by violent instantaneous spikes, because the response is all-or-nothing and extremely fast.

entries.closingLine: Because the response is near-instantaneous, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Fruit Fly

modes.label: Salivary gland cells replicating their DNA repeatedly without dividing, so each chromosome becomes a bundle of a thousand aligned copies • Those giant chromosomes showing a fixed pattern of dark and light bands, each band a reproducible landmark along the DNA • Deletions, inversions and duplications visible directly as missing or reversed bands under an ordinary microscope

waveform.description: A rapid regular cycle repeated without variation, because generations turn over in about ten days indefinitely.

entries.closingLine: Because generations turn over in days, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Galah

modes.label: Paired inside the flock • Preening each other • Returning to the same hollow

waveform.description: A lively even chatter of similar peaks, because the social contact is constant rather than occasional.

entries.closingLine: Because that contact is continuous through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Galápagos Sea Lion

modes.label: Hauling out on rock and sand directly on the equator • Holding flippers up to the air and lying in shade, surf or wet sand • Returning to cold upwelled water to shed heat when nothing else works

waveform.description: A steady moderate rhythm without extremes, because the animal alternates continuously between resting and cooling.

entries.closingLine: Since cooling behaviour recurs through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Galápagos Tortoise

modes.label: Massive • Slow-burning • Stored

waveform.description: An almost flat low line: a body that changes its output very little from day to day.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a strongly low-frequency system: heavy, economical and built for a time horizon measured in decades.

entries.name: Garden Warbler

modes.label: Laying down fat before departure • Becoming restless at night for a number of weeks that matches the journey • Stopping when the internal programme runs out rather than when the destination is reached

waveform.description: A quiet line rising into a sustained elevated period twice and returning, because migration is a long programmed state rather than an event.

entries.closingLine: Since the whole cycle runs once a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Gaur

modes.label: Massive • Ridged • Unhurried

waveform.description: A heavy low line with slow shallow movement.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, heavy and defended by scale rather than by behaviour.

entries.name: Geoffroy's Cat
entries.archetype: Small Enough to Live on Rodents

modes.label: Nocturnal • Solitary • Repetitive

waveform.description: A steady repeated hunting rhythm through the night.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: repeated small captures rather than rare large ones.

entries.name: Geometer Moth

modes.label: Gripping a stem with the rear prolegs only, since the middle pairs are absent • Holding the entire body out rigid at an angle with no support at the front • Maintaining that posture for hours with silk sometimes anchoring the head end

waveform.description: An almost entirely flat line, because the animal holds one position for hours at a time and moves rarely.

entries.closingLine: Because the posture is held for long periods, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: German yellowjacket

modes.label: Rasping • Pulping • Expanding

waveform.description: A season-long climb in activity that ends abruptly rather than tapering.

entries.closingLine: Continuous building and provisioning makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Ghost Ant

modes.label: Many queens distributed across many small nests rather than one queen in one place • New nests founded by a group simply walking away with a queen rather than by a mating flight • Disturbance or poisoning causing the colony to fragment further, so treatment multiplies the number of nests rather than removing them

waveform.description: A continuous busy rhythm with no dominant period, because many small nests operate independently and simultaneously.

entries.closingLine: Because the network operates continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Ghost Mantis

modes.label: Hanging motionless among dry foliage with an irregular leaf-shaped body • Swaying gently as though in a breeze • Striking anything that comes within reach of the forelegs

waveform.description: A long motionless line broken by isolated full-depth strikes, because the animal does nothing at all between very brief attacks.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes are rare and the cycle runs across months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant African Land Snail

modes.label: Growing a shell up to twenty centimetres long • Rasping calcium from render, mortar, bones and other snails' shells as well as plants • Requiring a supply of calcium that vegetation alone cannot provide

waveform.description: A slow steady line with small regular excursions, because a large snail feeds continuously at an unvarying pace.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Asian Mantis

modes.label: Rows of spines along the femur and tibia of each foreleg, offset so they interlock when the limb closes • The tibia snapping back against the femur so the prey is caught between two rows of opposed spines • The whole strike completed in a few hundredths of a second, before the prey can begin to respond

waveform.description: A long motionless line broken by extremely brief strikes, because the animal is still and then instantaneous.

entries.closingLine: Because the strike is measured in hundredths of a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Burrowing Mayfly

modes.label: Burrowed • Feeding • Waiting
Emerged • Swarming • Mouthless

waveform.description: A very long flat floor ending in one narrow burst.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a very long accumulation and a single unrepeatable expenditure.

entries.name: Giant freshwater prawn

modes.label: Staying small and fast • Sneaking matings under the dominant male • Growing quietly
Growing rapidly • Carrying orange claws • Waiting for the position above to open
Carrying long blue claws • Holding a territory • Guarding moulting females

waveform.description: A stepped profile that climbs and falls back, because a male moves up through discrete forms rather than growing smoothly.

entries.closingLine: The forms also turn over at different rates, a small male moulting and growing quickly where a blue-claw male holds one position for a season, which is why this is an adaptive system running three states rather than one rhythm.

entries.name: Giant Golden Orb-weaver

modes.label: Dragline silk spun from proteins that crystallise into stiff regions embedded in a flexible matrix • That combination giving high tensile strength together with the ability to stretch far before breaking • A web of it absorbing the full kinetic energy of a large flying insect without snapping or throwing the prey back out

waveform.description: A long building effort followed by a settled watch, because the web takes time to construct and then simply waits.

entries.closingLine: Because the web is rebuilt over days, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Gourami

modes.label: A chamber above the gills filled with thin bony plates folded into a maze and covered in respiratory tissue • Air gulped at the surface held in that chamber where the enormous folded surface absorbs oxygen • The fish surviving in stagnant water and rice paddies where dissolved oxygen is close to nothing

waveform.description: A steady repeating rhythm of surfacing, because the fish must return to the air at regular intervals.

entries.closingLine: Because surfacing recurs constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Honey Bee

modes.label: Foraging • Layered • Working
Shimmering • Rippling • Repelling

waveform.description: A steady colony rhythm breaking into a rapid travelling ripple.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady collective work and a fast, coordinated, whole-colony response.

entries.name: Giant Malabar Squirrel

modes.label: Leaping • Counterweighted • Aloft

waveform.description: A repeated leaping rhythm between levels.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: continuously active in three dimensions and confined to one layer.

entries.name: Giant Otter
entries.archetype: A Family That Hunts as One Animal

modes.label: Grouped • Loud • Coordinated

waveform.description: Dense continuous high-rate group activity.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: loud, continuous and collectively powered.

entries.name: Giant Redeye

modes.label: A palm leaf cut and rolled into a tube fastened with silk, occupied by a single large larva • The inside and the larva itself coated in a white waxy powder secreted by the caterpillar • That powder keeping the interior dry and non-adhesive so frass and moisture do not accumulate against the animal

waveform.description: A slow build and decline over the larval period, because the whole system runs once through development.

entries.closingLine: Because development runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Scoliid Wasp

modes.label: A larva developing on a single scarab grub and receiving no more than that one grub contains • Adult body size therefore determined by the mass of the host it was laid on • The species reaching enormous size because its hosts are the largest scarab larvae in the forest

waveform.description: A single seasonal cycle of search and development, because everything happens once per generation.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is generational, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Stonefly

modes.label: Flattened • Clinging • Oxygen-hungry

waveform.description: A very low steady line with almost no variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: still, clinging and entirely dependent on the condition of the water around it.

entries.name: Giant Weta

modes.label: Heavy • Flightless • Browsing

waveform.description: A very slow browsing rhythm with no urgency anywhere in it.

entries.closingLine: Slow heavy browsing makes this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Whip Scorpion

modes.label: Paired glands at the base of the abdomen producing a concentrated mixture of acetic and caprylic acid • A short movable turret at the rear that can be swivelled to point in any direction • The spray directed accurately at a specific attacker rather than released in all directions

waveform.description: A flat nocturnal line with isolated sharp discharges, because the animal walks quietly and fires only when attacked.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters are rare, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Glass Catfish

modes.label: Hanging at an angle in midwater in a tight shoal • Transmitting light through a body with no scales and almost no pigment • Producing flashes of colour as muscle fibres diffract the light passing through

waveform.description: An even unremarkable rhythm, because the animal hovers and adjusts continuously without abrupt events.

entries.closingLine: Since movement is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Goffin's Cockatoo

modes.label: Working at a problem with no species-typical solution • Producing a tool from whatever material is available • Making a different tool for each part of a task when one will not do

waveform.description: An irregular exploratory pattern with varied excursions, because the animal is solving rather than repeating.

entries.closingLine: Since problem-solving bouts recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Golden Jewel Beetle

modes.label: Rhythmic • Posture-led • Display

waveform.description: A gently undulating mid-level line showing repeated, moderate shifts in visibility and activity as the beetle alternates between stillness on bark and short feeding movements.

entries.closingLine: This produces a mid-frequency system built around rhythmic, posture-led use of metallic armor as a visibility filter rather than either pure stillness or explosive bursts.

entries.name: Golden Lancehead

modes.label: Arboreal • Waiting • Migration season

waveform.description: A long quiet baseline with occasional modest lifts — the snake feeds rarely, and only when birds are passing.

entries.closingLine: Because it feeds only when birds pass and otherwise spends almost nothing, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Golden Tortoise Beetle

modes.label: Reflecting gold from a fluid-filled multilayer cuticle • Draining the layers when disturbed • Turning red as the mirror collapses

waveform.description: Two stable levels with rapid transitions between them, because the colour is either mirrored or not and does not sit between.

entries.closingLine: Since the change occurs within minutes, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Goldfish

modes.label: Working the bottom • Sifting sediment • Learning where food appears
Under ice for months • No oxygen available • Converting lactate to alcohol

waveform.description: An active season lifted out of a long flat winter floor, because the cold state produces nothing that registers.

entries.closingLine: Since both are indispensable and neither is a slowed version of the other, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Goodfellow's Tree-kangaroo

modes.label: Climbing • Browsing • Balancing

waveform.description: A slow deliberate arboreal pace with no hopping rhythm in it.

entries.closingLine: Unhurried movement on low-value leaves makes this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Goose Barnacle

modes.label: Attaching by the front of the head and secreting cement • Combing plankton from the water with feathery legs • Travelling wherever the object it settled on goes

waveform.description: A rapid even rhythm sustained without variation, because the feeding legs sweep continuously whenever the animal is submerged.

entries.closingLine: Since the legs sweep many times a minute, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Grasshopper & Locust

modes.label: Living solitary, green or brown, avoiding others • Moving little and breeding locally • Being a grasshopper nobody notices
Turning yellow and black with enlarged flight muscle and a different brain chemistry • Actively seeking others rather than avoiding them • Marching as bands and flying as swarms across continents

waveform.description: Two clearly different levels with rapid transitions between them, because the change is a switch rather than a gradient.

entries.closingLine: Because the two states are switched by density and the animal can move between them, this runs as an adaptive system.

entries.name: Gray Angelfish

modes.label: A small black juvenile with bright yellow bars, holding a cleaning station and picking parasites from larger fish that come to it
A large grey adult feeding on sponges, tunicates and algae across the reef, ignored by and ignoring the fish it once cleaned

waveform.description: A rapid high-amplitude early rhythm flattening into a slow shallow one, because an interactive juvenile becomes a solitary adult.

entries.closingLine: That is not a refinement of the same strategy but a change of trophic architecture: from a mutualist whose living depends on other animals choosing to come, to a specialist grazer whose living depends on chemistry, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Gray Whale

modes.label: Rolling onto one side on shallow Arctic bottom • Sucking mouthfuls of sediment in and straining them through short coarse baleen • Leaving pits in the seafloor and plumes of mud behind

waveform.description: A slow steady line with broad regular dips, because each feeding dive is a prolonged event at an unhurried pace.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Gray Wolf

modes.label: Trotting • Approaching • Letting most of them go
Committing • Holding • Taking the risk

waveform.description: A long even travelling rhythm punctuated twice by narrow spikes, most of the trace being movement that leads to nothing.

entries.closingLine: Because a long economical assessment phase funds a rare and hazardous commitment, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Grayling

modes.label: Holding station low on clean gravel in fast water • Raising an outsized dorsal fin into the flow • Using it to brace, to turn and to display in the spawning season

waveform.description: A steady moderate rhythm without large events, because the fish holds position continuously and adjusts constantly.

entries.closingLine: Since station-holding adjustments are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Great Crested Grebe

modes.label: Head-shaking face to face • Diving for weed and rising breast to breast • Repeating the whole sequence through the season

waveform.description: Paired rises that build toward a central maximum and fall away, because the sequence escalates through stages and then subsides.

entries.closingLine: Since ceremonies recur through the season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Great Crow

modes.label: Adults feeding at withered plants to take up pyrrolizidine alkaloids they cannot synthesise • Storing those compounds in the body so that the butterfly is unpalatable to birds • Converting part of the same supply into the courtship pheromone released from extrusible hairpencils

waveform.description: A slow even drift, because the butterfly moves unhurriedly and accumulates its chemistry over time.

entries.closingLine: Because acquisition runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Great Eggfly

modes.label: A bacterium inherited through the egg that kills male embryos, leaving populations almost entirely female • A suppressor gene appearing that blocks the killing without removing the bacterium • That gene sweeping through the population within about ten generations as any male carrying it leaves enormous numbers of offspring

waveform.description: A long flat depressed line that rises sharply and then levels, because the recovery happened abruptly after a long suppression.

entries.closingLine: Because generations run over months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Great Green Bush-cricket

modes.label: A row of fine teeth on the underside of one forewing forming a file • A hardened scraper on the edge of the other wing drawn across those teeth as the wings close • Each tooth producing a click, and a thin membrane on the wing resonating to amplify the train of clicks into a continuous song

waveform.description: A very rapid regular oscillation, because each tooth strike produces one pulse and the rate is fixed by the mechanism.

entries.closingLine: Because the mechanism cycles thousands of times a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Great Mormon

modes.label: Wearing a tailed, red-bodied, white-patched pattern • Copying a distasteful Pachliopta swallowtail • Protected only where birds have learned that model
Wearing the plain dark tailless pattern shared with the males • Copying nothing • Relying on size, speed and forest shade

waveform.description: Two clearly separated stable levels joined by a single transition, because an individual is one form or the other with nothing between.

entries.closingLine: The two strategies also work on different timescales, one needing a season of predator learning and the other acting within a single encounter, which makes this a bimodal system.

entries.name: Great Plains Toad
