modes.label: Hardened keratinised tubercles on the heel of each hind foot working as blades • The animal shuffling backwards into loose soil rather than digging forwards with the hands • Descending until it is well below the dry surface layer and remaining there for months

waveform.description: A long buried flat line with one abrupt surge, because the animal spends most of the year underground and emerges in a burst.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Great Tit

modes.label: Approaching novel objects quickly or slowly depending on individual temperament • Passing that tendency to offspring • Being favoured or penalised depending on how hard the year is

waveform.description: A varied pattern whose excursions differ in depth from one to the next, because individuals differ in how strongly they respond.

entries.closingLine: Since exploratory behaviour recurs daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Great-tailed Grackle

modes.label: Occupying irrigated farmland, car parks, city squares and anywhere with water and waste • Nesting colonially in ornamental trees and roosting in thousands • Following irrigation and settlement north across a continent

waveform.description: A busy irregular pattern of varied excursions, because the animal is doing many different things across a day.

entries.closingLine: Since foraging and social interactions recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Greater Amberjack

modes.label: Cruising in open water above reefs and wrecks • Driving down a shoal until individuals tire • Turning on the ones that fall behind

waveform.description: A rapid sustained pattern of strong excursions with no rest between them, because the animal operates at high output continuously.

entries.closingLine: Since pursuit is continuous, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Greater Bee Fly

modes.label: A female hovering over the ground near solitary bee nest entrances rather than landing at them • Eggs coated in dust or sand picked up into an abdominal chamber to add weight • Those eggs flicked from the air towards or into the burrow entrance while the fly never touches the ground

waveform.description: A hovering rhythm with repeated darting deliveries, because the fly works over the ground making many short casts.

entries.closingLine: Because the season is short, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Greater Mouse-deer
entries.archetype: Drumming the Ground With the Hooves

modes.label: Frozen • Tiny • Understorey
Drumming • Rapid • Signalling

waveform.description: A still line broken by a rapid repeated drumming sequence.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: near-total stillness and a short percussive signal.

entries.name: Greater Rhea

modes.label: Guarding • Pooled • Watchful

waveform.description: A steady sustained rhythm: continuous guarding rather than intermittent effort.

entries.closingLine: That makes the rhea a mid-frequency system: steady, coordinated and organised around continuous protection of a shared investment.

entries.name: Greater Weever

modes.label: Lying buried in sand with only the eyes and the first dorsal fin exposed • Raising black venomous spines when disturbed • Injecting through grooved spines into whatever presses down on it

waveform.description: A long buried line broken by isolated sharp events, because nothing happens until contact and then everything does.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur through the season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Greek Tortoise

modes.label: Digging a nest and laying eggs in it • Having the temperature during a middle window of incubation determine whether each embryo develops as male or female • Producing clutches skewed by the weather that season

waveform.description: A very slow even line with a single small rise, because everything about this animal happens across months and years.

entries.closingLine: Since generations take decades, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Green Anole

modes.label: Shifting between green and brown over minutes • Responding to temperature, stress and social state • Not matching the surface it sits on

waveform.description: A slow smooth drift between two levels with no abrupt transitions, because the change is gradual and driven from inside.

entries.closingLine: Since shifts occur over minutes, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Green Chafer Beetle

modes.label: Adults feeding on the foliage of a very wide range of unrelated plant families rather than on any particular host • Mandibles and digestion general enough to handle whatever leaf is available • Populations therefore unaffected by the absence of any single plant, because something suitable is always present

waveform.description: A single nightly feeding period, because the adults are active after dark and rest through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Green June Beetle
entries.archetype: Two Years Spent Eating Rotted Matter Underground

modes.label: Living as a grub in decaying soil organic matter • Crawling on its back • Emerging briefly as an adult

waveform.description: A very long even stretch ending in a single brief peak, because years of buried feeding precede a short adult period.

entries.closingLine: Since a generation takes a year or more, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Green Peach Aphid

modes.label: Females producing live daughters without mating, each daughter genetically identical to the mother • Those daughters already containing their own developing embryos at the moment they are born • Three generations therefore present inside one animal, so the population grows faster than the generation time alone would allow

waveform.description: A rapid oscillation with a rising trend, because generations turn over quickly and the total keeps climbing.

entries.closingLine: Because generations turn over in days, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Green Peafowl

modes.label: A train of elongated upper tail coverts raised into a fan with rows of iridescent eyespots • The shorter tail feathers behind it vibrated rapidly so the whole train rattles and shimmers • The vibration producing infrasound below human hearing that the female can detect at a distance

waveform.description: A fast shivering oscillation, because the display is a sustained vibration rather than a static pose.

entries.closingLine: Because the vibration runs several times a second, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Green-blotched Moth

modes.label: Adults flying into orchards at night to pierce ripening fruit and leaving before dawn • Larvae developing not on the crop but on Menispermaceae vines in surrounding forest and scrub • The breeding population therefore sitting entirely outside the orchard, where no crop treatment reaches it

waveform.description: A single nightly incursion and withdrawal, because the adults arrive after dark and leave before morning.

entries.closingLine: Because generations run seasonally, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Green-cheeked Conure

modes.label: Roosting communally inside a tree cavity every night • Pressing together in contact with several other birds • Maintaining those relationships by allopreening through the day

waveform.description: Daytime activity alternating with a long quiet plateau, because the birds are either active as a group or packed together asleep.

entries.closingLine: Since social contact is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Green-winged Cicada

modes.label: A pair of ribbed membranes on the abdomen buckled inward by muscle and springing back elastically • Each buckle producing a sharp click, repeated hundreds of times a second • The largely hollow abdomen behind them acting as a resonating chamber that amplifies the result into a continuous shrill

waveform.description: An extremely rapid regular oscillation, because the mechanism cycles hundreds of times every second.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is hundreds per second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Green-winged Macaw
entries.archetype: Slow Life History Built on a Pair Bond

modes.label: Holding one mate for decades • Raising one or two chicks at long intervals • Depending on a cliff or hollow that cannot be built

waveform.description: A long flat line broken by rare narrow peaks, because reproduction is an occasional event against decades of adult life.

entries.closingLine: Since a generation takes decades, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Greenbottle Blow Fly

modes.label: Detecting the volatiles • Arriving within minutes • Larvae done in days

waveform.description: A fast repeating spike train with almost no floor, because everything about this animal is a race against something rotting.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole strategy is speed against a vanishing resource, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Greenland Shark

modes.label: Swimming at under a metre a second in near-freezing water • Growing about a centimetre a year • Not breeding until past a century old

waveform.description: A nearly flat line with almost no variation across its whole length, because nothing in this animal changes quickly enough to register.

entries.closingLine: Since a generation takes a century, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Grevy's Zebra

modes.label: Males holding large territories containing water • Females moving freely across them • Mating decided by where the water is rather than by herding

waveform.description: Long level stretches with occasional raised sections, because a territory is held continuously and contested only occasionally.

entries.closingLine: Since territories are held across seasons, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Grey Seal

modes.label: At sea • Diving • Loading
Ashore • Fasting • Spending

waveform.description: A steady loading rhythm followed by a long low spending plateau.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a long steady accumulation and a short total expenditure.

entries.name: Grey-crowned Babbler

modes.label: Retaining grown offspring in the group rather than dispersing them • Sharing nest building, feeding and defence across all members • Recruiting the same helpers into the next season

waveform.description: A long even line with a modest sustained rise, because the group's work is continuous and the breeding season is a raised phase rather than a spike.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle turns over annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Greylag Goose

modes.label: Rhythmic • Coordinated • Route-led

waveform.description: A steady mid-level waveform with gentle repeating undulations, showing ongoing coordinated activity without extreme peaks or lows.

entries.closingLine: This creates a mid-frequency system built on rhythmic, repeated group movement and communication: coordinated, route-led activity rather than rare bursts or deep reserve use, so Greylag Goose is classified as a SINGLE, MID-frequency pattern.

entries.name: Groundhogs

modes.label: Feeding almost continuously through summer • Converting grass and crops into fat • Digging and maintaining a burrow system alone
Sealed in a winter chamber below the frost line • Body temperature falling to a few degrees above freezing • Heart rate dropping to a handful of beats a minute

waveform.description: Active variation giving way to a long flat depressed line, because the animal genuinely alternates between two physiological states.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two physiologies, making it a bimodal system.

entries.name: Guinea Pig

modes.label: Grazing in a group • Calling constantly • Young running the first day

waveform.description: An even close-spaced rhythm with nothing sharp in it, the trace of an animal that never accelerates and never stops.

entries.closingLine: Because the grazing and the calling run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Guppy

modes.label: Carrying male colour patterns that vary with local predation • Maturing earlier and smaller where predators are abundant • Producing measurably different populations within a handful of generations

waveform.description: A rapid varied pattern whose excursions differ from one to the next, because individuals and populations differ continuously.

entries.closingLine: Since generations turn over in weeks, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Hackberry Emperor

modes.label: Ignoring flowers almost entirely • Feeding on sap runs, rotting fruit, dung, carrion and the sweat of animals including people • Extracting sodium and nitrogen that a nectar diet cannot supply

waveform.description: A busy repeated rhythm of similar events, because the butterfly moves constantly between scattered feeding sources.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding visits recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Hamadryas Baboon

modes.label: Rhythmic • Coordinated • Ordered

waveform.description: A steady mid-level oscillation showing ongoing, rhythmic adjustments that keep the troop coordinated without extreme spikes.

entries.closingLine: This produces a strongly mid-frequency system: continuous, rhythmic troop-ordering activity that keeps signals, rank and movement clear enough to prevent chaos.

entries.name: Harnessed Moth

modes.label: A pair of ridged structures on the thorax buckled rapidly to produce trains of ultrasonic clicks • Those clicks emitted in response to a bat's own calls, at the moment the bat is closing in • The returning echoes disrupted so the bat's final approach is misjudged and the attack is broken off

waveform.description: A very fast burst rhythm, because the clicks are produced in rapid trains during the seconds of an attack.

entries.closingLine: Because the clicks run at very high rates, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Harris's Hawk

modes.label: Stacked perching • Leapfrogging • Watching one another
Flushing • Relaying • Closing together

waveform.description: An even patrol rhythm that lifts into one long sustained block rather than a spike, because the chase is relayed and lasts.

entries.closingLine: Because a continuous coordinated formation funds a rare and disproportionately expensive pursuit, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Head Louse

modes.label: Each leg ending in a curved claw that closes against a thumb-like spur on the tibia • The gap between them matching the diameter of a human head hair almost exactly • The insect gripping individual shafts so firmly that combing, washing and scratching do not dislodge it

waveform.description: A steady unvarying rhythm, because the animal feeds and moves at short regular intervals without episodes.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding recurs every few hours, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Hecale Longwing

modes.label: Trap-lining the same flowers • Kneading pollen into a drop • Living for months

waveform.description: A slow even glide with no sharp movement, because this is a butterfly that never needs to hurry and lives long enough not to.

entries.closingLine: Since the circuit repeats at one unhurried daily tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Helmeted Curassow
entries.archetype: A Casque Above a Very Low Voice

modes.label: Walking • Booming • Rarely breeding

waveform.description: Slow, deep pulses spaced far apart across a quiet baseline.

entries.closingLine: Slow-moving, low-density and slow-breeding, it is a low-frequency system throughout.

entries.name: Hermann's Tortoise

modes.label: Thermal • Pacing • Shelter-led

waveform.description: A gently undulating low line showing small, regular rises and falls in activity as the tortoise follows sun and shelter without sharp bursts.

entries.closingLine: Because its whole system is built around slow, conservative, thermally gated movement instead of bursts or distinct alternative modes, Hermann's tortoise is a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Hermit Crab

modes.label: Crabs gathering around a newly available shell that is too large for any of them • Lining up by size from largest to smallest beside it • Every crab swapping simultaneously the moment the largest moves in, so one shell rehouses the whole line

waveform.description: A flat line broken by a sudden cluster of activity, because nothing happens until a shell appears and then everything does at once.

entries.closingLine: Because shells appear rarely, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Herring Gull
entries.archetype: A Red Spot That Releases Food

modes.label: Carrying a red spot on the lower mandible • Having it pecked by chicks that respond to the mark rather than the parent • Regurgitating food in response to the pecking

waveform.description: A rapid unvarying repetition, because begging and feeding are short exchanges repeated constantly through the day.

entries.closingLine: Since exchanges recur within seconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Hieroglyphic Cicada

modes.label: Males aggregating in the same trees and calling at the same time rather than spacing out • Overlapping calls merging into a continuous wall of sound with no clear origin • Any individual made harder to locate because the acoustic field cannot be resolved into sources

waveform.description: A dense continuous high-rate oscillation, because many overlapping sources merge into one unbroken sound.

entries.closingLine: Because the call cycles hundreds of times a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Himalayan Monal

modes.label: Working alpine slopes with a short heavy decurved bill • Digging through soil and snow for tubers, rhizomes and insects • Occupying ground above the treeline where surface food is scarce

waveform.description: A steady even line with modest occasional rises, because digging is patient continuous work rather than a series of events.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Hispaniolan Solenodon

modes.label: Nightly • Probing • Methodical

waveform.description: A persistent series of small probing efforts through the night, each one shallow, none of them a burst.

entries.closingLine: Because value is extracted by steady methodical probing across hours rather than by reserves or bursts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Honduran White Bat

modes.label: Small • Sheltered • Frugivorous

waveform.description: A long sheltered baseline with a few short feeding excursions — a life lived mostly inside something the animal made.

entries.closingLine: Because a very small energy budget is protected by built shelter rather than by activity, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Horned Nerite Snail

modes.label: Adults living and breeding in fresh water well upstream, laying egg capsules on rocks • Hatched larvae carried downstream and out to sea, where they develop in the plankton for weeks • Settled juveniles returning to the river mouth and then climbing upstream over months, sometimes in enormous aggregations

waveform.description: A long round-trip cycle, because the population moves down and then back up over the course of a year.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Hottentot Teal

modes.label: Rows of fine comb-like lamellae along the inside edges of the bill • Water drawn in at the tip and pumped out at the sides by the tongue • Small invertebrates, seeds and plankton retained on the lamellae while the water passes through

waveform.description: A rapid continuous small-amplitude rhythm, because the bill pumps steadily without pause while feeding.

entries.closingLine: Because pumping is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: House Centipede

modes.label: Running down prey • Throwing legs over it • Detaching a leg if grabbed

waveform.description: A dense violent oscillation with almost no floor, because this animal is either running or not operating.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole body plan is arranged around speed and reaction, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: House Cricket

modes.label: Rubbing wings • Calling all night • Slowing as it cools

waveform.description: A dense even pulse train whose spacing widens slightly toward the end, because the rate itself tracks the falling temperature.

entries.closingLine: Because the calling and feeding run continuously through the dark at a steady tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: House Crow

modes.label: Working human waste • Nesting in any fork • Riding vessels to new coasts

waveform.description: An opportunistic uneven rhythm where no two peaks match, because each is a different scrap being worked.

entries.closingLine: Since the scavenging runs continuously through daylight, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: House Finch

modes.label: Feeding on seeds, buds and fruit • Depositing dietary carotenoids into growing feathers at the moult • Wearing a colour that reports what was available

waveform.description: A working baseline with periodic deeper excursions, because feeding is continuous and the moult is an occasional heavy demand.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding and moult cycles repeat, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: House Fly

modes.label: Regurgitating fluid onto solid food • Dissolving it outside the body • Sponging the liquid up through channelled mouthparts

waveform.description: An extremely dense run of brief identical events, because the animal feeds and moves in very short repeated bouts all day.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding bouts recur constantly, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: House Sparrow

modes.label: Feeding on spilled grain • Nesting in a building cavity • Roosting as a flock

waveform.description: A busy sociable chatter of similar peaks, because the flock feeds and squabbles continuously through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because the feeding and social activity run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: House Wren

modes.label: Packing several cavities with sticks • Offering the set to a female to choose from • Denying the same holes to every other bird

waveform.description: A rapid unvarying sequence of identical efforts, because the bird repeats the same filling work across many sites.

entries.closingLine: Since building is repeated through the season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Household Casebearer Moth

modes.label: A flattened silk case built by the larva and covered in sand grains, dust, hair and fibre from wherever it lives • The larva living permanently inside it, extending the head and front legs to move and feeding on wool, hair and debris • Both ends left open so the animal can turn within the case and emerge from either, without ever leaving it

waveform.description: A very slow steady rhythm, because the animal moves and feeds gradually over months without episodes.

entries.closingLine: Because development runs across months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Hoverfly

modes.label: Wearing black and yellow bands resembling a wasp or bee • Being an unconvincing copy by any measurement anyone applies • Being avoided anyway by birds that will not risk finding out

waveform.description: A rapid fine oscillation without larger structure, because the animal hovers and darts continuously all day.

entries.closingLine: Since hovering and visits recur constantly, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Human

modes.label: Food heated before eating, breaking down starches and denaturing proteins outside the gut • More energy released per mouthful and far less chewing and digestion required • A shorter gut and a larger brain becoming affordable on the same total energy budget

waveform.description: A long slow accumulation and settling, because the change operates across generations rather than days.

entries.closingLine: Because the change runs across generations, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Humboldt Penguin

modes.label: Diving the cold band • Returning to the same burrow • Dumping heat through bare skin

waveform.description: A regular diving rhythm of similar efforts, because the bird works the same water on the same schedule every day it can.

entries.closingLine: Because the diving and returning repeat at one steady daily tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Huntsman Spider

modes.label: Waiting flat against a vertical surface • Running sideways on laterigrade legs • Seizing prey directly with no web involved

waveform.description: Long stillness broken by extremely brief maximal events, because the animal waits motionless and then moves at full speed without any build-up.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes happen in a fraction of a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Ili Pika

modes.label: Cutting • Curing • Short summer
Sheltered • Drawing down • Long winter

waveform.description: One short raised season and a long flat one — the shape of a year in which almost all the work happens in a few weeks.

entries.closingLine: Because neither state can be removed without the animal failing, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Imperial Moth

modes.label: A large larva resting stretched along a stem, brown and mottled, resembling a dead twig or a strip of bark
On disturbance the larva rears and contracts the front segments, expanding a pair of enormous eyespots and a row of white marks that read as a face with teeth

waveform.description: A long flat line broken by violent sudden episodes, because the display is instantaneous and everything else is stillness.

entries.closingLine: So it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Indian Pied Myna

modes.label: Hundreds of birds converging on the same trees at dusk from feeding areas across a wide radius • Birds that fed poorly following birds that fed well when the roost disperses at dawn • Information about where food is spreading through the roost without anything being deliberately communicated

waveform.description: A daily rhythm with one strong convergence, because the flock scatters through the day and gathers sharply at dusk.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is daily, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Indo-Pacific Horseshoe Crab

modes.label: Circulating amebocytes in copper-based blue blood • Having those cells clot instantly around bacterial endotoxin • Sealing an infection into a gel before it can spread through an open circulatory system

waveform.description: A very slow even line with a small disturbance, because a long-lived bottom-walking animal does almost nothing quickly.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Indo-Pacific Tarpon

modes.label: Gulping air at the surface • Passing it into a lung-like swim bladder • Holding position in water too poor for gills

waveform.description: Flat stretches interrupted by regular sharp rises, because the fish holds steady between deliberate trips to the surface.

entries.closingLine: Since surfacing recurs through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Indochinese Tiger
entries.archetype: An Intact Forest With Nothing In It

modes.label: Holding a huge territory • One large kill • Days at the carcass

waveform.description: Long quiet intervals punctuated by rare large kills.

entries.closingLine: Large infrequent kills and long quiet intervals make this a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Indonesian blue-tongued skink

modes.label: Moving slowly • Holding the bluff • Opening everything at once

waveform.description: A slow flat line with two small nicks in it, because the display is over before it registers as a change of state.

entries.closingLine: Because everything else about the animal is slow and continuous, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Io Moth

modes.label: Folded • Cryptic • Unfed
Snapped • Startling • Instant

waveform.description: A flat resting floor cut by three identical vertical flashes — a display with no build-up, no gradient and no follow-through.

entries.closingLine: Because a near-zero resting state is paired with an instantaneous full-commitment display, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Iris Lorikeet

modes.label: A total world range confined to Timor and Wetar and nothing beyond • Dependence on remnant eucalypt and monsoon forest that occurs only in parts of that island • No possibility of movement to any other population because none exists

waveform.description: A steady rhythm with a slow downward drift, because ordinary life continues while the total keeps declining.

entries.closingLine: Because the pressures run across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Isabella Tiger Moth

modes.label: An active larva feeding, growing and moulting through the warm months in the ordinary way
A larva under leaf litter with glycerol and related compounds flooding its tissues, ice forming outside the cells and the animal frozen solid for months at temperatures far below zero

waveform.description: An active varying rhythm flattening into an entirely level line, because the second state has no activity of any kind.

entries.closingLine: These are not degrees of the same state; one is a metabolising animal and the other is a frozen object with its chemistry suspended, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Jackson's Chameleon

modes.label: Shifting pigment cells and reflective crystal layers within seconds • Producing high-contrast display colours during rival encounters and courtship • Returning to muted greens when no other chameleon is present

waveform.description: A quiet baseline with repeated bright display episodes, because the colour changes when another animal appears.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Jambu Fruit Dove

modes.label: A wide flexible gape that swallows fruit whole rather than pecking pieces from it • Seeds passing through the gut intact and being voided in flight far from the parent tree • Fruits above the gape width taken by nothing at all, so which trees are dispersed depends on a measurement of the bird

waveform.description: A quiet even rhythm, because the bird moves slowly and feeds steadily through the canopy.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs seasonally, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Japanese Beetle

modes.label: Grubs feeding on grass roots for most of a year • Adults emerging and skeletonising leaves • Damaged foliage and feeding beetles drawing in still more

waveform.description: A long quiet line rising into one accelerating hump and falling away, because damage builds on itself within a single short adult season.

entries.closingLine: Since a generation takes a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Japanese Bush Warbler
entries.archetype: A Loud Song From a Bird That Stays Hidden

modes.label: Singing a long carrying whistle from dense cover • Holding territory by sound alone • Never showing itself

waveform.description: Long quiet intervals punctuated by tall narrow spikes, because a drawn-in breath precedes each sudden carrying whistle.

entries.closingLine: Since bouts of song repeat through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Japanese Quail

modes.label: Hatching precocial and feeding within a day • Reaching sexual maturity at about six weeks • Laying almost daily thereafter

waveform.description: A rapid unvarying sequence maintained throughout, because everything in this animal's life happens quickly and repeatedly.

entries.closingLine: Since laying and development recur within days, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Japanese Sea Nettle

modes.label: A tiny polyp attached to hard substrate on the seabed, budding slowly and persisting for years as a stable colony
Strobilation, in which each polyp stacks and releases dozens of juvenile medusae into the water within days, producing a bloom that appears suddenly along the coast

waveform.description: A completely flat benthic line that breaks into a rapid oscillating band, because the two stages are different systems rather than different levels.

entries.closingLine: The two stages are not versions of one another but separate architectures, benthic and attached against pelagic and drifting, connected by a threshold, so it operates as a phase-change system.

entries.name: Japanese Spider Crab

modes.label: Walking slowly across deep soft bottom • Reaching food without moving the body • Carrying a shell far too small to shelter the legs

waveform.description: A long even line with a few shallow rises, because the animal moves slowly and almost nothing about its routine varies.

entries.closingLine: Since moults are years apart, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Javan Myna

modes.label: Approaching the new • Working food courts • Roosting in thousands

waveform.description: A quick opportunistic rhythm with uneven peaks, because each one is a different situation being investigated.

entries.closingLine: Because the investigating and feeding run continuously through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Javan Pond Heron

modes.label: Walking the bund • Standing over shallow water • Striking often

waveform.description: A patient repeating rhythm of small dips, because the strikes are frequent and none of them is large.

entries.closingLine: Because the stalking and striking run together through every workable stage of the cycle, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Javan Rusa Deer

modes.label: A stag in rut thrashing its antlers through vegetation and gathering grass, vines and foliage into them • That material carried and displayed on the antlers during contests and courtship, making the rack appear substantially larger • Rivals and females assessing the whole loaded structure rather than the bone alone

waveform.description: A single seasonal rise and fall, because the whole display period is concentrated into the rut.

entries.closingLine: Because the rut is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Javanese Grasshopper

modes.label: Muscle in the hind femur contracting slowly against a locked joint rather than extending the leg • Elastic protein in a thickened band storing that energy while the joint is held closed • The catch released so the whole store discharges in a few thousandths of a second

waveform.description: A quiet baseline broken by extremely sharp discharges, because the jump is instantaneous and everything between is still.

entries.closingLine: Because the release takes milliseconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: John Dory

modes.label: Turning to face prey so only a thin edge is presented • Easing forward with fin movements alone • Shooting a protrusible jaw tube forward at the last moment

waveform.description: A slow steady approach that steepens into a single narrow spike, because the stalk is long and the strike is instantaneous.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: June Beetle

modes.label: Larvae living in soil for two to three years feeding on grass and crop roots • Damage appearing above ground as wilting and dieback with no visible cause • Adults emerging in a synchronised flush for a few weeks to feed on foliage and mate

waveform.description: A long low stretch broken by one sharp emergence, because almost the entire life is spent underground.

entries.closingLine: Because development runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Kenya Tree Coral

modes.label: Growing as a branched upright colony that continues to extend at the tips • Constricting at the base of a branch until it detaches and drifts away • That fragment settling on nearby substrate and establishing as a genetically identical new colony

waveform.description: A repeating cycle of growth and release, because branches build and drop on a continuing rhythm.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs over months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Killdeer

modes.label: Slipping off the nest before the predator sees it • Dragging a wing and calling loudly at a distance from the eggs • Recovering and flying once the pursuer has followed far enough

waveform.description: A calm line rising into a sustained shaped event and returning, because the display builds, holds and then ends deliberately.

entries.closingLine: Since displays recur through the season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Kirk's Dik-dik
entries.archetype: A Nose That Works as a Radiator

modes.label: Browsing • Waterless • Nose-cooled

waveform.description: A careful low browsing rhythm with small steady variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: small, careful and built entirely around not spending water.

entries.name: Knobbed Hornbill

modes.label: Large fruits swallowed whole that almost nothing else on the island can handle • Seeds held in the gut and regurgitated or voided intact after a long flight • Distances of several kilometres covered between feeding and roosting, so seeds arrive far outside the parent tree's shadow

waveform.description: A daily pattern of long commutes, because the bird travels between feeding and roosting sites twice a day.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is daily and seasonal, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Kodkod

modes.label: Threading • Climbing • Taking small

waveform.description: A quiet repeating search rhythm with many small attempts in it.

entries.closingLine: Continuous secretive searching through dense cover makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Koi

modes.label: Rooting through the bottom • Growing all summer • Taking food from the hand
Motionless near the bottom • Not feeding at all • Metabolism at a fraction

waveform.description: A summer of movement lifted out of a long flat winter floor, because the cold state registers almost nothing.

entries.closingLine: Since a warm growing season and a cold non-feeding suppression are both obligatory and chemically different, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Koran Angelfish

modes.label: Dark blue with concentric white and pale arcs • Tiny and confined to a crevice or a small territory • Unrecognisable as the adult species
Olive-brown with fine blue speckling and blue-edged fins • Large, ranging over a reef • Holding and defending a territory as a pair

waveform.description: One level held, a single transition, and a different level held afterwards, because the change happens once and never reverses.

entries.closingLine: The pattern shift is therefore a change of social identity as much as of appearance, and because it happens once and irreversibly it operates as a phase-change system.

entries.name: Kuhl’s pipistrelle bat

modes.label: Flying circuits around a lamp where insects have accumulated • Calling continuously and steepening the call rate as a target closes • Taking prey every few seconds in a concentration nothing natural supplies

waveform.description: A rapid pulse train that tightens abruptly at intervals, because the call rate accelerates into a buzz each time prey is closed on.

entries.closingLine: Since calls recur many times a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Labyrinth Funnel Weaver

modes.label: Waiting • Tunnelled • Hours
Dashing • Biting • Instant

waveform.description: Long flat waiting broken by two very narrow spikes — the dash is over in a fraction of a second.

entries.closingLine: Because it needs both the long wait and the instant response, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Lantern Bug

modes.label: Driving a stylet bundle through bark into the phloem • Taking sap under the tree's own pressure • Voiding the excess sugar as honeydew

waveform.description: An almost unvarying line across the whole span, because the insect feeds continuously from a source that does not fluctuate.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Lar Gibbon

modes.label: Hanging from one arm with a hook-shaped hand and a ball-and-socket wrist that lets the body rotate freely beneath it • Swinging forward under gravity and releasing at the top of the arc • Reaching the next branch with almost no muscular work because the body is falling rather than being pushed

waveform.description: A pure regular swing repeated without variation, because each arc is mechanically identical to the last.

entries.closingLine: Because the motion is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Large Flying Fox

modes.label: Feeding on fruit and nectar at one site then flying tens of kilometres to a distant roost • Carrying seeds and pollen in the gut and on the fur across that whole distance • Depositing them into forest patches no other animal connects

waveform.description: A strong nightly excursion repeated with a flat day between, because the whole system is one long flight out and back.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is nightly and colonial, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Leaf Insect

modes.label: Hatching red-brown and slender • Running actively in daylight like an ant • Climbing upward to reach foliage
Turning green after the first feed • Flattening into a leaf with veins, notches and blotches • Rocking gently and moving almost never

waveform.description: A rapid active opening that gives way to a long flat line and never returns, because the transition happens once and does not reverse.

entries.closingLine: Since the change happens once and is irreversible, it operates as a phase-change system.

entries.name: Leopard Cat

modes.label: A small wild cat drawn into early farming villages by the rodents that grain stores attract • Remains from Chinese Neolithic sites showing the species living commensally alongside people thousands of years ago • The relationship ending there, with no domestication, so the cats stayed wild while the same process elsewhere produced the domestic cat

waveform.description: A nocturnal cycle without any long-term change, because the animal's pattern has stayed the same throughout.

entries.closingLine: Because the pattern runs nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Leopard Lacewing

modes.label: Larvae feeding on passion vines whose tissues carry cyanogenic compounds • Those compounds sequestered rather than excreted and retained through pupation into the adult • Bright orange and black wings advertising the retained toxicity to anything that has tasted one before

waveform.description: A steady unhurried rhythm, because the butterfly flies slowly and openly rather than evading anything.

entries.closingLine: Because the accumulation runs across the life cycle, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Leopard Shark

modes.label: Hovering over soft sediment and applying suction to extract buried prey • Taking the exposed siphons of clams and the tails of innkeeper worms rather than the whole animal • Returning to the same flats as those parts regenerate

waveform.description: A steady repeated rhythm of feeding passes, because the shark works the same ground over and over.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is repeated, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Leopard slug

modes.label: Circling and following a partner's slime trail for hours • Lowering together on a single mucus thread • Exchanging sperm through entwined everted organs

waveform.description: A long slow approach rising to a single suspended peak and subsiding, because everything builds toward one prolonged event.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across a season, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Leopoldi Stingray

modes.label: Settling under sand • Breathing through the top • Trapping under the disc

waveform.description: An almost unbroken low line, the trace of an animal whose normal state is being indistinguishable from the riverbed.

entries.closingLine: Because everything is slow, benthic and continuous, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Lesser Adjutant Stork
entries.archetype: Limited by Trees, Not by Water

modes.label: Striding shallows • Taking what appears • Nesting very high

waveform.description: A slow deliberate wading rhythm with few sudden events.

entries.closingLine: Slow and deliberate, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Lesser Banded Hornet

modes.label: A guard detecting a threat near the nest and releasing alarm pheromone from the sting apparatus • That chemical settling on the intruder itself rather than dispersing generally • Every hornet arriving afterwards directing its attack at whatever carries the mark rather than searching for a threat

waveform.description: A busy baseline with an abrupt violent spike, because ordinary traffic continues until an alarm converts it instantly.

entries.closingLine: Because the response unfolds in seconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Lesser Grison

modes.label: Following • Low • Everywhere

waveform.description: An active mid-level rhythm with no long pauses.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: persistently active across every kind of ground rather than fast on any one.

entries.name: Lesser Sandeel

modes.label: Shoaling in open water over sandbanks by day • Driving headfirst into coarse sand with a pointed snout and elongated body • Spending nights and whole winter months buried in the sediment

waveform.description: Activity alternating with long flat depressed stretches, because the animal is either in open water or inside the seabed.

entries.closingLine: Since emergence recurs daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Lesser Whistling Duck

modes.label: Male and female indistinguishable in plumage, with no display difference between them • Both birds incubating in turn rather than the female alone • Both escorting and defending the ducklings for months after hatching

waveform.description: A steady alternating rhythm, because two birds exchange duties continuously rather than one carrying it.

entries.closingLine: Because the alternation is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Little Owl

modes.label: Watching from a low perch in open farmland at dusk and by day • Dropping onto the ground and then running after prey on long legs • Taking beetles, earthworms and insects as well as small mammals

waveform.description: A watchful rhythm broken by regular short drops, because the bird perches and then goes to the ground repeatedly.

entries.closingLine: Since hunting drops recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Little Wood-Satyr

modes.label: Resting with wings closed and small ringed eyespots along the outer margin • Having birds strike at those spots rather than at the body • Flying off with a notched wing and an intact thorax

waveform.description: A quiet line with small brief disturbances, because the animal flies weakly and the attacks it survives are minor events.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Long-legged Fly

modes.label: A visual system detecting the approach of a looming object in a few thousandths of a second • Take-off initiated before the image has been fully resolved, using a coarse early signal rather than a complete one • The fly airborne within about five milliseconds of the stimulus, faster than any deliberate response could be assembled

waveform.description: A jittery baseline with instantaneous vertical departures, because the escape is faster than anything else the animal does.

entries.closingLine: Because the response is measured in milliseconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Long-legged Spiny Lobster

modes.label: Sheltering by day in a crevice or cave used repeatedly rather than occupied once • Walking out at night on long slender legs to forage across distances a short-legged animal could not cover • Returning to the same shelter before dawn rather than sheltering wherever it ends up

waveform.description: A single broad nightly excursion with a flat day either side, because the whole pattern is one outward and return trip.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Long-spined porcupinefish

modes.label: Drifting slowly • Crushing shells • Swelling if seized

waveform.description: A slow low drift interrupted twice by short lifts, because the inflation is brief and cannot be held.

entries.closingLine: Because everything else runs slowly, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Long-spined sea urchin

modes.label: Grazing the rock • Sensing shadow • Swinging the spines toward it

waveform.description: A very shallow slow undulation, the trace of an animal whose fastest movement is a spine turning.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at the pace of scraping rock, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Long-tailed Macaque

modes.label: Working whatever the site offers • Copying what pays • Testing the boundary

waveform.description: An uneven opportunistic rhythm where no two peaks match, because each is a different opening being taken.

entries.closingLine: Because the foraging and copying run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Longhorn Cowfish

modes.label: Holding the trunk completely rigid inside a fused bony carapace • Sculling with fins alone in a hovering, precise way • Blowing jets of water into sand to uncover prey

waveform.description: A very regular low-amplitude pattern with no sharp features, because the animal moves slowly and never accelerates.

entries.closingLine: Since fin strokes recur continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Longspine Snipefish

modes.label: A long tubular snout with a tiny toothless mouth at the end • The fish hanging head-down over the bottom and drawing individual prey items in by suction • Small crustaceans taken one at a time from between sand grains and among invertebrates where a wide mouth cannot reach

waveform.description: A rapid repeating rhythm of small suctions, because the fish takes one tiny item at a time continuously.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Lowland Streaked Tenrec

modes.label: Digging • Buzzing • Regrouping

waveform.description: A fast pulse train running continuously under ordinary foraging.

entries.closingLine: Continuous foraging with continuous signalling makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Luzon Garden Spider

modes.label: A large female sitting at the hub of a web she built and maintains, feeding, growing and producing eggs
A male a small fraction of her mass, barely feeding, wandering in search of females and often not surviving the mating

waveform.description: A calm large-scale rhythm interrupted by small rapid episodes, because the two sexes operate at entirely different scales.

entries.closingLine: The asymmetry is not a curiosity of size but two entirely different solutions to what an individual of each sex should spend its life doing, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Lycaenid Butterfly

modes.label: Secreting sugar and amino acids from a gland on the abdomen • Attracting ants that feed on it and stay • Being defended by those ants against wasps and predators for the whole larval period

waveform.description: A long even line with a single modest rise, because the relationship runs continuously and quietly through the larval stage.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs once a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Macaroni Penguin

modes.label: Foraging • Oceanic • Distant
Colonial • Crowded • Reduced

waveform.description: An active foraging rhythm alternating with a crowded colonial phase.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long distant foraging and a crowded, deliberately reduced breeding phase.

entries.name: Malachite butterfly

modes.label: Working rotting fruit • Probing dung and carrion • Rarely visiting a flower

waveform.description: An unhurried gliding wave with long shallow arcs, because a butterfly working fallen fruit has nowhere it needs to be quickly.

entries.closingLine: Since that action repeats at one unhurried tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Malayan Box Turtle

modes.label: A hinge across the plastron allowing both lobes to be drawn up against the carapace • The shell closing completely, with no opening left at either end once the head and limbs are inside • A defence that is total against a predator and useless against a hand, so the animal simply shuts and is picked up

waveform.description: A very flat line with occasional closures, because the animal moves slowly and shuts when disturbed.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters are occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Malayan Porcupine

modes.label: A cluster of short hollow open-ended quills on the tail, distinct from the long solid defensive spines • Those tail quills vibrated rapidly to produce a loud dry rattle when the animal is threatened • The warning delivered first, with the animal turning, stamping and reversing into the threat only if the rattle does not work

waveform.description: A single nightly activity period, because the animal forages after dark and rests through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters are occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Malaysian field rat

modes.label: Populations in oil palm plantations rising wherever predators are absent, on a food supply that never stops • Barn owls provided with nest boxes establishing at high density in the same plantations • Each owl pair taking a sustained toll that holds the rat population below the level at which damage matters

waveform.description: A rising population line progressively pushed down, because the predator pressure builds while the food supply does not change.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs over seasons, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Malaysian Leaf Insect

modes.label: Eggs dropped to the forest floor with a hard sculptured shell that resembles a plant seed • A fleshy structure on the shell corresponding to the elaiosome of an ant-dispersed seed • Ants carrying the eggs into their nests, eating that structure and discarding the intact egg in the refuse chamber, where it develops underground and protected

waveform.description: A slow seasonal cycle, because eggs are dropped over months and develop underground over further months.

entries.closingLine: Because development runs over months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mallard

modes.label: Pumping water through the bill • Straining seeds and invertebrates on comb-like lamellae • Upending to reach the bottom in shallow water

waveform.description: A fine, rapid, low-amplitude oscillation with no large features, because the bill works at a fast steady rate the whole time.

entries.closingLine: Since the bill cycles many times a second, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Maned Sloth

modes.label: Selective • Fermenting • Sedentary

waveform.description: A nearly flat line — intake, movement and output all proceed at the same very low rate.

entries.closingLine: Because intake, processing and movement all run at the same very low rate, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mangrove Horseshoe Crab

modes.label: Accumulating tetrodotoxin and saxitoxin from bacteria and diet in mangrove sediment • Concentrating those toxins in the eggs and in some tissues • Producing a clutch that poisons anything eating it rather than one that is merely hidden

waveform.description: A slow shallow swell, because toxin accumulates and is committed to eggs over a long seasonal cycle.

entries.closingLine: Because reproduction is seasonal, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Marmalade Hoverfly

modes.label: Migrating • Visiting • Returning

waveform.description: A long seasonal swell of arrival, presence and departure.

entries.closingLine: Sustained long-range movement and constant flower work make this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Marsh Deer

modes.label: Wading • Webbed • Solitary

waveform.description: A slow deliberate wading rhythm through soft ground.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, deliberate movement made possible by the foot rather than by strength.

entries.name: Marsh Tit

modes.label: Holding one territory with the same mate for life • Knowing every cache site and cavity within it • Refusing to leave even in the hardest winter

waveform.description: A remarkably even line across the whole span, because the bird does the same thing in the same place all year.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: May Beetle

modes.label: Underground • Chewing roots • Counting out the years
Emerging together • Flying at dusk • Six weeks and done

waveform.description: A long dead-flat floor ending in one square block of activity, because the emergence is a plateau with vertical walls rather than a peak.

entries.closingLine: Because years of hidden low-cost accumulation are discharged into one brief synchronised flight, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Mealworm beetle

modes.label: Larvae chewing polystyrene and passing it into the gut • Gut bacteria depolymerising the long carbon chains rather than the insect itself digesting them • Part of the carbon leaving as carbon dioxide and part incorporated into the larva, with the rest excreted as altered fragments

waveform.description: A slow shallow progression, because the process is gradual and continuous rather than event-driven.

entries.closingLine: Because the process runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Medicinal Leech

modes.label: Attaching with a rear sucker and cutting a Y-shaped incision with three jaws • Secreting hirudin and anaesthetic into the wound • Taking several times its own weight and digesting it over months

waveform.description: A very long flat line broken by one broad event, because a single meal supports the animal for months afterwards.

entries.closingLine: Since feeds are months apart, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mediterranean House Gecko

modes.label: Holding the wall • Watching the light • Short dashes

waveform.description: A dead-level hold broken by brief identical upward flicks, because the animal alternates between gripping and one short dash.

entries.closingLine: Because that rhythm is continuous and cheap through the dark hours, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Mexican Paper Wasp

modes.label: Running an open-comb colony through the wet season • Foraging, building and rearing brood on a single comb • Holding rank through dominance interactions among the foundresses

Abandoning the nest entirely as the dry season begins • Flying to traditional aggregation sites, often at different elevations • Clustering there in large numbers of future queens until conditions return

waveform.description: Active colony life alternating with a long flat depressed stretch, because the wasps genuinely leave and stop being a colony.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two states, making this a bimodal system.

entries.name: Milk Snake

modes.label: Moving at night • Wearing a warning it cannot back • Constricting what it finds

waveform.description: A slow even nocturnal rhythm with small regular variation, because nothing this animal does is abrupt.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs slowly and nocturnally, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mint Moth

modes.label: Flying in sunshine • Spinning a mint leaf shut • Feeding inside it

waveform.description: A quick light flutter of small even peaks, because the animal is tiny and works in short sunlit bursts between rests.

entries.closingLine: Because the feeding and flying run at one quick, light, repeated tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Mirrorwing Flyingfish

modes.label: Hanging in the twilight zone • Sides reflecting the water • Belly lights matched to the surface

waveform.description: A quiet suspended drift with almost no variation, because an animal whose defence is not being seen does not move in ways that would give it away.

entries.closingLine: Since the hovering and watching run without interruption in a place that has no day or season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Mistle Thrush

modes.label: Claiming a single heavily fruiting holly, yew or mistletoe clump in autumn • Driving off every other bird that approaches it for months • Living off it into spring

waveform.description: A persistent pattern of similar strong events, because the bird is repeatedly driving off intruders throughout the season.

entries.closingLine: Since intrusions recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Monkfish

modes.label: Lying buried and motionless for long periods • Twitching a modified first dorsal ray as a lure • Opening the mouth so fast that water and prey are pulled in together

waveform.description: A long motionless line broken by two extremely brief full-depth events, because almost nothing happens and then everything does in milliseconds.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes are days apart, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Moon Jellyfish

modes.label: Carried • Pulsing • Contact-fed

waveform.description: A small, even, endlessly repeating pulse riding a flat baseline.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: it adds a small amount of work to a flow that is already doing most of the job.

entries.name: Moon Rat

modes.label: Nocturnal • Unspined • Pungent

waveform.description: A slow low nocturnal line with small steady variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, unhurried and defended by smell.

entries.name: Mosquito

modes.label: Rapid • Reactive • Repetitive

waveform.description: A dense sawtooth signature representing rapid repeated sampling and response.

entries.closingLine: That makes the mosquito a high-frequency system: reactive, agile and built around repeated micro-opportunities.

entries.name: Mourning Cloak

modes.label: Emerging in midsummer and feeding on tree sap and rotting fruit rather than nectar • Entering dormancy in a cavity before autumn • Reappearing in early spring, mating and dying after nearly a year on the wing

waveform.description: Long flat depressed stretches with two separated active periods, because the same individuals fly in spring and again in late summer.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mourning Dove

modes.label: Gathering seed • Making milk • Starting again

waveform.description: A gentle rolling wave of even amplitude, unhurried and without any sharp event in it.

entries.closingLine: Because that rhythm is continuous across a long season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Mud Dauber

modes.label: Collecting mud in pellets and shaping it into tubular cells on a sheltered surface • Hunting spiders, paralysing them with a sting that preserves rather than kills • Packing several into each cell with one egg and sealing it before starting the next

waveform.description: A regular alternation between building and provisioning trips, because the two activities cycle continuously.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs seasonally, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mule Deer

modes.label: Pushing off with all four legs together in a stiff-legged bound • Covering broken rock, brush and slope in a series of high arcs rather than a run • Changing direction completely on landing because each bound starts from a standstill

waveform.description: A regular series of identical arcs, because each bound is a repetition of exactly the same launch and landing.

entries.closingLine: Because escape events recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Multicolored Asian lady beetle

modes.label: Hunting colonies • Breeding fast • Bleeding when seized

waveform.description: A busy unbroken feeding rhythm, quick and even, with no pause long enough to read as rest.

entries.closingLine: Because the year of consequence is one continuous rhythm of finding, eating and breeding at speed, this operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Muscovy Duck

modes.label: Perching • Quiet • Self-sufficient

waveform.description: A low steady line: an unhurried bird that spends little and rests high.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: quiet, economical and organised around removing risk by choosing where to rest rather than by escaping.

entries.name: Mute Swan

modes.label: Floating • Upending • Holding the stretch

waveform.description: A slow wide swell with no sharp edges at all, the trace of a heavy body moving deliberately and continuously.

entries.closingLine: Because the feeding is continuous, unhurried and repeated for many hours a day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Neotropic Cormorant

modes.label: Shallow • Flocked • Repeating

waveform.description: A brisk repeating rhythm of short dives with brief surface intervals.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: frequent, mobile and worked in company rather than alone.

entries.name: New Caledonian Crow

modes.label: Selecting a twig or a Pandanus leaf • Working it into a hooked or barbed tool away from the food • Carrying the finished tool to the prey and keeping it afterwards

waveform.description: A structured build-up to a peak repeated at intervals, because each episode is a sequence of preparation steps ending in use.

entries.closingLine: Since tool episodes recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Niger Triggerfish

modes.label: Reversing into a crevice tail first when threatened • Raising the heavy first dorsal spine and locking it upright with a smaller second spine wedged behind its base • Becoming impossible to extract because the spine bears against the rock rather than against muscle

waveform.description: An active feeding rhythm with occasional sharp withdrawals, because the fish forages in the current and bolts for cover.

entries.closingLine: Because withdrawals recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Nile Tilapia

modes.label: Growing • Spacious • Large
Stunted • Crowded • Early

waveform.description: A growth rhythm alternating with a compressed low state.

entries.closingLine: That makes it an adaptive system: the strategy is set by the conditions rather than by the species.

entries.name: Northern Bobwhite

modes.label: A covey of a dozen or so birds settling on the ground together at dusk • Arranging themselves in a tight circle with tails inward and heads facing outward • Every direction covered by a watching bird while the bodies press together to conserve heat

waveform.description: A daily cycle converging to a settled low period, because the covey disperses to feed and reassembles at night.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is daily, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Northern Flicker

modes.label: Hopping on open ground • Driving the bill into soil • Withdrawing a loaded tongue

waveform.description: Long flat hops broken by deep single probes, because each strike drives the whole bill into the ground rather than flicking at the surface.

entries.closingLine: Since that action repeats steadily through daylight, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Northern Mockingbird

modes.label: Sampling • Repeating • Expanding

waveform.description: Groups of repeated phrases, each group a different shape from the one before.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic and continuous, where output is a steadily growing library delivered in repeated bursts.

entries.name: Northern Pig-tailed Macaque

modes.label: Grooming • Ranked • Coordinated

waveform.description: A steady social rhythm repeated through every day of the group's life.

entries.closingLine: That makes the macaque a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, repeated and coordination-led.

entries.name: Northern Pike

modes.label: Holding motionless among weed with fins barely moving • Curving the body into an S with the tail cocked • Straightening it in a fraction of a second to arrive at the prey

waveform.description: A motionless baseline broken by extremely narrow full-depth strikes, because nothing happens and then everything does at once.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes occur in a fraction of a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Northern Snakehead

modes.label: A suprabranchial chamber above the gills acting as a lung and requiring air from the surface • Surviving out of water for days while the skin and that chamber stay moist • Wriggling across wet ground between water bodies rather than being confined to one

waveform.description: A steady rhythm of surfacing and submerging, because the fish must return to the surface continuously to breathe.

entries.closingLine: Because surfacing is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Norway Lobster

modes.label: Leaving the burrow to forage when light at the seabed falls to a narrow band • Walking over mud taking worms and carrion • Returning before the light changes again
Remaining inside a deep mud burrow • Irrigating it with the pleopods • Neither feeding nor visible to anything above

waveform.description: Two clearly held levels alternating on a regular cycle, because the animal is either out or entirely inside with nothing between.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, out and in are two different states with different exposure, physiology and availability, making this a bimodal system.

entries.name: Oleander Hawk-moth

modes.label: Larvae feeding on oleander, whose tissues carry cardiac glycosides that stop a vertebrate heart • Those compounds tolerated rather than avoided, through target-site changes and rapid excretion • A food plant left almost untouched by other insects, available in quantity wherever it grows

waveform.description: A single seasonal cycle of growth and pupation, because the larva develops once through a generation.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is generational, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Olive Baboon

modes.label: Trying it • Being watched • Copied by the troop

waveform.description: A varied uneven rhythm in which the peaks differ from one another, because each is a different thing being tried.

entries.closingLine: Because testing and copying run continuously through every foraging day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Olive Ridley Sea Turtle

modes.label: Oceanic • Dispersed • Solitary
Massed • Simultaneous • Overwhelming

waveform.description: A long dispersed low line with one enormous concentrated event.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long dispersal and one overwhelming synchronised event.

entries.name: Oncilla

modes.label: Nightly • Repeated • Small-kill

waveform.description: Many modest peaks of similar height through the night — no single capture dominates the trace.

entries.closingLine: Because returns come from many repeated modest captures rather than from storage or a decisive kill, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Opossum

modes.label: Hissing and baring fifty teeth at a threat • Collapsing involuntarily into a rigid open-mouthed state if that fails • Remaining unresponsive for minutes to hours while producing a foul anal secretion

waveform.description: Ordinary activity rising into a sharp event and then dropping to a sustained flat depressed state, because the collapse is not a return to normal.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur through the night, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Orange Moth

modes.label: Carrying a coat of translucent gelatinous spines • Shedding them on contact • Leaving an attacker with jaws stuck together

waveform.description: A long even line broken by two brief raised sections, because the defence is passive almost all the time and only acts on contact.

entries.closingLine: Since a generation turns over across months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Orange-headed Thrush

modes.label: A bird working shaded forest floor by picking up leaves in the bill and flicking them aside • Invertebrates sheltering beneath that litter exposed by the movement rather than being searched for visually • Each flick revealing a small patch, so the forager processes the floor leaf by leaf rather than scanning it

waveform.description: A steady methodical rhythm, because the bird works the floor one flick at a time without pause.

entries.closingLine: Because the work is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Orange-striped Assassin Bug

modes.label: Creeping • Adhesive • Warned

waveform.description: A very slow low line with minimal variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, adhesive and protected by advertisement.

entries.name: Oriental Dwarf Kingfisher

modes.label: Perching low on a branch above shaded forest floor rather than above water • Watching leaf litter for spiders, mantises, geckos and small frogs • Dropping onto them directly, with no dive, no refraction to correct and no water involved

waveform.description: A long motionless watching line with abrupt drops, because the bird sits still and strikes without warning.

entries.closingLine: Because strikes are infrequent, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Oriental Fire-bellied Toad

modes.label: Mottled • Still • Switchable

waveform.description: A quiet cryptic line broken only where the underside comes up.

entries.closingLine: Small, cheap to run and long-lived for its size, this is a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Oriental Garden Lizard

modes.label: An ordinary brown or olive lizard basking, feeding and moving inconspicuously through vegetation
A breeding male with the head and throat flushed bright crimson, holding an elevated position and head-bobbing at rivals

waveform.description: A quiet even rhythm broken by tall display episodes, because the animal switches between concealment and advertisement.

entries.closingLine: Because the display runs seasonally against a continuous background, it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Oriental Latrine Fly

modes.label: Adults locating a body within minutes by volatile compounds released as decomposition begins • Laying eggs in a narrow window before other species dominate • Larvae developing at a rate set by temperature, so their stage gives an elapsed time

waveform.description: One sharp early surge followed by a long decline, because the fly dominates the first phase and then gives way.

entries.closingLine: Because generations are rapid, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Oriental Magpie-Robin
entries.archetype: A Song That Holds the Garden

modes.label: Singing • Perched • Territorial

waveform.description: A varied sustained vocal rhythm across the day's edges.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, sustained and carried entirely by signal.

entries.name: Oriental Pied Hornbill

modes.label: Provisioning • Enclosed • Sustained

waveform.description: A long series of identical delivery events at a steady interval.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, sustained and defined by continuous provisioning rather than by any burst of effort.

entries.name: Oriental White-eye

modes.label: Small parties moving through canopy and joined by drongos, minivets, babblers, woodpeckers and flycatchers • Each species foraging at a different height and in a different manner, so competition stays low while numbers stay high • Many more eyes watching for raptors, and insects flushed by one species taken by another

waveform.description: A continuous busy rhythm, because the flock moves and forages constantly through the canopy.

entries.closingLine: Because foraging is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Orinoco Mata Mata Turtle

modes.label: Sitting motionless on the bottom with a flattened fringed head that reads as leaf litter • Expanding the throat explosively when a fish comes within range • Drawing prey in on the inrush of water rather than by any pursuit

waveform.description: A flat line broken by two very sharp narrow spikes, because nothing happens at all until the strike, which is nearly instantaneous.

entries.closingLine: Because the capture is rare and the animal is otherwise still, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Ornate Spiny Lobster

modes.label: Growing on shallow reef and seagrass in the Torres Strait • Migrating hundreds of kilometres to spawning grounds in the Gulf of Papua • Spawning there and dying rather than returning

waveform.description: A steady line rising into broad sustained events, because the migration is a prolonged movement rather than a moment.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Ornate Spiny-tailed Lizard

modes.label: A diet of desert plants carrying far more potassium and sodium salts than the body can use • Nasal glands actively concentrating those salts and excreting them as crystals • Crusts of salt accumulating around the nostrils and being sneezed away, so water is not spent flushing them through the kidney

waveform.description: A single daily arc of emergence and retreat, because activity follows the sun and returns to the burrow.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Oscar Fish

modes.label: Moving gravel with the mouth • Clearing a flat surface • Guarding it as a pair

waveform.description: A deliberate working rhythm of even efforts, because moving substrate by the mouthful is repetitive rather than dramatic.

entries.closingLine: Since that operation runs at a steady tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Owlet Moth
