modes.label: A simple ear on each side of the thorax with very few sensory cells, tuned to ultrasound • A distant bat call producing steady firing that turns the moth away • A close call producing saturated firing that collapses the flight into a spiral or a drop

waveform.description: A quick irregular flight line broken by violent instantaneous collapses, because evasion is abrupt and total.

entries.closingLine: Because the response is near-instantaneous, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Pacific Black Duck

modes.label: Waiting through dry years without breeding • Responding to flooding within weeks • Raising broods while the water and its invertebrates last

waveform.description: A long flat stretch broken by one broad rise, because years can pass with nothing happening and then everything happens at once.

entries.closingLine: Since breeding events are years apart, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pacific Sea Nettle

modes.label: Slow rhythmic pulsing of the bell that moves the animal forward rather than chasing anything • Long tentacles and frilled oral arms trailing far behind, forming a wide curtain through the water • Anything that touches the curtain stung by nematocysts and passed forward to the mouth

waveform.description: A slow regular pulse repeated without variation, because propulsion and feeding are the same continuous rhythm.

entries.closingLine: Because the pulsing is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Paddyfield Warbler

modes.label: Climbing reed stems rather than perching on branches • Foraging up and down a vertical world • Singing from inside the stand

waveform.description: Rapid alternation between two levels, because the bird is continually working up and down the stems rather than settling.

entries.closingLine: Since foraging bouts repeat through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Pagoda Cup Coral

modes.label: Growing as broad horizontal plates rather than branches or mounds • Stacking successive plates in offset tiers as the colony expands • Presenting maximum surface to a dim overhead light while letting sediment slide off the sloping edges

waveform.description: A slow steady climb without oscillation, because the colony only accumulates and never cycles.

entries.closingLine: Because growth accumulates over years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Painted Turtle

modes.label: Hauled onto a log • Warming to working temperature • Feeding in the shallows
Under the ice • No oxygen at all • Dissolving its own shell to survive it

waveform.description: A working season lifted out of a long dead-flat floor, because the winter state produces no activity of any kind to register.

entries.closingLine: Because both are indispensable and neither is a quieter version of the other, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Pallas's Cat

modes.label: Dense • Still • Close-range

waveform.description: A long flat hold with one short, shallow commitment near the end — the cat's whole hunt is waiting, then a few metres.

entries.closingLine: Because this animal earns its living by holding still, keeping its own heat in and spending energy only at the last moment, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pantropical Jumping Spider

modes.label: Hind legs with flexor muscles but no extensor muscles at the crucial joints • Body fluid driven into the legs by rapid contraction of the abdomen, straightening them hydraulically • A jump many times the body length produced with no extensor muscle at all, and a silk dragline paid out as a safety line

waveform.description: A careful stalking baseline broken by instantaneous jumps, because the approach is slow and the leap is not.

entries.closingLine: Because the jump is measured in milliseconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Pantry Moth

modes.label: Hatching from eggs laid on or near stored food • Boring through plastic film, paper and thin card to reach it or to leave • Webbing the food together with silk as they feed

waveform.description: A rapid even rhythm sustained throughout, because generations follow one another continuously in a heated building.

entries.closingLine: Since generations turn over in weeks, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Paper Wasp

modes.label: Several females founding a nest together • Establishing rank through repeated dominance encounters • The top female laying while the others forage and build

waveform.description: A continual back-and-forth without settling, because rank is maintained through repeated interaction rather than fixed once.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Parasitic wasp

modes.label: Tapping and listening along a surface to detect a host concealed inside wood or plant tissue • Locating it by vibration, chemical trace and the response of the substrate • Drilling through with a hair-thin ovipositor and laying an egg directly on or in the hidden host

waveform.description: A long searching baseline with one deliberate committed episode, because location takes far longer than the act itself.

entries.closingLine: Because each act takes a long search, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Peacock Bass

modes.label: A large visual daytime predator introduced into a lake whose fish had never encountered one • Native species showing no avoidance because nothing in their history selected for it • Whole guilds of small fish removed within a few years, and the effects propagating upward to birds and outward to mosquito numbers

waveform.description: A normal rhythm collapsing into a flat depleted line, because the change is one-directional and does not recover.

entries.closingLine: Because the collapse runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Peacock Butterfly

modes.label: Sitting closed with wings that look like dead leaf • Snapping them open to present four large eyespots • Rubbing the wing bases together to produce an audible hiss

waveform.description: A flat concealed line broken by sharp discrete displays, because nothing happens until the animal is found and then everything does at once.

entries.closingLine: Since disturbances recur unpredictably through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Pearl Oysters

modes.label: Detecting material lodged between the mantle and the shell • Depositing successive layers of aragonite tablets and protein over it • Producing a smooth interior where an irritant would otherwise wound the mantle

waveform.description: An almost unvarying line across the span, because deposition is continuous and extremely slow.

entries.closingLine: Since deposition is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Pere David's Deer
entries.archetype: A Species Rebuilt From Eighteen Animals

modes.label: Wading • Splayed • Marsh-built
Recovered • Bottlenecked • Identical

waveform.description: A slow wading rhythm with a recovery rising from a very low floor.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a wetland-adapted animal and a population rebuilt through an extreme bottleneck.

entries.name: Periwinkle

modes.label: A horny plate on the foot that fits the shell aperture exactly • The animal withdrawing at low tide and pulling that plate closed behind it • A sealed chamber of seawater retained inside while the rock around it dries, heats and freezes

waveform.description: A tidal rhythm of activity and closure repeated twice a day without variation.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is tidal, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Persian Leopard

modes.label: Lying up • Watching • Approaching
Short rush • Grapple • Carry up

waveform.description: Long still watching cut by an attack that covers very little ground.

entries.closingLine: Long motionless watching paying for a very short rush makes this a bimodal system, low-frequency on the ledge and high-frequency at the end.

entries.name: Pheasant

modes.label: Tens of millions of birds reared in pens each year and released into the countryside before the shooting season • That release adding a very large seasonal mass of birds to the landscape at one time • Predator and scavenger populations, plant communities and invertebrates all responding to a food supply that appears and disappears on a calendar set by people

waveform.description: A sharp annual pulse and decline, because the population is created in a few weeks and consumed through the winter.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Philippine Bulbul

modes.label: A generalist frugivore taking fruit from a very wide range of trees rather than specialising on any • Occupying secondary growth, plantation edge and regenerating clearings as readily as closed forest • Depositing seeds of pioneer and forest trees into cleared ground, so the bird that benefits from disturbance also reverses it

waveform.description: A steady untroubled rhythm, because the bird moves and feeds continuously without strong seasonal pattern.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Philippine Tarsier

modes.label: Clinging • Turning • Waiting

waveform.description: A held motionless line broken twice by a launch and a landing.

entries.closingLine: Long motionless watching between occasional leaps makes this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pied Butcherbird

modes.label: Watching from a bare branch • Dropping on prey • Wedging it into a fork

waveform.description: Long flat watches broken by short identical drops, because the hunt is a wait followed by one committed fall.

entries.closingLine: Since watching and singing run together through daylight, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Pied Crow

modes.label: Building on pylons, poles and planted trees • Feeding along road verges • Spreading wherever both appear together

waveform.description: A regular baseline with evenly spaced peaks, because the bird works a landscape whose resources are arranged in a line.

entries.closingLine: Since foraging turns over daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Pied Cuckoo

modes.label: Eggs laid in babbler nests that closely match the hosts' own in colour and size • The cuckoo chick hatching earlier and growing faster but leaving the host chicks alive in the nest • Out-begging its nestmates with a louder call and a wider gape so it takes most of what arrives

waveform.description: A single seasonal rise and fall, because the whole parasitic episode runs once through a breeding cycle.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pied Fantail

modes.label: Moving restlessly through foliage with the tail fanned and swung • Startling insects into flight with the flash of black and white • Taking them in the air before they can settle again

waveform.description: A very rapid continuous pattern with no settled moments, because the bird is in constant motion the whole time it is awake.

entries.closingLine: Since the movement is continuous, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Pied Paddy Skimmer

modes.label: Broad opaque dark patches of pigment laid into otherwise transparent wing membrane • Those patches held out and displayed during territorial encounters over water • Rivals assessing the patches directly, so disputes over perching sites are settled by display rather than by collision

waveform.description: A busy repeating rhythm of patrols and encounters, because the insect holds a territory and meets rivals constantly.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Pink Fairy Armadillo

modes.label: Sand-swimming • Sealed • Nocturnal

waveform.description: A shallow steady rhythm below the baseline — digging is continuous and slow rather than intermittent.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal moves slowly through sand and rarely surfaces, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pink-necked Green Pigeon

modes.label: Fruit swallowed whole and passed into a heavily muscled gizzard containing grit • Seeds ground and crushed there rather than passed intact through the gut • The bird taking the nutrition in the seed itself, so it removes the seeds it consumes instead of dispersing them

waveform.description: A quiet even feeding rhythm, because the bird works steadily through fruiting canopy without episodes.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is steady, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pink-spotted Hawkmoth

modes.label: Resting head-up along a grass blade or stem • Carrying a long conical head and slanted face that continues the line of the stem • Moving slowly and turning to keep the narrow profile toward an observer

waveform.description: A very flat slow line with a single small disturbance, because the animal is motionless for long periods and moves deliberately.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Planthopper

modes.label: Glands on the abdomen of the nymph extruding long threads of white wax • Those threads held in a fan behind the insect, breaking its outline completely • The threads detaching in a predator's mouth or grip while the nymph jumps clear

waveform.description: A quiet feeding line with abrupt escapes, because the nymph sits still on a stem and jumps when disturbed.

entries.closingLine: Because the wax accumulates over days, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Plumbeous Ibis
entries.archetype: A Bill That Reads by Touch

modes.label: Probing soft ground and shallow water • Detecting prey by touch rather than sight • Closing on contact without seeing what was taken

waveform.description: A persistent even series of identical probes, because the bird works the substrate at a steady rhythm rather than in bursts.

entries.closingLine: Since probes repeat continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Plume Moth

modes.label: Divided • Rolled • T-shaped

waveform.description: A slow light line with very small variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: delicate, economical and defended by resemblance.

entries.name: Postman butterfly

modes.label: Wearing another species' pattern • Both being genuinely toxic • Sharing the cost of teaching

waveform.description: An unhurried even glide, matched to a relative rather than distinguished from it, because the biology genuinely is shared.

entries.closingLine: Since the flower circuit repeats daily across a long life, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Pot-bellied Seahorse

modes.label: The female depositing eggs into a sealed pouch on the male's abdomen • Pouch tissue growing a dense capillary bed around the embedded eggs and regulating salinity, oxygen and nutrients inside • The male carrying the brood for weeks and then expelling fully formed young by muscular contraction

waveform.description: A long sustained raised period, because the whole brood is carried continuously for weeks.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Potato Leafhopper

modes.label: Probing leaf veins with piercing mouthparts • Injecting saliva that plugs the phloem • Feeding while the leaf beyond the puncture starves

waveform.description: A very rapid shallow repetition across the whole span, because feeding probes are continuous and individually tiny.

entries.closingLine: Since probes recur constantly, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Potter Wasp

modes.label: Building a clay pot the size of a small marble • Suspending a single egg from the ceiling on a fine filament before any food goes in • Packing paralysed caterpillars beneath it and sealing the lid

waveform.description: A repeated sequence of similar effortful cycles, because each cell is built, stocked and sealed the same way.

entries.closingLine: Since cells are completed within days, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Powder Blue Isopod

modes.label: Secreting a fine waxy bloom across the whole cuticle surface • Reducing water loss through that layer in air other isopods cannot tolerate • Renewing the coating after each moult as the old cuticle is shed

waveform.description: A brisk even oscillation, because this is a fast-moving active isopod rather than a slow one.

entries.closingLine: Because the maintenance is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Powder Blue Tang

modes.label: Holding a defined patch of reef and grazing it repeatedly • Driving off other herbivores that enter • Cropping the turf short enough to keep it growing rather than letting it mature

waveform.description: A working grazing rhythm punctuated by sharper events, because feeding is continuous and intruders are driven off repeatedly.

entries.closingLine: Since grazing and defence are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Prevost's Squirrel

modes.label: Populations separated by the large rivers and straits of Sundaland • Each isolated block diverging in coat colour into sharply distinct regional forms • Dozens of named subspecies across Borneo, Sumatra and the peninsula differing mainly in how the black, white and chestnut are arranged

waveform.description: A stepped drifting line, because each isolated population moves independently rather than as one connected system.

entries.closingLine: Because divergence runs over evolutionary time, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Purple Finch

modes.label: Cracking • Repetitive • Precise

waveform.description: A repeated working rhythm: the same modest force applied over and over.

entries.closingLine: That makes the finch a mid-frequency system: rhythmic and repeatable, where output comes from accurate repetition rather than from any large effort.

entries.name: Pygmy Three-toed Sloth

modes.label: Small-bodied • Mangrove-fed • Sedentary

waveform.description: An almost unbroken low line — the system rarely departs from its baseline at all.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal has solved a small island by becoming a smaller animal that spends almost nothing, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Racket-tailed Roller

modes.label: Climbing steeply and then diving with the wings half closed • Rolling and tumbling through the descent so the flight is barely controlled • Pulling out close to the ground while calling, with the elongated tail rackets streaming behind

waveform.description: A flat line broken by violent tumbling excursions, because the display is a sequence of abrupt uncontrolled-looking movements.

entries.closingLine: Because displays are seasonal, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Raggiana Bird-of-paradise

modes.label: Rhythmic • Site-faithful • Social
Intense • Focused • Spectacle

waveform.description: A mostly mid-level line with one sharp, narrow dip upward (higher activity) showing a brief, intense display phase rising out of a steady rhythmic baseline.

entries.closingLine: That makes the Raggiana Bird-of-paradise a bimodal system: a mid-frequency, site-faithful rhythm that supports a high-frequency, disciplined display burst.

entries.name: Rainbow Crab

modes.label: Living in deep burrows inland, breathing air through modified gill chambers kept moist • Carrying eggs until they are ready and then migrating to the shore to release larvae into seawater • The larvae developing entirely in the sea before returning as juveniles to colonise land again

waveform.description: A flat resident line with one pronounced migratory episode, because the year is ordinary except for the run to the sea.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Rainbow Lorikeet

modes.label: A tongue tipped with erectile papillae that rise into a brush when extended • Sweeping nectar and pollen out of flowers rather than crushing seed • Moving between flowering trees as different species come into bloom across the year

waveform.description: A rapid repeating rhythm, because the bird works flower after flower in quick succession all day.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is continuous through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Rainbow Trout

modes.label: Holding the seam • Reading the drift • Taking and returning

waveform.description: A fine rapid serration riding on one flat hold line, because the interceptions are frequent and small and the station never moves.

entries.closingLine: Because a continuously held position is worked by a constant fine rhythm of interceptions, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Rakali

modes.label: Swimming the margin • Carrying prey ashore • Dissecting it precisely

waveform.description: A repeating cycle of entering the water and returning to the bank.

entries.closingLine: Continuous nightly hunting makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Ray

modes.label: Lying flat under sand with only the eyes and two openings on the upper surface exposed • Drawing clean water in through those spiracles behind the eyes rather than through the mouth below • Passing it over the gills and out beneath, so respiration continues without disturbing the sand or the disguise

waveform.description: An extremely flat and even line, because a buried ray does almost nothing at all for long periods.

entries.closingLine: Because a buried ray is nearly motionless, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Razorfish

modes.label: Holding the body vertical with the snout pointing at the seabed • Hovering in synchronised groups between the spines of a sea urchin • Moving as a unit while keeping the same orientation

waveform.description: A very steady shallow rhythm, because the fish hovers and adjusts constantly without ever moving quickly.

entries.closingLine: Since adjustments are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Ant

modes.label: Releasing volatile alarm compounds from head glands on contact • Drawing nestmates toward the source within seconds • Stinging or spraying acid once they arrive

waveform.description: Flat stretches broken by abrupt spikes that decay quickly, because the alarm signal is volatile and fades almost as fast as it appears.

entries.closingLine: Since the signal rises and decays within seconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Imported Fire Ant

modes.label: A single queen founding alone • Workers killing any additional queen • Territories defended against neighbouring colonies
Dozens or hundreds of queens in one network • No aggression between neighbouring nests • Spread by budding rather than flight

waveform.description: Two clearly separated levels held for long stretches, because a colony is in one social form or the other and does not sit between them.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two colony architectures, making this a bimodal system.

entries.name: Red Junglefowl

modes.label: Producing different alarm calls for aerial and ground predators • Calling far more when a hen is within earshot • Staying silent when alone or when only a rival male is present

waveform.description: A working baseline broken by alarm events of differing depth, because the response varies with who is present.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Lory

modes.label: A liquid nectar diet with very little bulk and almost no fibre • A short simple gut with rapid transit that extracts sugars and passes the rest through within an hour or two • No capacity to store a meal, so the bird must feed for much of the day and cannot go long without

waveform.description: A very rapid repeating rhythm, because feeding and processing cycle many times through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle repeats many times a day, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Red paper wasp

modes.label: Chewing wood fibre into paper • Building a single uncovered comb on a stalk • Defending it with bodies rather than with a wall

waveform.description: A steady moderate rhythm without extremes, because the colony works continuously at one modest scale.

entries.closingLine: Since the colony cycle runs through a season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Slug

modes.label: A mucus that behaves as a solid glue when undisturbed and as a liquid when sheared by the foot • Waves of muscular contraction passing along the foot, liquefying the mucus locally under each moving section • The rest of the animal held firmly in place by the same mucus while those sections advance, so it can climb vertical surfaces without sliding

waveform.description: A regular wave rhythm, because waves of contraction pass along the foot continuously while the animal moves.

entries.closingLine: Because the waves pass continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Swamp Crayfish

modes.label: Carrying the oomycete Aphanomyces astaci in its cuticle while remaining healthy • Shedding spores continuously into any water it occupies • Killing native European crayfish that have no resistance while itself persisting and spreading

waveform.description: A steady relentless advance without episodes, because the spread is continuous rather than event-driven.

entries.closingLine: Because the spread runs across seasons, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Tegu

modes.label: Basking first • Ranging wide • Eating almost anything
Burrowed • Cold • Months without food

waveform.description: A long flat floor with a single raised working season lifted out of it, because the year has two settings and no gradual middle.

entries.closingLine: Because conditions select between two genuinely different operating states, this is an adaptive system.

entries.name: Red Zebra Cichlid

modes.label: The female taking her eggs into her mouth immediately after laying • The male displaying yellow egg-shaped spots on his anal fin • The female nipping at those false eggs and taking in sperm, fertilising the clutch already in her mouth

waveform.description: A flat line with one raised breeding episode, because the whole sequence happens once in a cycle of weeks.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-bellied Pacu

modes.label: Rows of broad flat molar-like teeth strikingly similar to human molars • Fruit and hard nuts falling into flooded forest during the annual high water • The fish cracking those seeds, digesting some and voiding others intact far from the parent tree

waveform.description: A single broad annual swell, because the whole feeding pattern follows the rise and fall of the river.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-bellied Titi
entries.archetype: The Infant Attaches to the Father

modes.label: Duetting at dawn • Sitting tails twined • The father carrying

waveform.description: A quiet stable rhythm with a duet at the start of the day.

entries.closingLine: Small, quiet and stable over years, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-breasted Nuthatch

modes.label: Conifer resin collected and carried in the bill, sometimes on a flake of bark used as an applicator • Smeared in a ring around the outside and inside of the nest hole entrance • The bird flying straight in without touching the sides, while anything that lands on the rim is caught

waveform.description: A seasonal build and decline, because the resin is applied repeatedly through the nesting period and then stops.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-breasted Parakeet

modes.label: Contact calls learned from surrounding birds rather than inherited • Populations in different parts of the range converging on distinct call structures • A bird's calls identifying where it came from and whether it belongs to the local flock

waveform.description: A varied rhythm that differs from place to place, because the material is learned rather than fixed.

entries.closingLine: Because dialect change runs across generations, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-eared Slider

modes.label: Hauling out onto logs, banks and rocks to raise body temperature above the water • Occupying the best basking sites earlier, longer and more aggressively than native turtles • Forcing residents into cooler or more exposed places where digestion and egg development slow

waveform.description: A strong daily cycle of hauling out and returning, because the whole pattern is driven by the movement of the sun.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-footed Cannibalfly

modes.label: Perched • Watching • Aimed
Intercepting • Grappling • Injecting

waveform.description: A still perched line broken by a short violent interception.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: motionless watching and one violent committed interception.

entries.name: Red-lipped Batfish

modes.label: Propped • Shuffling • Luring

waveform.description: A barely moving line with a few small shuffles and one extension.

entries.closingLine: Almost no movement and long waits make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-spotted Purple

modes.label: Dark iridescent blue wings with no white band • Resembling the toxic pipevine swallowtail • Occurring where that model is common
A bold white band across both wings • No resemblance to any toxic species • Occurring north of where the model lives

waveform.description: Two separated stable levels joined by a single transition, because the two forms meet only in a narrow band of country.

entries.closingLine: The two defences also work on different timescales, the mimicry depending on a season of predator learning where the banded form acts within one encounter, which makes this a bimodal system.

entries.name: Red-tailed Black Shark

modes.label: Holding a territory around a cave, root or rock on the stream bed • Attacking intruders in proportion to how closely they resemble itself • Ignoring fish of different shape and habit that use other parts of the water

waveform.description: A calm baseline interrupted by regular sharp confrontations, because the fish patrols quietly and charges intruders.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-veined Darter

modes.label: Arriving in spring from further south • Breeding immediately in warm shallow water • Producing adults from those eggs within about two months, which then breed again or move on

waveform.description: A working rhythm with two distinct raised events, because the summer contains two separate emergences.

entries.closingLine: Since emergences and breeding recur within a season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Redclaw crayfish

modes.label: Carrying eggs beneath the tail • Hatching young already formed • Releasing juveniles straight into the burrow

waveform.description: Broad low plateaus separated by raised sections, because brooding periods interrupt an otherwise even routine.

entries.closingLine: Since brooding cycles repeat within a season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Redwing

modes.label: Flying through the night over unlit country • Giving a thin high seep call repeatedly • Keeping a loose flock together by sound alone

waveform.description: A regular unvarying pulse maintained across the whole span, because the call is repeated steadily through hours of flight.

entries.closingLine: Since calls recur through the night, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Reeves's Muntjac

modes.label: Solitary • Small • Hidden
Barking • Repetitive • Prolonged

waveform.description: A quiet line broken by a long series of repeated calls.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a hidden solitary baseline and a persistent vocal response.

entries.name: Reticulated river stingray

modes.label: Settled on sand • Net pattern breaking the edge • Feeling for worms

waveform.description: A long shallow drift with no events in it, the trace of an animal whose main activity is not being seen.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs slowly across a river bottom, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Rice Grasshopper

modes.label: Life spent on rice stems standing in water rather than on dry ground • The insect swimming when it falls in and climbing back onto a stem rather than drowning • Eggs laid in the raised bunds and drier margins above the waterline, so the vulnerable stage is never submerged

waveform.description: A steady active rhythm, because the insect feeds, climbs and moves continuously through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because activity is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Ring-billed Gull

modes.label: Working whatever is briefly abundant • Learning where and when it appears • Moving on when it stops

waveform.description: Irregular spikes of different heights against a common baseline, because each opportunity is a different size and arrives unpredictably.

entries.closingLine: Since opportunities turn over within days, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Ring-necked Dove

modes.label: Putting the bill into water and drawing continuously • Emptying a puddle in seconds without straightening up • Leaving the water almost immediately

waveform.description: A calm baseline broken by short flat-bottomed dips, because drinking is a brief continuous act rather than a series of movements.

entries.closingLine: Since drinking and feeding recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Roadside Hawk

modes.label: Perching on exposed posts, wires and low branches along the boundary of forest and open ground • Watching the cleared side while remaining in cover on the wooded side • Dropping short distances onto lizards, large insects and small vertebrates crossing that boundary

waveform.description: A steady repeating rhythm of perch, watch and short drop, sustained through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because hunting is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Roe Deer

modes.label: Paused • Timed • Annual

waveform.description: A steady year with a long flattened section in the middle — the months when development is paused rather than absent.

entries.closingLine: Because the annual cycle runs steadily, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Roloway Monkey

modes.label: Grouped • Signalling • Daily

waveform.description: A continuous social rhythm across the day — many small exchanges rather than any single event.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on constant low-cost signalling and steady daily foraging, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Rose-ringed Parakeet

modes.label: Feeding out in small parties • Returning to one roost • Following whoever fed well

waveform.description: A busy daytime rhythm with two taller convergences in it, because the flock assembles twice a day and disperses between.

entries.closingLine: Since the feeding and the assembling repeat on one daily cycle, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Rosy Tetra

modes.label: Holding spacing • Matching heading • Turning with the neighbour

waveform.description: An identical repeating ripple with no variation whatever, because every part of the system is doing the same thing as its neighbour.

entries.closingLine: Because the matching is continuous and never pauses, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Rove Beetle

modes.label: A bacterial symbiont living inside the beetle producing pederin, a compound the insect has no genes to synthesise • That toxin held in the body fluid, so crushing the beetle releases it onto skin • Blistering dermatitis developing hours later at the site, from a beetle that never bit or stung anything

waveform.description: A quiet line with occasional releases, because the beetle is unremarkable until it is crushed.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters are sporadic, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Ruddy Daggerwing

modes.label: Long thin tails projecting from the hindwings that resemble antennae • Dark lines on the closed underside converging towards those tails as if towards a head • A strike directed at that end removing a piece of wing while the butterfly leaves in the opposite direction

waveform.description: A quiet resting line with a single sharp interruption, because the butterfly sits still and is attacked occasionally.

entries.closingLine: Because attacks are occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Ruddy Ground Dove

modes.label: Cryptic • Still • Ground-gleaning

waveform.description: A flat low trace: almost nothing about the bird's output varies.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: quiet, economical and dependent on not being detected at all.

entries.name: Rufous Hornero

modes.label: Mud and dung carried beakful by beakful and built up in courses that are allowed to dry between them • A domed chamber formed with a side entrance and an internal wall creating a curved passage • The nest baking hard in the sun into a rigid shell that lasts years and is used by many other species afterwards

waveform.description: A long seasonal build and decline, because the nest takes weeks of accumulation and is then simply occupied.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Rugose Hermit Crab

modes.label: A shell occupied on land, where its full weight must be carried rather than supported by water • The interior worn away and remodelled by the crab so the walls become thinner and the internal volume larger • A shell that is lighter to carry and roomier to grow in than the same shell would be for a marine crab

waveform.description: A nightly activity period, because the crab forages after dark and shelters through the heat of the day.

entries.closingLine: Because the remodelling runs over months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sahara Spiny-tailed Lizard

modes.label: Emerging dark, almost black, in the cold morning to absorb solar radiation quickly • Lightening through the day to yellow, orange or red as body temperature rises • Reflecting rather than absorbing once the target temperature is reached

waveform.description: A smooth daily arc, because the colour tracks body temperature continuously from dawn to dusk.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Sailfin Tang

modes.label: Swimming with the enormous dorsal and anal fins folded flat against the body • Erecting both simultaneously when threatened or challenged, roughly doubling the apparent body depth • Turning side-on so the expanded outline faces the other animal directly

waveform.description: A calm line with repeated sharp expansions, because the display snaps on and off rather than building.

entries.closingLine: Because displays recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Sally Lightfoot Crab
entries.archetype: Ten Legs on Wet Vertical Rock

modes.label: Sprinting • Adhering • Multi-directional

waveform.description: Dense rapid movement with no pause.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: continuously fast and continuously adhering.

entries.name: Salmon-crested Cockatoo
entries.archetype: A Signal That Changes In A Second

modes.label: Decades of pairing • Slow breeding • Instant signalling

waveform.description: A very slow underlying life with brief flicks of signal on top.

entries.closingLine: Everything about the system is low-frequency except the one channel that had to be fast.

entries.name: Saltwater Crocodile

modes.label: Floating • Waiting out the wrong tide • Riding the right one
Lunging • Clamping • Rolling

waveform.description: A long flat floor rising gradually into one enormous spike and settling slowly afterwards, because the approach is a slow gather and the release is not.

entries.closingLine: Because an overwhelmingly cheap waiting state exists to fund rare and enormous releases of power, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Sambar Deer

modes.label: Detecting a stalking predator by scent, sound or sight while browsing alone • Giving a loud repeated metallic bell call that carries far through dense forest • Other deer, langurs and peafowl responding to that call as reliable information

waveform.description: A flat line broken by a short cluster of repeated calls, because the alarm is delivered as an insistent burst and then stops.

entries.closingLine: Because alarms are occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sand Goby

modes.label: Excavating sand from beneath a bivalve shell to make a chamber • Attracting a female to lay on its underside • Fanning the clutch with the pectoral fins continuously until it hatches

waveform.description: A rapid shallow oscillation maintained without a break, because the fanning continues for days without stopping.

entries.closingLine: Since fin beats repeat continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Scaly-foot Snail

modes.label: Fed by bacteria • Enormous heart running • Plating itself in iron sulphide

waveform.description: A steady unvarying pulse, the trace of an animal whose largest organ is a heart that never changes rate.

entries.closingLine: Because the circulation and chemosynthesis run continuously at one unvarying rate, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Scarlet Skimmer
entries.archetype: Pointing the Abdomen at the Sun

modes.label: Patrolling • Red • Contested
Obelisk • Vertical • Cooling

waveform.description: An active patrolling rhythm dropping into a still midday pause.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: active contested patrolling and a still thermal posture.

entries.name: Scimitar-horned Oryx

modes.label: Allowing body temperature to rise through the day rather than sweating it away • Cooling arterial blood to the brain through a network in the nasal passages • Shedding the stored heat at night when the desert cools

waveform.description: A slow smooth rise and fall across the span, because the whole system is a single daily cycle of storing heat and releasing it.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is daily and generations are slow, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sea Pig

modes.label: Walking on inflated tube feet • Reading the mud chemically • Facing into the current

waveform.description: A barely perceptible drift across the whole span, because nothing this animal does registers as an event.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at the rate food falls, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Secretarybird

modes.label: Striding • Flushing • All-day
Stamping • Precise • Milliseconds

waveform.description: An even walking band with two needle-thin strikes — the strike is so short it has no width on the trace.

entries.closingLine: Because sustained walking search supports a rare, extremely brief application of force, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Sedge Warbler

modes.label: Feeding almost exclusively on plum-reed aphids at autumn reedbeds • Nearly doubling body weight in a fortnight • Flying the whole distance to sub-Saharan Africa without stopping

waveform.description: A working rhythm that descends into a deep sustained excursion and recovers, because the fuelling period is a prolonged departure from normal life.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Seed Bug

modes.label: Fallen seed accumulating on the ground and persisting for months or years as a dormant bank • Stylets inserted through the seed coat and enzymes injected to liquefy the contents • The insect drawing out the liquefied endosperm, so a hard dry package becomes drinkable

waveform.description: A steady low-amplitude rhythm, because the food supply persists and feeding continues without seasonal peaks.

entries.closingLine: Because the supply is persistent, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Seven-spotted Ladybird

modes.label: Finding a colony • Laying into it • Larvae clearing it

waveform.description: A brisk working rhythm with slightly rising peaks, because a larva's appetite grows through every instar.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is a continuous cycle of finding colonies and converting them, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Shield & Stink Bug

modes.label: Brilliant metallic colour produced by layered structure in the cuticle rather than by pigment • Glands on the thorax releasing a strongly repellent mixture of aldehydes when the insect is handled • The colour functioning as an advertisement of that chemistry rather than as decoration or camouflage

waveform.description: A quiet feeding line with occasional discharges, because the insect sits and feeds and only rarely releases.

entries.closingLine: Because discharges are occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Shore Crab

modes.label: Moving between full seawater, estuary and rockpool within a tide • Actively pumping salts across the gills to hold internal concentration • Feeding on whatever the change of water exposes

waveform.description: A regular tidal rhythm of moderate excursions, because activity follows the water rather than the clock.

entries.closingLine: Since tidal movements recur twice a day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Short-beaked Echidna

modes.label: Nosing damp soil • Reading faint fields • Digging straight down

waveform.description: A single slow shallow undulation across the whole frame, as close to nothing as a working animal produces.

entries.closingLine: Because every process here is slow, cheap and measured in months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Siamese algae eater

modes.label: Working the surface • Rasping the film • Moving to the next stone

waveform.description: A close repetitive rasp of near-identical strokes, because the work is thousands of small identical passes.

entries.closingLine: Because that rasping is repetitive, unhurried and effectively constant, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Siamese Fighting Fish

modes.label: Breathing at the surface • Flaring the gill covers • Tending a raft of bubbles

waveform.description: A working rhythm with three taller lifts in it, because the display is repeated whenever a boundary is tested.

entries.closingLine: Because the breathing, guarding and displaying run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Siberian Musk Deer

modes.label: Lichen-fed • Tusked • Solitary

waveform.description: A shallow steady rhythm low on the trace — a small animal eating poor food at an unvarying rate.

entries.closingLine: Because intake is poor and the pace is unvarying, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Siberian Sturgeon

modes.label: Completing the entire life cycle within one river system rather than running to the sea • Migrating long distances upstream and downstream inside the same catchment • Depending on that river's gravels, depth and flow for every stage from egg to adult

waveform.description: A broad slow cycle within a single range, because the fish moves long distances but always within the same water.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle spans years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Signature Spider

modes.label: Bands of dense white silk laid in a zigzag across the centre of an otherwise near-invisible orb web • That structure varying between individuals, days and conditions rather than being fixed • Several competing explanations supported in different studies, with no single function established across all cases

waveform.description: A quiet variable rhythm without a fixed pattern, because the structure itself is built inconsistently.

entries.closingLine: Because the web is rebuilt over days, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Silky Carpenter Ant

modes.label: Workers emerging across a continuous range of sizes from small to very large within one colony • Small individuals handling brood, nest work and tasks requiring fine manipulation • Large individuals with disproportionately enlarged heads and jaws handling defence, cutting and carrying, so the same colony covers jobs needing opposite body sizes

waveform.description: A continuous busy rhythm, because many individuals are working simultaneously at different tasks.

entries.closingLine: Because the colony works continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Silver Dollar Fish

modes.label: Broad flat teeth adapted for shearing leaves rather than flesh • Shoaling in numbers through flooded forest and vegetated river margins • Feeding on submerged plants, fallen leaves and fruit taken directly from the water column

waveform.description: A brisk even oscillation, because a shoaling fish moves and feeds continuously without pauses or peaks.

entries.closingLine: Because shoaling is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Silver Pheasant

modes.label: Walking forest floor and displaying on the ground rather than in the air • Carrying upperparts of white feathers each ruled with fine black lines • Producing a pattern that reads as bright white from a distance and as fine detail up close

waveform.description: A quiet line broken by broad moderate rises, because displays are occasional and sustained rather than sudden.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Silvery Gibbon

modes.label: Morning-call • Brachiating • Territorial

waveform.description: A rising sequence of call phrases at dawn, a long quiet working day, and a shorter answering bout — the day is bracketed by song.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system runs on a repeated daily broadcast and a steady canopy circuit, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Slender Skimmer

modes.label: Intercepting • Rapid • Visual

waveform.description: Rapid repeated attack peaks with almost no gap between them.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: fast, reactive and organised around many brief precise events.

entries.name: Small Branded Swift

modes.label: Short narrow wings carrying a thick heavily muscled body, giving very high wing loading for a butterfly • Wingbeats fast enough to blur, with no capacity to glide or soar at all • Flight that is extremely fast and abruptly directional, darting between perches rather than flapping across open ground

waveform.description: An extremely fast unbroken beat, because the insect cannot glide and must beat continuously to stay airborne.

entries.closingLine: Because the beat is continuous, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Smooth Ground Beetle

modes.label: Carrying elytra fused into a single rigid shell with no wings beneath • Walking everywhere it goes • Being unable to cross a road, a field or a clearing that a flying beetle would not notice

waveform.description: A long slow unvarying line with one small rise, because everything this animal does happens at walking pace.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Smooth-coated Otter

modes.label: Formation • Herding • Synchronised

waveform.description: Dense continuous coordinated activity.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: continuously active and continuously coordinated.

entries.name: Snail

modes.label: Drawing a chitinous ribbon carrying thousands of teeth across a surface • Wearing the front rows away as it works • Growing replacements continuously from the back so the working edge is always new

waveform.description: A rapid even rasping rhythm sustained without variation, because the ribbon is drawn back and forth continuously while feeding.

entries.closingLine: Since rasping repeats many times a minute, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Snout Moth

modes.label: Labial palps projecting forward from the head into a long pointed snout • Wings held in a triangular tent whose outline resembles a curled dead leaf • The projecting snout continuing that outline as the leaf stalk, so the most animal-like part of the head becomes the least

waveform.description: An almost perfectly level line, because the moth rests motionless in one posture through the whole day.

entries.closingLine: Because the posture is held for long periods, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Snubnose Pompano

modes.label: Regulating internal salt balance across water from nearly fresh to full seawater • Continuing to grow rather than merely surviving across that whole range • Occupying estuaries, lagoons and open coast without a physiological transition

waveform.description: A steady moderate oscillation, because the fish is continuously compensating for water that keeps changing around it.

entries.closingLine: Because compensation is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Song Sparrow

modes.label: Learning several song types as a young bird • Matching the type a neighbour just sang • Escalating or retreating on the basis of the match

waveform.description: Repeated bouts of similar height with small differences between them, because the bird cycles through a set of song types rather than repeating one.

entries.closingLine: Since exchanges occur within seconds, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Sooty-headed Bulbul

modes.label: Switching • Edge-dwelling • Sociable

waveform.description: A steady unremarkable rhythm that continues whatever the season is doing.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, rhythmic and reliable because it is never committed to a single resource.

entries.name: South American Coati

modes.label: Rooting • Banded • Reversible

waveform.description: A steady searching rhythm sustained through the day.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, wide and continuously searching rather than waiting.

entries.name: South American Tapir

modes.label: Swallowing whole fruits and large seeds no smaller animal can take • Walking kilometres through forest before voiding them • Depositing them in dung far from the parent tree

waveform.description: A long slow even line with a small rise, because the animal moves steadily and nothing about its routine is abrupt.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Southeastern Five-lined Skink
entries.archetype: A Tail Meant to Be Struck

modes.label: Carrying a vivid blue tail as a juvenile that draws the eye away from the head • Shedding it at a fracture plane when it is seized • Leaving it writhing for minutes while the animal leaves

waveform.description: A line broken by a sharp event after which it settles at a different level, because the loss is real and the recovery is partial.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Southern African Porcupine

modes.label: Digging • Nocturnal • Unhurried
Rattle • Reverse • Committed

waveform.description: A slow flat baseline, a warning step, then one sharp committed reversal.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a cheap unhurried baseline holding one brief, expensive and deliberately advertised defence.

entries.name: Southern Black Widow

modes.label: Anchored • Waiting • Disproportionate

waveform.description: A near-flat line with two small disturbances from something else's struggle.

entries.closingLine: Minimal expenditure and a durable structure make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Southern Lapwing

modes.label: Feeding in the open • Screaming at anything approaching • Dragging a wing away from the nest

waveform.description: A working rhythm cut by three sharp lifts, because the display is deployed repeatedly rather than held.

entries.closingLine: Because that vigilance and feeding run together through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Southern Lechwe
entries.archetype: Hooves Made for Bounding Through Water

modes.label: Splashing • Bounding • Committed

waveform.description: A bounding rhythm of repeated leaps through resistance.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: continuously active in a medium that is itself the defence.

entries.name: Southern Platyfish

modes.label: A pigment-cell gene in the platyfish held in check by a suppressor elsewhere in its own genome • Crossing with a swordtail bringing the gene in without that suppressor • The unrestrained gene driving pigment cells into malignant melanoma in the hybrid offspring

waveform.description: A flat line disturbed by one developing excursion, because the effect only appears when two genomes are combined.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is generational, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Southern Three-banded Armadillo
entries.archetype: A Shell With Room to Close

modes.label: Walking • Loose-shelled • Tiptoed
Rolled • Sealed • Sprung

waveform.description: A low walking line rising abruptly into a held closed state.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: an unhurried ordinary gait and a single complete transformation.

entries.name: Southern Toad

modes.label: Sitting still when approached • Secreting a milky toxin from glands behind the eyes • Relying on the attacker releasing it rather than on escape

waveform.description: A long unbroken flat line with a single abrupt spike, because nothing happens until contact and then everything does.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur through active periods, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Spectacled Bear

modes.label: Climbing • Chewing • Platformed

waveform.description: A slow steady line with gentle variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, powerful and built to use poor material.

entries.name: Spider Crab

modes.label: Walking the seabed alone through most of the year • Feeding on molluscs, echinoderms and algae • Carrying a spined carapace that is hard and adequate
Gathering into mounds of hundreds of animals • Moulting inside the heap while soft and defenceless • Relying on the bodies of the others for protection until the shell hardens

waveform.description: Even solitary activity giving way to a long flat depressed section, because the animal alternates between ordinary life and a state in which it can do nothing.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, a soft aggregated animal and a hard solitary one are two states, making this a bimodal system.

entries.name: Spider Monkey

modes.label: A long prehensile tail with a hairless friction pad on the underside of the tip • Ridged skin on that pad forming patterns like fingerprints and densely supplied with touch receptors • Hanging, bridging and feeding with the tail supporting the whole body weight while both hands work

waveform.description: A continuous flowing rhythm with no pauses, because the animal is always in contact with several supports at once.

entries.closingLine: Because movement is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Spinner Dolphin
entries.archetype: Rotating on the Long Axis in Mid-Air

modes.label: Resting • Shallow • Half-asleep
Diving • Deep • Nocturnal

waveform.description: An active nocturnal rhythm alternating with a shallow daytime lull.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a shallow resting phase and a deep active one.

entries.name: Spiny Lizard

modes.label: Carrying brilliant blue patches on the belly and throat that are invisible from above • Doing push-ups on a rock to flash them sideways and downward • Being a mottled grey-brown animal the rest of the time

waveform.description: A calm line broken by sharp bursts, because the displays are short and repeated against an otherwise still background.

entries.closingLine: Since displays recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Spinybacked Orbweaver

modes.label: Rebuilding an orb web daily across an open gap • Adding conspicuous tufts of white silk along the anchor lines • Sitting in the hub behind a hard spined abdomen

waveform.description: A steady repetitive pattern of comparable effort, because the web is rebuilt and maintained on the same cycle continually.

entries.closingLine: Since web maintenance is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Spotted Barb

modes.label: Occupying streams, ditches, rice fields and rivers across a vast area of Southeast Asia • Showing considerable variation in form and markings between populations • Having genetic work reveal that the name covers several distinct lineages rather than one fish

waveform.description: A steady even rhythm with modest variation, because a small stream barb's day is continuous and unremarkable.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Spotted Dove

modes.label: Producing crop milk in both sexes • Feeding chicks on it regardless of season • Breeding through most of the year

waveform.description: A gentle, even undulation with no sharp features, because the system runs continuously at a low amplitude.

entries.closingLine: Since nesting attempts repeat within weeks, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Spotted Gar

modes.label: Diamond-shaped ganoid scales locked to one another by peg-and-socket joints • A hard enamel-like ganoine surface over a bone base across the whole body • A rigid casing that resists bite and puncture while allowing only limited flexion

waveform.description: A long flat line with two sudden strikes, because the fish hangs motionless and then lunges sideways.

entries.closingLine: Because strikes are infrequent, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Spotted Garden Eel

modes.label: Holding the tail in a mucus-lined burrow • Extending the body into the current and picking plankton • Withdrawing entirely when anything approaches

waveform.description: A gently varying raised level that drops flat at intervals, because the animal is either up in the current or entirely gone.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding picks recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Spotted Jellyfish

modes.label: Pulsing • Straining • Photosynthesising

waveform.description: A pure regular pulse with identical peaks and no interruption anywhere, because the bell has no other rhythm to switch into.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal runs one uninterrupted pulse that is simultaneously its propulsion and its feeding, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Spotted Linsang

modes.label: Nocturnal • Sheathed • Weightless

waveform.description: A quiet careful nocturnal line with minimal variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: light, quiet and almost entirely undetected.

entries.name: Spotted Sharpnose Puffer

modes.label: Feeding across reef on invertebrates and algae • Accumulating tetrodotoxin produced by bacteria and passed along the food chain • Carrying it in the skin and organs and inflating when threatened

waveform.description: A calm line rising into sustained raised events, because inflation is held for as long as the threat is present.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Spotted Wood Owl

modes.label: Perched • Listening • Motionless
Drop • Silent • Decisive

waveform.description: A long motionless watch broken by one narrow drop that settles quickly.

entries.closingLine: That makes the owl a bimodal system: a very cheap listening state and one brief committed descent.

entries.name: Spotted-winged Antlion
entries.archetype: A Pit Dug to the Angle of Collapse

modes.label: Buried • Waiting • Collapsing

waveform.description: An almost featureless low line.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: near-zero expenditure with the environment doing the work.

entries.name: Squilla Mantis

modes.label: Waiting at a burrow mouth in soft mud • Unfolding barbed raptorial appendages in milliseconds • Impaling soft prey and withdrawing underground

waveform.description: A flat line broken by extremely narrow full-depth spikes, because the strike is over before anything else has time to change.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes happen in thousandths of a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: St Mark's Fly

modes.label: Larvae developing through autumn and winter in soil and leaf litter and all reaching maturity together • Adults emerging within a narrow window in late April in numbers large enough to be conspicuous • Males hanging in swarms with legs dangling, the whole population mating and dying within a fortnight

waveform.description: A long flat absence with one sharp spike, because the whole adult population appears and disappears within days.

entries.closingLine: Because the emergence is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Stalk-eyed Fly

waveform.description: A calm line with repeated confrontations, because encounters occur regularly and resolve quickly.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters recur, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Stars and Stripes Pufferfish

modes.label: Four teeth fused into a heavy beak, two above and two below • Continuous growth of that beak throughout life • Crushing molluscs, urchins and coral so that the beak is worn back as fast as it grows

waveform.description: A flat line with deliberate isolated bites, because the fish moves slowly and feeds in discrete crushing events.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding events are discrete, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Steppe Eagle

modes.label: Soaring • Wide • Opportunistic

waveform.description: A low soaring rhythm covering distance without effort.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: economical, wide-ranging and opportunistic.

entries.name: Sterlet Sturgeon

waveform.description: A gentle rise and slow settling, because the life history is compressed but still measured in years.

entries.closingLine: Because generations still run over years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Stick Insect
