waveform.description: Long flat stretches with a single shallow raised section, because almost the entire cycle is stillness broken by a slow night of feeding.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle turns over across a season, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Stick Mantis

modes.label: An extremely elongated body with leaf-like flanges and irregular projections breaking the outline • The insect rocking gently from side to side while stationary rather than holding perfectly still • That movement matching what surrounding vegetation does in moving air, so stillness in a moving background would be the thing that stood out

waveform.description: A gentle continuous sway with small amplitude, because the insect is always moving slightly and never abruptly.

entries.closingLine: Because the sway is continuous, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Stilt Bug

modes.label: Extremely long slender legs holding the body well clear of the leaf surface • Only the small tips of the feet in contact at any moment, and those moved deliberately and slowly • Progress across sticky glandular hairs that trap and kill insects with ordinary leg contact

waveform.description: A slow careful even rhythm, because the animal moves deliberately and never hurries.

entries.closingLine: Because the movement is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Straw-headed Bulbul

modes.label: A loud rich bubbling song delivered from riverside vegetation and audible at a distance • That song prized above almost any other in the Southeast Asian songbird trade and in competitions • Trappers locating and taking birds by the song itself, so the trait that defines the species is what removes it

waveform.description: A normal rhythm drifting steadily downward, because ordinary behaviour continues while the population falls.

entries.closingLine: Because the decline runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Streaked Gurnard

modes.label: The lowest three pectoral fin rays on each side detached and free-moving • Those rays used to walk over the bottom and to probe the sediment • Chemoreceptors on them detecting buried prey by taste before anything is seen

waveform.description: A steady exploratory rhythm, because the fish works methodically across the bottom without pause.

entries.closingLine: Because searching is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Striped Albatross

modes.label: Developing in the wet season with broader dark markings • Flying in cooler cloudier conditions • Producing the form that most descriptions treat as typical
Developing in the dry season with reduced dark markings and paler wings • Flying in hot bright conditions • Being taken repeatedly for a different species

waveform.description: Two separated levels with transitions between them twice, because the forms alternate with the seasons rather than switching once.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two developmental states, making it a bimodal system.

entries.name: Striped Blister Beetle

modes.label: Feeding openly on foliage in conspicuous stripes • Releasing haemolymph from leg joints when seized • Delivering cantharidin that blisters the skin of whatever grasped it

waveform.description: A quiet line broken by isolated sharp events, because the defence is discharged only on contact.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Striped Snakehead

modes.label: An active fish in standing water, breathing air at the surface, hunting and guarding young in the wet season
A fish buried in the mud of a dried pool, metabolism suppressed, held in a moist chamber and surviving months without water

waveform.description: An active varying rhythm dropping to a flat suppressed line, because the animal moves between two different physiological states.

entries.closingLine: The two states are distinct architectures, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Sturgeon

modes.label: Cruising just above the bed with a flattened snout lowered • Detecting buried prey with barbels and electroreceptors • Protruding a toothless tube-like mouth downward to suck it out

waveform.description: A long slow even line with almost no features, because a large bottom-feeding fish moves and feeds at one steady unhurried rate.

entries.closingLine: Since generations run in decades, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sugar Glider

modes.label: Launching from a high trunk with limbs spread • Gliding on a membrane stretched between fifth finger and ankle • Steering by altering the tension and landing head-up on the next trunk

waveform.description: A repeated pattern of sharp launches followed by controlled descents, because each movement between trees is one glide with a definite shape.

entries.closingLine: Since glides recur through the night, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Sulcata Tortoise

modes.label: Digging • Waiting • Decadal

waveform.description: One seasonal rise where the rains allow activity, settling back into a long underground floor for the rest of the year.

entries.closingLine: Because a very low-cost body waits out the hard season inside a structure it built, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sumatran Bamboo Rat

modes.label: Cutting tunnel with the incisors • Reaching rhizomes from below • Pulling the culm down

waveform.description: A slow steady working rhythm with no peaks, because progress is measured in centimetres of tunnel rather than in events.

entries.closingLine: Because everything proceeds slowly and without interruption, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sundas Pit Viper

modes.label: A membrane-lined pit between eye and nostril on each side of the head • Detecting temperature differences of a fraction of a degree across that membrane • Overlaying the thermal image on the visual one so a warm body is located in total darkness

waveform.description: A low irregular baseline of scanning with occasional sharp strikes, because the snake searches continuously and strikes rarely.

entries.closingLine: Because scanning is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Swift Fox

modes.label: Burrows occupied and maintained throughout the year rather than only for raising young • Multiple entrances and several dens within a home range, used and switched constantly • The animal retreating underground from coyotes, raptors, heat and cold alike, on ground with no cover of any kind

waveform.description: A single nocturnal excursion each day, because the animal is below ground for most of every cycle.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Swinhoe's Pheasant
entries.archetype: Iridescence Aimed at a Light Gap

modes.label: Foraging • Orienting • Flashing

waveform.description: Quiet forest-floor foraging with brief aimed flashes.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady ground foraging carrying a signal that is aimed rather than simply worn.

entries.name: Swordfish

modes.label: Descending • Resolving • Slashing

waveform.description: Level cruising torn open by strikes that reach the top of the frame.

entries.closingLine: Short committed attacks between long cruising makes this a single high-frequency system.

entries.name: Tadpole Shrimp

modes.label: Hatching within a day of a pool filling • Growing to full size in two or three weeks • Feeding on everything in the pool and laying before the water goes
Lying in dry sediment as a desiccated cyst • Withstanding years or decades without water • Requiring drying and rewetting before hatching at all

waveform.description: Long flat depressed stretches interrupted by short violent bursts, because almost all of the time nothing is alive and then everything happens at once.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two different states, making it a bimodal system.

entries.name: Tench

modes.label: Living in warm shallow water thick with vegetation • Tolerating dissolved oxygen levels that kill other fish • Burying into soft mud and remaining there when conditions become impossible

waveform.description: A slow steady line with small occasional excursions, because a fish in still warm water does everything at a deliberate pace.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Tenkile

modes.label: Confined • Slow • Agreement-held

waveform.description: A low steady line with a slight upward drift — a population recovering slowly from very few animals.

entries.closingLine: Because everything about the system runs at a very low rate, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Texas Tortoise

modes.label: Pushing a shallow depression under dense thorn scrub • Using vegetation rather than depth for shelter • Depending on that scrub for shade, humidity and concealment

waveform.description: A very flat slow line with a single small rise, because a small tortoise in scrub does almost nothing quickly.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Thorny Oyster

modes.label: Cemented to rock • Growing spines outward • Letting sponges cover them

waveform.description: A near-flat line with two shallow rises in it, because the only rhythm a cemented filter feeder has is the tide passing over it.

entries.closingLine: Because the filtering and growing proceed at one unvarying slow rate, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Three-spined Stickleback

modes.label: Building • Fanning • Breeding season

waveform.description: A rapid unbroken rhythm — the fanning that oxygenates the eggs continues almost without pause for days.

entries.closingLine: Because building and fanning run as a fast steady cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Three-spot Gourami

modes.label: Trailing two long thread-like pelvic rays ahead and beside the body • Touching surfaces and objects it cannot see • Building a bubble nest at the surface and guarding it

waveform.description: A continuous gentle exploratory rhythm with no strong events, because the feelers are in motion almost all the time.

entries.closingLine: Since the filaments move constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Tibetan Fox

modes.label: Narrow • Paired • Following

waveform.description: A patient low line with small steady variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: patient, narrow and dependent on one prey species entirely.

entries.name: Tiger Barb

modes.label: Maintaining a constant order of chasing and nipping within the group • Spreading that aggression across many individuals when the shoal is large • Concentrating it destructively on one or two when it is small

waveform.description: A dense continuous pattern of similar small events, because the interactions are constant, minor and never stop.

entries.closingLine: Since interactions recur every few seconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Tiger Moth

modes.label: Feeding as a larva on fig leaves that bleed latex when cut • Tolerating and storing the compounds in that latex • Advertising the result with orange, black and white warning colours as an adult

waveform.description: A quiet even line with a single modest rise, because the animal's year is one slow larval period and a brief adult stage.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Tiger Wolf Spider

modes.label: Held still • Legs on the ground • Eyes open to the dark
Turning • Lunging • Holding

waveform.description: A long quiet floor broken by one needle-thin spike and nothing else, because the whole night reduces to a single committed movement.

entries.closingLine: Because a long cheap listening state exists in order to fund one very short and very expensive movement, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Tinfoil Barb

modes.label: Flanks covered in guanine-crystal scales that reflect light almost like a mirror • Hundreds of fish shoaling and turning together so the reflections flash and shift constantly • A predator unable to hold a single target because the visual field is broken into moving points of light

waveform.description: A rapid coordinated rhythm, because the whole shoal turns and flashes continuously.

entries.closingLine: Because turning is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Toadstool Leather Coral

modes.label: Withdrawing the polyps and developing a waxy film across the whole surface of the cap • Holding that state for days while algae and settling larvae accumulate on the film • Sloughing the entire layer off and reopening, leaving a clean surface beneath

waveform.description: A slow accumulation followed by an abrupt return, because fouling builds up and is then discarded at once.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Toque Macaque

modes.label: Individual monkeys identified, named and followed continuously since the late 1960s at Polonnaruwa • Births, deaths, ranks, injuries and migrations recorded for every animal across their whole lives • Patterns emerging that no short study could detect, including how rank is inherited, how droughts remove cohorts and how lineages rise and fall

waveform.description: A steady continuous rhythm with no interruption, because the record and the society both run without a break.

entries.closingLine: Because the patterns run across generations, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Trashline Orb-weaver

modes.label: Prey husks, moulted skins, plant fragments and egg sacs fastened into a vertical line down the centre of the web • The spider sitting at the hub in the middle of that line, matched in size and colour to the debris around it • A searching predator presented with a row of similar objects, only one of which is alive

waveform.description: A very flat line with only slight variation, because the spider sits motionless at the hub for long periods.

entries.closingLine: Because the line accumulates over days, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Tree Frog

modes.label: Pressing a broad toe pad against a leaf or a stem • Secreting a thin film of mucus between the pad and the surface • Holding on by the surface tension and viscosity of that film rather than by suction or glue

waveform.description: A steady holding line broken by sharp brief events, because the animal clings still and then jumps.

entries.closingLine: Since grips and jumps recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Treehopper

modes.label: Sitting still on a stem with a helmet that reads as a thorn or a piece of debris • Feeding on sap through the bark • Signalling to others through vibrations in the plant itself

waveform.description: A near-flat line with small occasional disturbances, because the animal barely moves and its signalling is a subtle vibration rather than an event.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding and signalling are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Triangulate Combfoot

modes.label: Waiting in a tangle web in a corner or under furniture • Flicking sticky silk over an entangled animal from a distance using a comb of serrated bristles on the hind legs • Approaching only once the prey is wrapped and immobile

waveform.description: A still line broken by short sequences of escalating events, because the wrapping builds before the spider approaches.

entries.closingLine: Since captures recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Tropical Carpenter Bee

modes.label: Boring dead wood • Provisioning each cell • Sealing behind her

waveform.description: Bursts of heavy cutting separated by flat stretches, because the bee stops to clear shavings before boring again.

entries.closingLine: Because that cycle repeats steadily through the season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Tropical Leatherleaf Slug

modes.label: Carrying a thick tough mantle covering the whole upper surface with no shell beneath it • Breathing through a single pore at the rear rather than a mantle cavity on the side • Burrowing into soil by day and grazing at night

waveform.description: A very slow even line with a single small rise, because everything about this animal happens at a crawl.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: True Oyster

modes.label: Drifting as larvae until they detect chemical cues from existing oyster shell • Cementing the left valve permanently to it • Growing into a three-dimensional structure built from generations of shells

waveform.description: A rapid shallow rhythm with no larger structure, because the animal filters continuously and never does anything else.

entries.closingLine: Since filtering is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Tunnelweb Spider

modes.label: Heavy forward-pointing chelicerae driven by large muscles filling the front of the body • Prey seized and crushed mechanically rather than subdued by venom alone • Snails, beetles and other hard-cased animals opened by force that a puncturing bite could not handle

waveform.description: A long still line with occasional powerful events, because the spider waits and then commits heavily.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding events are occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Turbot

modes.label: Swimming upright in the plankton as a symmetrical larva • Having eyes on both sides of the head • Feeding in open water like any other fish
Lying on the bottom on the right side • Carrying both eyes on the left with a twisted skull • Ambushing from within the sediment for the rest of its life

waveform.description: One level held, a single transition, and a different level afterwards, because the change happens once and cannot reverse.

entries.closingLine: Because the change happens once and irreversibly, it operates as a phase-change system.

entries.name: Turkey Tail

modes.label: Threading dead wood • Breaking down lignin • Fruiting in zoned brackets

waveform.description: An almost unbroken low line, because a process measured in years has nothing in it that happens.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole process runs at the speed of enzymatic decay, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Two-spotted Cricket

modes.label: Rubbing a file on one wing across a scraper on the other • Producing a pure carrying tone in short pulses • Hearing it through tympanal membranes on the foreleg tibia

waveform.description: Tight groups of identical pulses separated by short gaps, because the song is built from repeated chirps rather than a continuous tone.

entries.closingLine: Since chirps repeat several times a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Umbrella Cockatoo

modes.label: Growing specialised down feathers that never stop growing and never moult • Having their tips disintegrate continuously into a fine keratin powder • Working that powder through the plumage while preening, where it absorbs oil and repels water

waveform.description: A steady even rhythm sustained throughout, because preening is continuous and the powder is produced without interruption.

entries.closingLine: Since preening is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Underwing Moth

modes.label: Adults nearly identical across dozens of species, separable only by fine differences in the hindwing bands • Larvae specialising tightly on particular trees, one group on oaks, another on hickories, another on willows and poplars • Populations diverging along hostplant lines rather than by geography, producing sibling species side by side in the same wood

waveform.description: A varied line with many similar excursions, because the genus repeats the same pattern across many near-identical species.

entries.closingLine: Because the divergence runs across generations, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Vampire Crab

modes.label: Holding a few square metres • Carrying large eggs • Hatching finished crabs

waveform.description: A small quiet rhythm of short movements, because nothing in this animal's life happens more than a few metres from where it started.

entries.closingLine: Because everything is small, local and slow, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Variable Hawk

modes.label: Occupying everything from sea-level desert to high Andean plateau above four thousand metres • Taking whatever prey each of those zones provides rather than specialising anywhere • Varying enormously in plumage between individuals and regions across that whole span

waveform.description: An irregular varying rhythm without a fixed pattern, because the bird works whatever conditions it finds.

entries.closingLine: Because hunting is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Variegated Lizardfish

modes.label: Resting on or partly buried in sand with only the eyes exposed • Launching vertically off the bottom when a fish passes overhead • Holding the prey on inward-curving teeth that cover the jaws, palate and tongue

waveform.description: A long flat line with one sharp spike and a brief settling shoulder, because the fish is motionless, strikes once and then resettles.

entries.closingLine: Because strikes are infrequent, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Variegated Meadowhawk

modes.label: Flight timed to the passage of weather systems rather than to any fixed calendar • The insect moving with the tailwind ahead of a front rather than flying against the air • Hundreds of kilometres covered on wind energy that the dragonfly did not have to generate itself

waveform.description: A pattern of pushes and pauses rather than a steady rate, because the movement depends on when the weather arrives.

entries.closingLine: Because the pushes recur through the season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Velvet Swimming Crab

modes.label: Swimming clear of the bottom with flattened rear legs • Reaching prey and refuges a walking crab cannot • Turning to face anything that approaches

waveform.description: A brisk repeated pattern of strong excursions, because swimming bursts are frequent and each is a definite effort.

entries.closingLine: Since swimming bursts recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Vendace

modes.label: Feeding on zooplankton in cold open water through the year • Moving to shallow gravel in late autumn as the lake cools • Spawning at the coldest time of year so eggs develop slowly over winter

waveform.description: A long even line with one late rise, because almost the whole year is uniform and the event falls at the end of it.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Vervet Monkey

modes.label: Giving a distinct call for leopard, eagle or snake • Producing the matching escape in everyone who hears it • Learning through infancy which call fits what

waveform.description: Long ordinary stretches punctuated by isolated very sharp events, because social life is continuous and alarms are rare and total.

entries.closingLine: Since social exchanges recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Violet Carpenter Bee

modes.label: Landing on the outside of a long tubular flower • Slitting the base of the corolla with the mandibles • Drinking nectar directly without entering or pollinating

waveform.description: A steady busy rhythm of similar visits, because the bee works flower after flower at a consistent pace.

entries.closingLine: Since flower visits recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Walking Catfish

modes.label: Locking the stiff pectoral spines outward as props • Flexing the body from side to side to drive forward across wet ground • Breathing air through a branched organ above the gills the whole time

waveform.description: Ordinary activity interrupted by sustained excursions, because the overland journeys are prolonged events rather than moments.

entries.closingLine: Since journeys recur on wet nights, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Wall Spider

modes.label: A flat star-shaped silk sheet under which the spider waits pressed against a wall • An ant touching the sheet detected instantly and the spider bolting out and running around it • Silk paid out from spinnerets held high while circling, so the ant is bound in a lengthening tether before it can turn

waveform.description: A still waiting rhythm punctuated by extremely fast circling episodes, because the attack is a burst of running.

entries.closingLine: Because the attack takes seconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Walnut Orb-weaver

modes.label: Spending the day pressed into a crevice under bark or in a fence post • Being flat enough to occupy a gap of a few millimetres • Coming out after dark to build and work an orb web nearby

waveform.description: Long hidden stretches alternating with an active period, because the animal is either sealed in a crack or out working the web.

entries.closingLine: Since web activity recurs nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Wandering Glider

modes.label: Climbing to altitude on rising air rather than flying under power • Riding monsoon wind systems across open ocean • Breeding in temporary pools that the same rains create, wherever they appear

waveform.description: A long smooth drifting line with very little structure, because the animal is carried rather than driving itself.

entries.closingLine: Since gliding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Warty Frogfish

modes.label: Motionless • Encrusted • Waiting
Six-millisecond • Total • Suction

waveform.description: Long motionless floor broken by two needle-thin vertical spikes — the strike has no build-up and no follow-through.

entries.closingLine: Because a near-static low-cost baseline is paired with an explosive committed capture, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Wasp Moth

modes.label: Wing scales largely absent so the wings are transparent like a wasp's rather than opaque
A narrow waist, banded yellow and black abdomen and clubbed antennae reproducing hymenopteran proportions
Rapid darting flight, frequent landing and abdomen-curling movements copied from a wasp rather than moth-like fluttering

waveform.description: A jittery irregular rhythm at several overlapping rates, because appearance, proportion and movement each operate on different timescales.

entries.closingLine: Each element runs on its own scale, structural, proportional and behavioural, and the deception fails if any one is missing, so it operates as a multimodal system.

entries.name: Wasp Spider

modes.label: Hanging head-down at the hub • Thick zigzag band through the centre • Waiting on vibration

waveform.description: A long still line with two narrow spikes, because the animal does nothing at all between arrivals and everything in the moment of one.

entries.closingLine: Since the animal is otherwise motionless for hours, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Water Buffalo

modes.label: Grazing coarse stems • Working • Lying in water

waveform.description: A steady working rhythm with one deep flat trough dropped into the middle of it, because the day is built around the hours spent submerged.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is a steady unbroken conversion with a cooling duty built into its daily cycle, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Water Chevrotain
entries.archetype: Down Into the Stream and Along the Bottom

modes.label: Nocturnal • Solitary • Understorey
Submerged • Walking • Vanished

waveform.description: A quiet nocturnal line rising briefly and returning.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a quiet hidden baseline and a brief submerged withdrawal.

entries.name: Water Strider

modes.label: Spreading weight across long legs tipped with water-repellent hair • Denting the surface film without piercing it • Rowing with the middle pair and signalling with ripples

waveform.description: A rapid even series of short strokes, because the animal moves in continual small rowing bursts across the surface.

entries.closingLine: Since strokes recur several times a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Wattled Crane
entries.archetype: Feeding at One Particular Water Depth

modes.label: Wading • Digging • Depth-bound

waveform.description: A slow deliberate wading rhythm with little variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, precise and tied to a narrow physical condition.

entries.name: Western Diamondback Rattlesnake

modes.label: Holding position and rattling at an approaching animal • Adding a segment at each shed • Striking only when the warning has failed

waveform.description: A quiet line breaking into a rapid buzz that escalates before one decisive spike, because the warning builds before anything else happens.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur through the active season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Western Gorilla

modes.label: Eating very large volumes of leaf, pith and stem • Fermenting it slowly in an enlarged hindgut • Moving short distances and resting most of the day

waveform.description: A wide, slow, barely varying curve with no sharp features at all, because the whole system operates at a deliberately low rate.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle turns over slowly, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Western Meadowlark

modes.label: Weaving standing grass into a dome over a scrape • Entering along a concealed side runway • Singing from a post well away from it

waveform.description: A regular alternation of song bouts against a working baseline, because the bird sings in repeated bursts through the day.

entries.closingLine: Since song bouts and feeding trips repeat, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Western Yellow Wagtail

modes.label: Feeding intensively at a stopover site for days or weeks before the desert crossing • Laying down fat until body mass rises by a large fraction, far beyond any normal condition • Flying across the Sahara without landing, the entire journey funded by reserves accumulated beforehand

waveform.description: A build to a peak followed by a sharp decline, because reserves are accumulated over weeks and spent in days.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Whinchat

modes.label: Perching on a tall stem, fence wire or thistle above the sward • Dropping onto insects seen on the ground below • Returning to the same or a nearby vantage

waveform.description: A regular pattern of short identical drops from a returning baseline, because every hunt is the same brief action from a perch.

entries.closingLine: Since hunting drops recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: White Grub

modes.label: Curled underground • Rasping roots • Fermenting it slowly

waveform.description: An almost unvarying low line with the faintest swell in it, because growth at this rate has no events.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at the pace of microbial digestion in the dark, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: White Peacock butterfly

modes.label: Perching low on bare ground • Wings held flat and open • Holding a small patch against rivals

waveform.description: A quick low flutter with short sharp peaks, because the flights are brief sallies from a perch rather than sustained travel.

entries.closingLine: Since those run continuously through the sunlit hours, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: White Seabream

modes.label: Broad chisel-like incisors at the front of the jaw for cropping and scraping • Rows of rounded molars further back for crushing • The two sets used in sequence so a single mouth both detaches and processes hard prey

waveform.description: A steady varied foraging rhythm, because the fish works along the rock taking whatever it finds.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: White Underwing Moth

modes.label: At rest on birch, forewings closed over the body in a pattern of white, grey and black that matches the bark exactly
On being disturbed, the forewings open to expose banded black and white hindwings, the moth flies erratically and lands with the wings closed again

waveform.description: A long flat line broken by a violent burst that stops as abruptly as it began.

entries.closingLine: These are not two settings of one defence but opposite strategies, one built on never being seen and the other on being seen very clearly and then not, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: White-backed Planthopper

modes.label: Developing short useless wings when the crop is young and the density is low • Putting everything into reproduction instead of flight muscle • Building the population where it already is
Developing full wings and flight muscle when density is high or the crop is deteriorating • Leaving the field entirely • Riding weather systems hundreds of kilometres to new crops

waveform.description: Two clearly separated stable levels alternating, because an individual develops into one form or the other with nothing between.

entries.closingLine: This is an adaptive system running two states.

entries.name: White-faced Cockatiel

modes.label: Raising and lowering a mobile crest • Signalling alarm, interest or calm continuously • Reading the same signal in others

waveform.description: Sharp rises returning quickly to a variable baseline, because the crest snaps up with arousal and settles again.

entries.closingLine: Since crest movements occur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: White-headed Fruit Dove

modes.label: A genus of fruit doves distributed across the Pacific with each island group holding its own species • Populations separated by sea crossings too long for a small canopy dove to make routinely • Each isolated group diverging in plumage and voice until it no longer recognises or interbreeds with its neighbours

waveform.description: A steady rhythm drifting apart step by step, because each isolated population moves independently of the others.

entries.closingLine: Because divergence runs across evolutionary time, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: White-rumped Shama

modes.label: A vocal organ at the junction of the two bronchi with independently controlled membranes on each side • Each side capable of producing its own note, with separate muscular control of pitch and timing • Two independent voices sounding together, so a single bird produces intervals and overlapping phrases no single larynx could make

waveform.description: A rapid intricate rhythm with overlapping components, because two independent sources are running at the same time.

entries.closingLine: Because the song runs at high rates, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: White-rumped Vulture

modes.label: Finding a carcass from the air and gathering in numbers • Stripping it within hours • Passing the material through a gut acidic enough to destroy anthrax spores, botulinum toxin and cholera

waveform.description: A long quiet line broken by intense concentrated events, because nothing happens until a carcass appears and then everything does.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: White-tailed Deer

modes.label: Feeding with the tail held down and the white underside hidden • Raising and flaring the tail on detecting a threat • Running with it up, making an unmissable moving signal

waveform.description: A calm feeding line broken by sharp sustained alarm events, because the display is held for the whole of a flight.

entries.closingLine: Since alarm events recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: White-throated Kingfisher

modes.label: Prey below the surface appearing displaced because light bends as it leaves the water • The bird judging the real position rather than the apparent one before committing to a dive • That correction applied from a perch at whatever angle the bird happens to be sitting at, so the offset differs on every attempt

waveform.description: A long still watching line with brief committed dives, because the bird waits motionless and then strikes.

entries.closingLine: Because dives recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Wild Boar

modes.label: Driving a hardened snout disc into soil and levering it upward • Exposing roots, tubers, invertebrates and fungi • Leaving turned ground that changes what grows there next

waveform.description: A persistent pattern of similar strong efforts, because rooting is repeated work at a consistent intensity.

entries.closingLine: Since rooting bouts recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Wild Turkey

modes.label: Scratching leaf litter • Heads up in rotation • Up a tree by dusk

waveform.description: A raised daytime band sitting on a flat floor at both ends, because the animal's operating day has hard edges at dawn and dusk.

entries.closingLine: Because the watching and the feeding proceed together through every daylight hour, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Willow Tit
entries.archetype: Its Own Hole in Soft Wood

modes.label: Finding a standing dead stem soft enough to work • Chipping out a cavity over days and carrying the chips away • Nesting only in a hole it made itself

waveform.description: A quiet line rising into one sustained working period and subsiding, because the excavation is days of concentrated effort once a year.

entries.closingLine: Since excavation happens once a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Willow Warbler

modes.label: Moulting the entire plumage after breeding in Europe • Moulting the entire plumage again on the wintering grounds in Africa • Carrying feathers that are never more than a few months old

waveform.description: A working line interrupted twice by broad sustained excursions, because the year contains two prolonged moults rather than one.

entries.closingLine: Since each moult is a months-long process within an annual cycle, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Winter White Dwarf Hamster

modes.label: A grey-brown summer coat with a dark dorsal stripe, full body mass and normal nightly activity
A white winter coat, reduced body mass, suspended reproduction and daily torpor in which body temperature falls for hours

waveform.description: An active high-amplitude phase giving way to a subdued low one, because the animal changes its whole operating level.

entries.closingLine: The two states are genuinely distinct systems, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Wolf Spider

modes.label: A female attaching the egg sac to her spinnerets and dragging it everywhere she goes • Opening it when the spiderlings are ready and letting them climb onto her abdomen • Carrying dozens of young on her back for days while continuing to hunt

waveform.description: A long flat line with one extended raised period, because the burden of carrying is sustained over weeks.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Woodlouse

modes.label: Overlapping plates on the underside of the female forming a sealed chamber • That chamber filled with fluid in which the eggs and early young develop • The whole aquatic stage carried inside the mother rather than taking place in water

waveform.description: A long flat line with one sustained raised period, because the brood is carried continuously for weeks.

entries.closingLine: Because brooding runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Woodlouse Hunter

modes.label: Enormous forward-projecting fangs carried on jaws that open unusually wide • Striking a woodlouse from above and below simultaneously so the armoured plates are pinned between them • Feeding almost exclusively on a prey type nearly every other spider ignores

waveform.description: A flat nocturnal line with brief decisive strikes, because the spider hunts by encounter rather than by waiting in a web.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters are occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Wreathed Hornbill

modes.label: The female entering a natural tree cavity and sealing the entrance to a narrow slit with mud, droppings and fruit pulp • Remaining sealed inside for months, moulting her flight feathers while incubating and brooding • The male passing every item of food through that slit for the whole period

waveform.description: A long sustained commitment rising and falling slowly, because the whole arrangement runs for months without interruption.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Xantus's Hummingbird

modes.label: Hovering • Circuiting • Expensive
Torpid • Cooled • Overnight

waveform.description: A dense band of maximum-rate activity through daylight that collapses to a deep flat floor at dusk — two states with nothing in between.

entries.closingLine: Because a maximum-rate daytime mode alternates with a genuinely suppressed nocturnal state, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Xantus's Murrelet

modes.label: Nocturnal • Offshore • Continuous

waveform.description: An even nightly rhythm — colony visits and offshore feeding alternate on the same steady cycle rather than building to a peak.

entries.closingLine: Because colony attendance and offshore feeding alternate on a steady nightly rhythm rather than in bursts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow Mongoose

modes.label: Radiating • Solitary • Tethered

waveform.description: An even mid-level rhythm of outward trips returning to the same level.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, repeated outward trips anchored to one fixed point.

entries.name: Yellow Seahorse

modes.label: Gripping a stem • Eyes moving separately • Snapping the head upward

waveform.description: A held line pricked by very narrow spikes at short intervals, because the strike is frequent and the body never moves.

entries.closingLine: Because that rhythm never pauses, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow Tang

modes.label: Grazing filamentous algae across Hawaiian reef all day • Being collected in enormous numbers for the marine aquarium trade • Having that trade halted by litigation rather than by biology

waveform.description: A steady even grazing rhythm with no interruptions, because the fish crops algae continuously through the day.

entries.closingLine: Since grazing is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow-banded Caecilian

modes.label: Burrowing • Chemosensing • Hidden

waveform.description: A slow unvarying rhythm in the low band — continuous small effort with no events at all.

entries.closingLine: Because everything is arranged for slow continuous work in a medium nothing else exploits, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow-banded Millipede

modes.label: Dozens of leg pairs each stepping slightly later than the one in front • The resulting pattern travelling backwards along the body as a continuous visible wave • Many legs always in contact with the ground, producing steady force rather than the alternating push of a few

waveform.description: An extremely regular travelling oscillation, because the same pattern passes down the body continuously.

entries.closingLine: Because the wave repeats many times a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow-billed Shrike

modes.label: Spread across perches • Watching different ground • Feeding each other's young

waveform.description: A steady watching rhythm of regular drops, because the group is always working and no single bird is doing anything dramatic.

entries.closingLine: Because the watching and feeding run together through daylight, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow-crowned Amazon Parrot

modes.label: A vocal organ with two independently controlled sides producing sounds without lips or teeth • Neural circuitry for vocal learning that stays open through adult life rather than closing after a juvenile period • New sounds acquired and added at any age, including those of entirely different species

waveform.description: An irregular varied rhythm that never settles, because the material keeps changing rather than repeating.

entries.closingLine: Because learning and calling are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow-crowned Night Heron

modes.label: Wading slowly • Seizing • Breaking the shell

waveform.description: A deliberate walking rhythm with modest regular dips, the trace of an animal that never hurries and never stops.

entries.closingLine: Because that foraging is sustained and repeated on every workable tide, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow-legged Gull

modes.label: Patrolling seabird colonies rather than foraging at sea • Taking eggs, chicks and adults of smaller species • Robbing food from birds returning to feed their young

waveform.description: A persistent pattern of strong repeated events, because the bird works a colony continuously rather than searching a landscape.

entries.closingLine: Since foraging events recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow-spotted Millipede

modes.label: Coiling into a spiral when disturbed • Releasing a precursor and an enzyme from separate chambers in paired glands along the body • Producing hydrogen cyanide and benzaldehyde at the moment of contact

waveform.description: A long slow line broken by very sharp brief events, because a slow animal's defence is instantaneous when it fires.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellowbelly Damselfish

modes.label: Eggs laid in a sheet on a cleaned surface of coral, rock or gorgonian rather than released into the water • The male remaining with them and fanning continuously with the pectoral fins • Attacking anything that approaches and removing dead eggs until they hatch

waveform.description: A long sustained raised effort that gradually releases, because the guarding runs continuously for days.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle repeats through the season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellowfin Surgeonfish

modes.label: Assembling into large mixed feeding schools over the reef • Entering damselfish territories as a mass rather than as individuals • Grazing the defended algae while the resident cannot expel more than one fish at a time

waveform.description: Repeated grouped surges against a calm baseline, because the fish feed normally until a mass incursion happens.

entries.closingLine: Because incursions recur often, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellowjacket & Hornet

modes.label: A single mated queen founding a nest alone in spring • Workers accumulating through summer until the colony numbers thousands • Every individual working toward a colony that will not survive the winter
New queens leaving in autumn and mating • Overwintering individually in crevices and log piles • The nest, the workers and the old queen all dying

waveform.description: A steep annual build followed by a collapse to a long flat low line, because the colony grows from nothing and ends completely.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two different states, making it a bimodal system.

entries.name: Yellowtail Damselfish

modes.label: Feeding on plankton in the water immediately above a coral head • Staying within a body length or two of the branches at all times • Darting into them at any movement and re-emerging seconds later

waveform.description: A busy feeding rhythm punctuated by very frequent sharp retreats, because the fish is constantly darting back to cover.

entries.closingLine: Since darts recur constantly, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Yeti Crab

modes.label: Waving • Grazing • Continuous

waveform.description: A smooth continuous oscillation — the waving never stops, because the crop stops growing if it does.

entries.closingLine: Because the waving and grazing run continuously, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Zebra Dove

modes.label: Walking on open ground • Barring breaking the outline • Calling from cover

waveform.description: A quiet even walking rhythm with very small variation, because nothing this bird does is abrupt enough to draw attention.

entries.closingLine: Because that routine is continuous through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Zebra Moray Eel

modes.label: Working reef crevices by smell rather than sight • Taking crabs, urchins and molluscs instead of fish • Crushing them between flattened pebble-like teeth rather than holding them with fangs

waveform.description: A slow steady line with occasional modest events, because the animal works crevices methodically rather than striking.

entries.closingLine: Since foraging is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Zoanthid

modes.label: Colonies spreading as connected mats across reef rock and holding the space against other invertebrates • Tissues carrying palytoxin, among the most poisonous non-protein substances known • Neighbouring corals and settling larvae suppressed chemically rather than by any physical contest

waveform.description: A slow steady spread with no cycle, because the colony only advances and never retreats or resets.

entries.closingLine: Because expansion runs over months, it operates as a low-frequency system.
